item.content:encoded:
Love Horoscope Today for Saturday, October 31, 2026: Leo's Love Life Will Be Wonderful, Know the Status of All 12 Zodiac Signs
Love Life Predictions for October 31, 2026: You will try to strengthen personal relationships. You will share happiness with family. Friends and acquaintances will support you.
Aries
Aries individuals will experience increased harmony in their love and family life. They will maintain good rapport with siblings and close ones. Efforts will be made to strengthen personal relationships. Happiness will be shared with family. Support from friends and acquaintances will be available. There may be opportunities to spend time with loved ones.
Taurus
Taurus natives will see emotional bonding grow in their relationships. They will behave well towards all family members. Happiness will prevail at home. The circle of friends may expand. There is a possibility of receiving a desired gift from someone close. Progress will also be made in matters related to love and affection.
Gemini
Gemini individuals will enjoy a joyful atmosphere at home and with family. Coordination with close ones will improve. Positive changes may occur in romantic relationships. They will listen carefully to their partner and express their own feelings. Support from loved ones will be received. Relationships may become sweeter than before.
Cancer
Cancer natives will need to control their emotions. They may hesitate to express their thoughts. Maintain humility and understanding in relationships. Try to increase interaction with close ones. Avoid making decisions influenced by others. Speaking less and responding thoughtfully will be better.
Leo
Leo individuals will experience harmony in their romantic relationships. They will share happiness with friends. Support from their partner will be available. There may be opportunities to go out together. Good news may also be received. Meetings with loved ones will bring joy. Trust in relationships will increase.
Virgo
Virgo natives will have a joyful atmosphere at home. Happiness may come from good news. They will take time for their loved ones and try to fulfil their responsibilities. Sweetness will remain in romantic relationships. There may be chances to spend memorable moments with their partner.
Libra
Libra individuals will see improvement in personal relationships. Positivity will continue in emotional matters. Support from friends and close ones will be available. They will trust their loved ones and move forward together. Signs of improvement in romantic relationships are present. Conversations and mutual understanding will give new strength to relationships.
Scorpio
Scorpio natives will need to maintain ease in their relationships. Keep conversations simple. Share personal matters thoughtfully. Family support will be available. Wait for the right time to express your feelings. Avoid being misled by anyone.
Sagittarius
Sagittarius individuals will experience increased sweetness in their love life. Support from their partner will be received. Mutual trust will strengthen. There may be meetings with a loved one. Friends and family will provide companionship. Emotional relationships will become stronger. Opportunities to spend quality time with loved ones will arise.
Capricorn
Capricorn natives will need to maintain patience in personal matters. Avoid reacting immediately to any issue. Show respect and honour towards everyone. Maintaining clarity in conversations will keep relationships balanced. They will be able to handle family responsibilities better.
Aquarius
Aquarius individuals may get opportunities to go out with family and loved ones. Sweetness and trust in relationships will increase. Important conversations may take place with someone close. Support from friends will be available. They will succeed in strengthening relationships through mutual understanding and advice.
Pisces
Pisces natives will focus on family and personal relationships. They will care for their loved ones’ happiness and spend time with them at home. Trust in relationships will increase. However, avoid stubbornness over small matters or being overly emotional. Your behaviour can affect relationships.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Saturday, October 31: Words Are Literally Spells This Halloween
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 31, 2026. It's Halloween, and you need to be careful with your words, or you might end up with a trick instead of a treat.
Retrograde Mercury in Scorpio squares Mars in Leo on Saturday. This energy is explosive and can create a situation you can't come back from. Secrets and long-buried frustrations are coming to the surface. Though your feelings are valid, be careful with what you say and how you say it. Don't let your anger get the better of you. This holiday is scary enough as it is.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Saturday, October 31, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your desire for change is real, Aries. But you must be careful with how you’re expressing it. You want commitment and to feel like you and your partner are truly doing life together. However, you need to go about it in the right way.
On Saturday, be careful with what you say. Don't try to force your partner into anything, even unconsciously. This includes playing games to get their attention.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be especially cautious on Saturday, Taurus. Pause before saying anything you might regret.
The energy on Halloween is bringing the truth to the surface, but you need to be careful with what you do with it. This is not a good day to make any impulsive decisions, especially those that involve moving in or out with someone you care about.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Take a step back, Gemini. You may be feeling more frustrated than normal on Saturday. This could make you lash out at your partner for something that really isn’t theirs to carry.
As Mercury in Scorpio squares Mars in Leo on October 31, be very careful when trying to elicit a reaction from someone. Something is going on with you, but it is yours to figure out. Take some time alone to do so.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t lose sight of what’s most important, Cancer. Saturday brings up discussions of finances and romantic priorities in your relationship. While you may have to compromise, don't sacrifice what you deserve.
This is always a balance for you to walk, but on October 31 it’s even more crucial. You're feeling fed up with always being the understanding person in your relationship. Make sure you stand up for yourself instead of letting resentment build.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This is not about you, Leo. Start your day by repeating your mantra. You might love the spotlight, but don't make what happens on Saturday about you.
If you want to improve your relationship or save your marriage, you must be careful with what you say and do. This is not the time to minimize what your partner is feeling or the needs they’ve shared. Validate their feelings and watch your words.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This isn’t coming out of nowhere, Virgo. You may feel like something suddenly comes up on Saturday. But if you're really honest with yourself, this isn't all that surprising.
Take time to work through your own feelings about what comes up before starting any conversations. And remember, you don't need to keep being a part of someone else's story if you know you’ve outgrown it.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be honest about what you’re feeling, Libra. Saturday's energy calls you to face something that’s been going on in your relationship or circle of friends.
You’ve felt taken advantage of recently. While this is valid, you also need to acknowledge how you overgive to the point of feeling like you’re not receiving the same back. You don’t have to shoulder the full weight of this, but you do need to own your part.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Stay the course, Scorpio. With Mercury retrograde in your zodiac sign, this is not the time to take any drastic action.
The journey you're on now won't end until November 13, so how you feel may look dramatically different in only a few weeks. Until then, stay the course. On Saturday, journal about what you feel, and try to approach situations and relationships more intentionally. Most importantly, save any life-altering decisions for next month.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t really move ahead if you’re not sure where you want to go, Sagittarius. You want to experience all that you can in every moment of life, but that doesn’t mean you’re always on the right path.
Saturday's energy reveals a new truth that may throw a wrench in your current plan. This changes how you feel and what you want. It may even shift your destiny. Take time to regroup, but make sure you're willing to change your plans.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Not all attention is the same, Capricorn. Be especially careful about trying to get attention in unhealthy ways on Saturday. You may not even be aware that what you’re doing isn’t going to lead to what you hope. So, you must pause and reflect.
Be honest with your needs and embrace your vulnerabilities instead of just trying to get yourself noticed. You also won’t have to work hard to get attention from someone who actually wants to be in your life.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Listen to your heart, Aquarius. Saturday may bring an unexpected detour into your life. Though you are focused on your career, you may suddenly realize that what you’re actually craving is love.
Whether you’re in a relationship or are single, take October 31 as the wake-up call it’s meant to be. You don’t necessarily need to change your life overnight, but you do need to start validating your need for romance and partnership. Don't worry: You can have professional success and love at the same time.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Hold steady, Pisces. On Saturday, you might want to choose a completely new path or relationship. Wait a second. This is not the day to make any impulsive decisions.
A second chance is entering your life on October 31. Rather than jumping on it immediately, hold steady. See where it all goes and how you feel before making any final decisions.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.title: [Cosmopolitan] You Definitely Shouldn’t Ignore These 12 Red Flags in Dating and Relationships
item.dc:creator: Rachel Varina

item.content:encoded:
There's nothing quite like the early stages of dating someone new. The butterflies, the flirting, the staying up way too late texting someone you barely know. Everything's going great until they do something that makes you wonder: Wait, is that a red flag?
Then again, according to the internet, practically everything is a red flag these days. Takes three hours to text back? Red flag. Still friends with an ex? Red flag. Puts ketchup on eggs? Believe it or not, jail.
But there's a difference between someone giving you the ick and someone showing signs that they might not be a particularly healthy partner.
“A red flag is a lighthearted and visual way of referring to behaviors or characteristics of a person or relationship that could become unhealthy or unsafe,” explains Golee Abrishami, PhD, VP of Clinical Care at Octave Mental Health.
So, which dating red flags actually deserve your attention, and which ones are just personal preferences? Ahead, relationship experts break down the warning signs worth watching for, the behaviors that aren't necessarily cause for concern, and what to do when something feels off.
What Are Red Flags in a Relationship?
Simply put, relationship red flags are warning signs that someone's behavior could lead to an unhealthy or potentially unsafe relationship. Think dishonesty, disrespect, manipulation, or controlling behavior, rather than someone occasionally being in a bad mood or forgetting to text you back.
And while the terms red flag and dealbreaker often get used interchangeably, they're not exactly the same thing.
“A dealbreaker is different because dealbreakers are personal,” explains Abrishami. For example, someone not wanting children might be a dealbreaker for you, but that doesn't mean they're doing anything wrong. The same goes for incompatibilities, like having different lifestyles, communication preferences, or long-term goals.
Red flags, on the other hand, tend to point to bigger issues involving respect, honesty, or safety. According to relationship therapist Adrienne Michelle, LMFT, host of The Audacity to Heal podcast, they're often patterns that reveal how someone treats others, including their partner.
Of course, one questionable moment doesn't necessarily mean someone is a walking red flag. As Abrishami emphasizes, red flags are information worth paying attention to, not an automatic verdict on someone's character. What matters is whether concerning behaviors continue and how someone responds when they're addressed.
12 Red Flags in Dating and Relationships You Shouldn't Ignore
Not every red flag announces itself with flashing lights and a giant RUN sign. Some are obvious from the first date, while others don't become apparent until you're months into a relationship. Here are 12 dating and relationship red flags experts say are worth paying attention to:
They Don't Respect Your Boundaries
Someone who treats your boundaries like suggestions rather than actual limits? Yeah, that's a problem. According to Angelika Koch, relationships and breakup expert at Taimi, people who use charm, anger, or guilt to push past your boundaries are showing you they don't respect them. Whether it's pressuring you into sex or refusing to accept a simple no, your boundaries shouldn't be up for negotiation.
They Love Bomb You
Being showered with attention can feel amazing, especially when you really like someone. But declaring their undying love after two dates, buying extravagant gifts immediately, or pushing for commitment before you even know their middle name? That might be love bombing.
Koch warns that excessive affection early on can be a red flag, particularly when someone uses that attention to rush intimacy or push past your boundaries. Of course, being really into someone isn't inherently suspicious. As Abrishami notes, context matters, especially when one person's idea of attentiveness feels overwhelming to the other.
They Make You Feel Like You're Walking on Eggshells
If you're constantly rehearsing conversations in your head because you're worried about how your partner will react, pay attention, says Michelle.
Abrishami adds that feeling increasingly anxious or uncomfortable around someone can be a red flag. Bringing up a problem shouldn't feel like preparing for a hostage negotiation.
They Never Take Accountability
Everyone screws up sometimes. The difference is whether someone can admit it. Abrishami says people who can't apologize without adding a “but,” blame everyone else for their problems, or refuse to acknowledge their role in disagreements may struggle with accountability.
As Michelle puts it, “What matters most is whether someone can reflect after the conflict, repair, and change.”
And if you're always the one expected to fix things afterward, that's not exactly a great sign.
They Try to Control Who You See or What You Do
There's a difference between occasionally feeling jealous and deciding your partner isn't allowed to have friends. Koch warns that jealousy involving your friends or family, accusations about where you've been, and attempts to dictate what you're allowed to do are serious red flags. A partner who demands access to your phone, monitors your whereabouts, or tries to isolate you isn't being protective. They're being controlling.
Their Words and Actions Don't Match
They say they want a relationship but disappear for days. They promise to change but keep doing the same thing. Sound familiar? Michelle identifies a disconnect between someone's words and actions as a potential warning sign. Koch also cautions against partners who start out warm and attentive but become consistently hot and cold. Nobody's perfect, but you shouldn't have to constantly guess which version of someone you're getting.
They Constantly Put You Down (Then Call It a Joke)
A little playful teasing is one thing. Repeatedly making comments that hurt your feelings and then telling you you're “too sensitive” when you speak up? Entirely different situation. Abrishami identifies this as a subtle red flag because it can indicate that your feelings aren't being considered. If the joke is always at your expense, it's probably not that funny.
They Blame All Their Exes
If every single person they've ever dated was supposedly “crazy,” toxic, or entirely responsible for the breakup, it's worth wondering why. Koch specifically flags someone who describes all their exes this way, while Abrishami recommends paying attention to how a potential partner talks about past relationships. Having a difficult ex isn't inherently suspicious. Refusing to acknowledge any personal responsibility across multiple relationships might be.
They Give You the Silent Treatment
Needing a little space to cool down after an argument? Totally reasonable. Refusing to speak to you for hours or days as punishment? Not so much. Michelle warns against partners who use silence to punish you, while Abrishami emphasizes the importance of returning to difficult conversations once emotions settle. Taking a break is healthy when it's communicated respectfully. Withholding affection or communication to make someone suffer isn't.
They Don't Respect Other People
Pay attention to how someone treats people they aren't trying to impress. Abrishami recommends noticing how a date interacts with servers, strangers, and other people they encounter. Michelle also suggests watching how someone treats people who can't do anything for them. Being charming to you while treating everyone else like garbage isn't exactly the glowing character reference they might think it is.
They Make Everything About Themselves
Relationships involve compromise, which becomes pretty difficult when one person thinks their needs are the only ones that matter. Koch identifies consistently prioritizing yourself at someone else's expense as a warning sign. Maybe your plans always revolve around their schedule, or your concerns somehow turn into conversations about their feelings. And somehow, you're always the one compromising.
They Make You Question Your Own Reality
If someone repeatedly denies things they said, insists events didn't happen the way you remember, or makes you doubt your own perceptions, you could be experiencing gaslighting. Michelle points to statements like “that never happened” as potential examples of this manipulation. Occasional disagreements about what happened aren't automatically gaslighting, but deliberately undermining someone's sense of reality is a serious red flag.
What Isn't Necessarily a Red Flag?
Despite what your group chat might have you believe, not every behavior you dislike is a red flag. Sometimes, people just have different preferences, priorities, or communication styles.
For example, Abrishami says taking a while to respond to texts, needing alone time, or having a close relationship with family aren't inherently concerning. And just because someone wants to take things slowly doesn't mean they're hiding something or aren't interested.
The same goes for someone who's upfront about not wanting a serious relationship. “Someone being honest that they aren’t ready for a relationship can feel like a red flag, but I actually love when people know what they want and don’t want and feel good communicating it,” says Michelle.
Of course, that doesn't mean you have to be okay with it. If you're looking for something serious and they're not, you're allowed to call it quits. That doesn't make either of you the bad guy.
The key, according to Abrishami, is considering the context. Is this a one-time thing or something that keeps happening? And if you bring it up, are they willing to have a conversation about it?
Can Someone Have Both Red Flags and Green Flags?
Unfortunately, yes. People are complicated, and someone can be funny, thoughtful, and great in bed while also having some pretty concerning behaviors.
“Green flags don’t cancel out a red flag, especially around safety, respect, or honesty,” says Michelle. In other words, just because someone remembers your coffee order and gets along with your friends doesn't mean you should overlook the fact that they constantly dismiss your feelings.
Koch agrees, emphasizing that it's less about whether someone has positive qualities (most people do!) and more about whether they're willing to recognize and work on their unhealthy behaviors.
And if you're finding yourself making excuses for someone because of all their good qualities, Michelle suggests asking yourself an important question: “Ask yourself whether you’re staying because of who they are now or because of the potential you see in them.”
Because dating someone's potential isn't quite the same as dating the person standing in front of you.
What Should You Do If You Notice Red Flags?
So, you've spotted a red flag. Now what? Before you start mentally drafting your breakup text, consider what actually happened, whether it's part of a larger pattern, and how it's affecting you.
Abrishami recommends identifying the specific behavior that's bothering you rather than immediately labeling someone a walking red flag. If you feel safe doing so, bring it up and pay attention to how they respond.
“You don’t have to say ‘that’s a red flag.’ Saying ‘this makes me hesitant to move forward with you’ is healthy language,” says Michelle.
Do they listen, take accountability, and make an effort to change? Or do they get defensive, dismiss your concerns, and continue doing the same thing? Koch emphasizes that someone's willingness to address unhealthy habits matters more than simply acknowledging they exist. After all, an apology doesn't mean much if the behavior never changes.
It can also help to talk things through with trusted friends or a therapist, especially if you're struggling to see the situation clearly.
And remember, there's a difference between working through ordinary relationship issues and dealing with abuse, coercion, or controlling behavior. If you feel afraid, controlled, or unsafe, prioritize getting support and making a plan to leave safely rather than confronting your partner. Michelle recommends reaching out to someone you trust or contacting the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 for confidential support.
At the end of the day, you don't need anyone else's permission to walk away from a relationship that doesn't feel right.
If you or someone you know doesn’t feel safe in a relationship, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 to speak to a trained counselor.

item.content:encoded:
[Publicidad]

Caridad Bravo Adams escribió “Yo no creo en los hombres” hace 77 años, exponiendo el machismo y la desigualdad que permean en la sociedad, algo que Valentina Buzurro y Adolfo de la Fuente creen, tristemente, sigue vigente, de ahí la actualidad de la telenovela.

Hay evolución, pero la protagonista de la serie que estrena hoy en la plataforma ViX opina que las conductas se mantienen, sólo se les ha puesto nombre, lo que no significa que se hayan erradicado.

“Sigue siendo súper actual el tema, se van transformando las formas en las que decimos ciertos términos pero es lo mismo. Ahora ya le ponemos nombre a ciertas acciones: ghosting, love bombing, pero realmente sigue siendo exactamente lo mismo, seguimos cayendo igual, redonditas todas”, dice la actriz a EL UNIVERSAL.

Su coprotagonista concuerda y considera que el problema está en la educación desde casa, con ejemplos de violencia desde edad temprana, haciendo que los pequeños normalicen estas conductas.

“Uno crece con esas costumbres, las cuales pensamos que están bien, porque nuestros ídolos o nuestra gente mayor, cercana, lo hace, es como lo normal, que si ellos gritan, si ellos pegan, nosotros también, es voltear al lado, a tu alrededor, todos tenemos mujeres cercanas que lo viven, trata a tus mujeres como te gustaría que trataran a las tuyas”, agrega.

Valentina ve que a los hombres les falta mucha humildad para aceptar lo que les hace falta trabajar.

[Publicidad]

“También tenemos una educación muy mala, desde la crianza nos educan con violencia y aprendes que eso está bien; si tu papá y tu mamá te gritan y te pegan, a veces crees que entonces esa es una forma también de amar”.

Tampoco se trata de una lucha de géneros, aclara Buzurru, sino de equilibrar los roles, entendiendo que ellos no son sólo proveedores ni las mujeres amas de casa.

“La sociedad un poco ayuda a estas acciones de los hombres, de repente también las mismas mujeres contribuyen al machismo buscando un hombre proveedor y que entonces no nos falte nada y nos den todo, que llegue el salvador, y los ponesen esta situación de querer aparentar ser el príncipe, y pues no existe ningún príncipe, no nos tiene que salvar nadie”, afirma la actriz.

[Publicidad]

La historia sigue a Julieta (Buzurro), quien se enamora de Arturo, un hombre adinerado que la engaña, dejándola para casarse con otra mujer elegida por su madre, para tiempo después reencontrarse y desencadenar una discusión que termina con la joven en prisión acusada de su asesinato.

Esta es la quinta adaptación versión de la historia, que comenzó como radionovela y novela y de la que se han hecho una película (1955), cuatro telenovelas en 1969, 1991 y 2014, y ahora esta miniserie.

En el drama grabado en locaciones de la CDMX, Burruzu comparte créditos con José Pablo Minor, Marisol del Olmo, Paulina Matos Cecilia Gabriela, Lourdes Munguía, Ruy Senderos, Sachi Tamashiro, Sandra Destenave, Alejandra Zaid, Martín Kuiper e Itza Sodi.

item.content:encoded:
Love may be blind, but is Boston's dating scene hopeless?
With the hit Netflix dating show "Love Is Blind" shining the spotlight on local singles, some are saying goodbye to dating apps and hello to some unconventional ways of finding love.
Even Morrey Eglin, one of the breakout stars of the Boston season of "Love Is Blind" said he'd rather meet someone the old-fashioned way.
“I’m a really social guy. I bounce at Lincoln, I’m in the scene, but it wasn’t working, so that’s why I went on 'Love Is Blind.'"
Eglin didn't leave the pods with a fiancée, so he's still looking.
“You know the Ben Affleck meme where he’s smoking a cigarette, holding a Dunkin'? I felt like that by the end of it. I was pretty emotionally drained.”
Eglin said he's putting dating on hold for now, but he's not interested in swiping his way to a soulmate.
Local
In-depth news coverage of the Greater Boston and New England area.
"I never wanted my love story to start on an app," he said. "I want to bump into somebody in an airport, like, I drop all my papers."
And he's not alone.
Julz Radly is the founder of Stoop Dating, a Boston-based social media dating show where she matches up singles for blind dates.
"If people are willing to go on a date on a stoop on camera, that's how you know dating is so bad nowadays," she said. "I think everyone just wants that human connection that the apps are lacking."
Radly said she's received thousands of applications from people who want to be set up.
“I think the apps have just made people so disposable and it’s easy to write someone off based on appearances, whereas with Stoop Dating, I matchmake you, you don’t know who you’re meeting. It’s just a fun conversation to get to know someone."
Some are taking their search offline entirely. Bored of Dating Apps hosts in-person events designed to bring back the "meet cute," and they're just about to launch in Boston.
"We like it when humans human and chat and flirt with each other. We don't need an algorithm, sometimes all you need is eye contact," Jessica Evans of Bored of Dating Apps said.
The first Bored of Dating Apps event here in Boston is in November, and there are still tickets available.
Stoop Dating also hosts events for people who want to keep their dating lives off camera, and there are plans to expand the dating show to every neighborhood in Boston.

item.content:encoded:
Experts and users reveal how swiping shapes our approach to love and rejection.
- Dating apps increase selectivity, promoting superficial judgments and emotional detachment in relationships.
- Users face challenges balancing standards with vulnerability, impacting mental health and connection quality.
- Some prefer in-person meetings to foster genuine bonds free from the digital judging culture.
Only the sun setting in the early afternoon and the brisk fall weather can bring a familial emotion that cuffing season can only answer. One might add that a few dating sites, a couple of scrolls, and a double tap can manifest a special comfort during these cooler months, but only if that person has the perfect body, porcelain teeth, is career-oriented with over six figures, is well-traveled, and is an avid hobbyist who hopefully embodies their curated aesthetic. If those criteria don’t apply, it’s simple—swipe no. However, why dismiss this individual without a conversation, better yet, why is it so easy?
“There is this sort of framing that psychologists describe as a paradox of choice. It's when we perceive that we have an endless number of options. Then we become more focused, essentially, on finding the best possible choice, and less willing to truly invest and take the time necessary to discern whether a connection actually has potential,” said Dr. Cashuna Huddleston.
She adds, “Small things that we might have overlooked or explored even further if we met the person just organically at the local coffee shop can quickly become reasons for people to swipe left and move on to the next person or just completely ghost you.”
With her work as a licensed psychologist and assistant professor of psychology at Texas Southern University, Huddleston believes dating apps admit a broader view of companionship. She adds that dating apps offer a positive way to explore a new environment and meet people, but believes these platforms make daters critical of potential partners.
“I think these dating apps encourage us to evaluate people on a checklist. Height. He's too short. She’s too tall. Career. He didn't go to college,” she told EBONY. “I think you have to give a little bit more room to meet people and really get to know them.”
Huddleston says swiping to the next becomes easier to negate the emotional labor and vulnerability. She claims the real work happens outside the app for a promising bond. The educator advises those in larger cities not to be discouraged, to use discernment, and to give potential romance a fair chance.
Cameron Hope became a Tinder user when he enrolled in college. Almost ten years later, the 26-year-old explains he occasionally uses the apps but prefers to meet his potential beaus in person since he believes online dating is for “accessibility purposes.” Hope admits the swiping left or right technique made him picky—a concept that accompanies the territory of online dating. Hope believes it's challenging for individuals to connect with reality and with those in proximity. As he navigates connections as a Black gay man, he recognizes the parallels of being the rejector and rejected—part of which could feel isolating.
“Sometimes it can be something as simple as them saying no, or they could ghost you or block you,” he told Ebony. “Sometimes it sucks, but you know you learn to take it to the chin and keep pushing. No shade.”
Though he says the apps can have a hypersexual connotation, he doesn't shy away from expressing his needs despite the current state of online dating. If necessary, Hope allows himself a mental health check-in and gives himself time to adjust.
He reiterates that those who have standards should maintain a balance that doesn’t go against one’s judgment, but should question which values are worth negotiating, especially where potential partners are deemed disposable. To him, his standards are aligned mentally, physically, emotionally, and spiritually. Despite his journey, Hope remains lighthearted and persistent with his dating experiences.
Trenton M. Alford prefers online dating since in-person interactions require him to “spit game” and “put effort”. From Alford’s perspective, he recognizes that women exude a blasé attitude when men try to converse with them in social settings—causing a rift between one’s true intentions and expectations. Though Alford appreciates a challenge when pursuing women, he says on the apps that charisma sells itself.
“If I'm in a room with 15 other people, I may not be the one who's dressed the flyest or looks the best. Now I'm competing, especially if the young lady's attractive—with all these other men who are similarly interested in her,” he told EBONY. “[With online dating] I can be like, ‘Hi, my name's Trenton. I have two degrees,’ which I do. The minute sells itself because nine times out of 10, the majority of men on Hinge or Tinder might not have two degrees, or much ambition or charisma via conversation than what I'm going to have,” he says.
Delving into his version of masculinity, dating apps became a playground for his personal pleasure. Early in his dating life, he sometimes sought physical connection, using charm to gain access. Now, at 34, he recognized that behavior was toxic and used the analogy of a club closing to dating—at his age, it’s late, and it’s time to get serious about dating.
“It's more about being honest, upfront, intentional, and not selling the dream, but selling the truth and letting the truth be what they're interested in, not letting them be interested in what could be,” he said.
As a reformed online dater, he acknowledges that apps disturb one’s psyche. Recently, Alford broke off most of his connections, which, to his surprise, was well received. After receiving a kidney transplant, it was a sensitive time when he had to share his diagnosis with women while being unemployed and healing from surgery, hoping their connection would remain fruitful.
“If you're willing to wait a little bit for me to heal, and if you're willing to wait a little bit for me to get a job, we can definitely make this shake. If you're willing to wait, I'm willing to give you the world," he told EBONY. “A lot of women were like, 'Okay, I'm willing to see where this goes because you're nice, you're sweet, you're interesting.’ The more I learned to be vulnerable, the more drastic changes I started seeing in Hinge.”
Lifestyle content creator, podcaster, Masionoo, is somewhat a stranger to online dating—with very few times using Instagram as a buffer to genuinely connect with women and using their shared adoration to potentially meet offline. To him, traditional apps seem systemic, and he says they take the genuine nature out of how love and relationships are supposed to exist. The 26-year-old believes online dating becomes a digitized cycle in which romance is caught in its abyss.
“It's an online thing. This is where you met this person. This person is watching and judging your every move, and it becomes so internet to the point where it never gets off the internet and never becomes a dynamic where you can eliminate the internet from [your] dynamic,” he told EBONY. “If you are gonna meet somebody on the internet, your job, if you're actually trying to take somebody serious off of the internet, is to eliminate the internet, because all it's gonna do is bring unnecessary turmoil to something that could be genuine, beautiful, and worthwhile.”

item.title: [VICE] A Dating App Just Launched 'Chivalry Mode' for People Tired of Modern Dating
item.dc:creator: Ashley Fike
item.description: Want a guy who opens the car door and has a five-year plan for the wedding? There’s an app setting for that now. item.content:encoded:
Want a guy who opens the car door and has a five-year plan for the wedding? There’s an app setting for that now.
Match Group recently relaunched Upward, a Christian dating app that’s now welcoming anyone looking for marriage and a little old-fashioned romance. Its new Chivalry Mode encourages men to message first, leaving women to reply or unmatch. There’s also Marriage Timeline, where users can share how soon they’d like to get married and find people with similar plans. So you can discuss wedding expectations before you’ve even gone on a first date.
Videos by VICE
Dating apps have changed their minds about who should make the first move. Bumble originally required women to message first when it launched in 2014, but eased that rule in 2024 after its CEO said some women found the expectation exhausting. Upward is now encouraging men to initiate conversations, with a special setting for people who prefer it that way.
Match Group is also betting that Gen Z is ready to get married.
‘Chivalry Mode’ Is the Latest Dating App Feature, and It’s Turning Modern Dating Upside Down
According to Match Group’s 2026 Singles in America research, 72% of Gen Z respondents want to get married. Upward has embraced the idea with an Americana-inspired advertising campaign called “Wanted for Life,” featuring lines like “Known to change a tire, not his feelings for you.” Someone actually got paid to write that.
Daniel Cox, director of the Survey Center on American Life, told WIRED that Gen Z’s age could help explain the high percentage. Younger adults are less likely to have married already, so their answers aren’t necessarily evidence of some renewed enthusiasm for traditional marriage. Cox also believes the interest in old-fashioned courtship comes from frustration with modern dating and its lack of established expectations. “People are wanting something over nothing,” he said.
And marriage hasn’t exactly been climbing everyone’s priority list. In a 2023 Pew Research survey, just 23% of American adults said being married was extremely or very important to having a fulfilling life. Close friendships came in at 61%. The percentage of high school seniors who expected to get married someday also fell from 80% in 1993 to 67% in 2023.
As for the people actually using Upward, the experience hasn’t been great for everyone.
Tauti, a California social work student, lasted less than 48 hours before getting fed up with the conservative men she encountered. “I did not know me being Christian and leaning liberal was a big ask,” she said on TikTok. Other users have criticized the decision to welcome non-Christian singles, arguing that the app is abandoning its original purpose.
There’s nothing wrong with wanting marriage or preferring traditional courtship. But an app offering a marriage timeline still doesn’t mean the person on the other end of the conversation is someone you’d want to marry.

item.title: [KOAM News Now] Alex Pretti’s family says feds are still stonewalling efforts for justice
item.dc:creator: Meridith Edwards; Whitney Wild; CNN
item.description: (CNN) — The parents of Alex Pretti, a US citizen shot and killed by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, are accusing the Department of Justice of violating their rights under a federal victims’ rights law, as they demand transparency and justice in their son’s death. In a July letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche — obtained exclusively by CNN — an attorney representing Michael and Susan Pretti wrote they have not received any substantive updates from the DOJ regarding an investigati
item.content:encoded:
(CNN) — The parents of Alex Pretti, a US citizen shot and killed by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, are accusing the Department of Justice of violating their rights under a federal victims’ rights law, as they demand transparency and justice in their son’s death.
In a July letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche — obtained exclusively by CNN — an attorney representing Michael and Susan Pretti wrote they have not received any substantive updates from the DOJ regarding an investigation into their son’s death, and called the department’s attitude toward the case “cruel.”
“The government’s pattern of conduct is not only unconscionable, but unlawful,” the letter states.
Pretti’s parents on Tuesday accused the federal government of “shielding Alex’s killers” by not turning over the entire federal case file to state investigators.
“We will no longer stay silent about the actions of the Department of Justice in the 275 days since Alex’s murder,” Pretti’s father, Michael, said in the family’s first news conference since the 37-year-old ICU nurse’s death.
The Pretti family met with US Attorney for the District of Minnesota Dan Rosen on July 13, the letter explains, the same day Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced in a news conference federal officials had handed over volumes of evidence from Pretti’s shooting.
However, the letter goes on to say that, despite a public acknowledgment from local officials of an evidence-sharing agreement, Rosen refused to provide any information and would not even confirm the arrangement.
“It is impossible to convey how the government’s refusal to engage in transparent communication with the Pretti family has compounded their heartbreak,” the missive says.
“Further, with each such refusal, U.S. Attorney Rosen even refused to explain the basis for his position, instead stating only that ‘I can’t tell you for all kinds of reasons,’ without providing a single one,” according to the letter.
Federal investigators who briefly agreed to share their evidence with state law enforcement have since stopped cooperating, said Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, who is leading a lawsuit against the Department of Justice.
“We are in litigation with the federal government right now to secure the rest of the remaining file, which they could give us this morning if they were inclined to do so, but it looks like we’re going to need a court order. I’m sorry that it comes to that,” Ellison told CNN’s Sara Sidner Tuesday morning. “Any prosecutor can tell you, you can’t go forward with half a file. You need the whole thing.”
CNN has reached out to the DOJ and the US Attorney for Minnesota.
In its response to Minnesota’s lawsuit, the Department of Justice said it is not required to turn over evidence to a state agency before an active court case is underway.
The Pretti family’s attorney, Steve Schleicher, says they have heard nothing from the DOJ since sending their letter.
“I’ve never seen a family treated with such cruelty and disrespect,” he said.
Pretti’s death was captured in its entirety on video. Like some other incidents that occurred as a result of the Trump administration’s ongoing immigration crackdown, the footage from Pretti’s shooting differed from the version of events provided by the Department of Homeland Security.
Kristi Noem, then-DHS secretary, initially described Pretti as a “terrorist” who “attacked” officers after “brandishing” a weapon, though the video disputed those claims. White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller referred to Pretti as an “assassin” who tried to murder federal agents.
“No one from the federal government called us on that horrible day, but they did go on TV to tell lies about Alex,” Michael Pretti said Tuesday.
Video footage shows, minutes before the fatal encounter with Pretti, immigration agents patrolling a Minneapolis street and interacting with bystanders. A witness, Nilson Barahona, told CNN agents were trying to apprehend someone who fled into a donut shop that locked its doors, leaving the group of federal officers on the sidewalk and street. Agents detained one observer as others blew whistles, yelled and recorded video on their phones.
Video shows Pretti attempting to intervene in a scuffle between an observer and the agents.
During the incident, Pretti was pepper-sprayed in the face. One of the officers can be heard in the footage shouting: “Gun! Gun! Gun!” as Pretti is on his knees and bent forward. An agent removed Pretti’s gun from his waistband and can be seen exiting the skirmish. At about the same time, one agent drew his service weapon.
About a second after the agent holding Pretti’s weapon moved away, the officer who drew his own weapon appeared to fire several shots at Pretti before another agent drew his weapon and a shot rang out. The other officer then raised his gun and fired more shots. At least 10 gunshots can be heard on the video.
The DHS report on its initial investigation into Pretti’s death says an officer yelled, “He’s got a gun” multiple times before the officers fired.
“It’s difficult to get up every day, to function, to be a parent, knowing that your child’s never coming home,” Susan Pretti told CNN’s Jake Tapper after Tuesday’s news conference. “No parent should have to live what we’re living. No daughter should have to wake up and know that her only sibling is no longer here.”
“What the federal government has taken away from us, from his friends, his family, his colleagues, from his patients, from the patients’ families. They’ve taken away all of that — and it’s reprehensible,” he told Tapper.
Susan Pretti said she knew Alex as her son, but the outpouring of support they’ve received from his friends and coworkers has helped her see another side of him.
“Every letter and card that we received from his colleagues, telling us who he was, at work … not only helping his patients but his colleagues,” Susan Pretti said, choking up. “You know what that’s like for a parent to hear? It is probably the kindest thing a parent can ever hear about their child.”
Michael Pretti said his trust in the government is fading.
Pretti’s death followed the fatal shooting of Renee Good on January 7 and the non-fatal shooting of Julio Sosa-Celis on January 14 by immigration agents during Operation Metro Surge. Those incidents prompted significant protests in Minneapolis and across the country for weeks.
Hennepin County prosecutors have fought the DOJ for key evidence in Pretti’s death for months, after federal law enforcement repeatedly threw up blockades to their access.
On the day Pretti was killed, the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension attempted to access the scene to launch an investigation but was banned by federal authorities. CNN was on scene the next day when the BCA first accessed the scene on a court order from a state judge.
State and local investigators sued the Trump administration in federal court to obtain evidence in Pretti’s killing. After an evidence-sharing agreement between the DOJ and Minnesota investigators was finalized in June, Hennepin County prosecutors received volumes of evidence in Pretti’s shooting.
Weeks later, the DOJ abruptly changed course and stopped sharing information, leaving Hennepin County prosecutors unable to access crucial evidence such as the weapons used to shoot Pretti and the firearm Pretti was carrying in his waistband at the time of the altercation, according to court records filed October 13.
The letter from Pretti’s parents asks the DOJ to identify the federal employees who shot and killed Pretti, commit to sharing information with state and local investigators, confirm whether the FBI is continuing to investigate Pretti’s murder, and return any items of Pretti’s personal property no longer needed for evidentiary purposes.
“No family should have to beg the U.S. government to do its job,” the letter says. “And no government should act with such caprice.”
The Pretti family’s attorney declined to say Tuesday whether they would file a suit of their own against the Department of Justice.
“The family will avail itself to any and all remedies in its pursuit of justice for Alex,” Schleicher said.
Until they find justice, the family is comforted by shared memories of their son. Michael Pretti recalled a specific camping trip when Alex was about 6 years old. Just as they were wrapping up the weekend and preparing to leave, Alex rode his new bike off a small bridge and into a creek.
“He comes back and he’s soaked,” Michael Pretti said with a grin, prompting a chuckle from his wife. “That was a good memory, that was a good weekend that stands out,” he said, adding “that’s probably where his love for hiking and biking started.”
CNN’s Andy Rose and Cindy Von Quednow contributed to this report.

item.title: [Queerty] Science says gay guys are better off swiping across multiple dating apps - Queerty
item.dc:creator: David Hudson
item.description: A new study from Australia concludes that gay men might benefit from using more than one type of dating app. The results appear in Psychology & Sexuality. “There are several fundamental differences between gay and mainstream dating apps that may significantly impact user experience, including the interface, image-sharing, and potential for non-consensual messaging,” says lead author Zac Bowman, a PhD candidate at Flinders University’s College of Human Sciences and Culture. For example, on Grindr
item.content:encoded:
A new study from Australia concludes that gay men might benefit from using more than one type of dating app. The results appear in Psychology & Sexuality.
“There are several fundamental differences between gay and mainstream dating apps that may significantly impact user experience, including the interface, image-sharing, and potential for non-consensual messaging,” says lead author Zac Bowman, a PhD candidate at Flinders University’s College of Human Sciences and Culture.
For example, on Grindr, you’re confronted with a wall of profiles that often feature plenty of flesh on display. You can exchange messages with anyone and may receive unsolicited, spicy photos. Previous studies have found that body objectification is rife on gay dating apps.
How about we take this to the next level?
Subscribe to our newsletter for a refreshing cocktail (or mocktail) of LGBTQ+ entertainment and pop culture, served up with a side of eye-candy.
By contrast, on Tinder and Hinge, you see users one at a time and swipe to indicate your interest. Messaging takes place only when users match.
The authors note that “Gay dating apps are used by an array of sexualities, including bisexual men, sexually curious men, or straight men looking for friendships”.
For this reason, their study sought the opinions of men from across the spectrum. They recruited participants via social media and Grindr adverts. In total, just under 580 men took part.
The researchers quizzed them on their app use and about their wellbeing. This included questions about body dissatisfaction, depression, anxiety, stress, and self-esteem.
What did the study find?
One of the study’s main findings was that queer users of both types of dating apps “reported significantly lower depression, anxiety, and stress scores than men who had used either mainstream or gay dating apps exclusively.”
By contrast, men who identified as straight reported more anxiety if they used both gay and mainstream dating apps. The authors speculate that the “straight” men who use gay dating apps might actually be struggling with their own sexuality, or fearful of judgement. Hence their greater anxiety.
“In contrast, for sexual minority men, participants who reported using both types of dating apps had significantly lower anxious symptomology than sexual minority men who used either mainstream or gay dating apps exclusively,” they say. “This result is surprising, as it not only opposes most previous literature reporting negative associations between dating app use and mental health, but also directly contradicts the relationship between using both app types and anxiety seen in straight men within this study.”
Why a diverse range of apps lessens anxiety in gay men
Why might using more than one type of dating app be better for your mental health? The authors suggest it might foster a feeling of having different irons in different fires, or maximising the chances of success, whether that’s seeking a hookup on a gay dating app or romance via a more mainstream app.
They say queer men “may have a wide range of motivations to access dating apps (e.g. love, sex, sexual identity exploration), and the use of multiple types of dating apps may increase the likelihood of achieving these goals.
“Perceived dating app success (i.e. achieving desired outcomes) has shown significant correlation with increased psychological wellbeing, and may therefore be a reason for the lower mental health concerns in sexual minority men who used both gay and mainstream dating apps.”
In short, the impact of dating apps on mental health isn’t one-size-fits-all — it depends on both the type of app and your orientation. Using a mix of platforms seemed helpful for gay guys but more complicated for straight men.
Sign up for the Queerty newsletter to stay on top of the hottest stories in LGBTQ+ entertainment, politics, and culture.

In a Relationship: Express your thoughts clearly, especially if you have been holding back an opinion to avoid disagreement. Honest discussion can help you understand each other better.
