item.content:encoded:
Love Horoscope Today, October 25, 2026
The love horoscope for October 25, 2026, brings a mix of romance, emotional clarity, and challenges across zodiac signs, encouraging open communication and heartfelt conversations.
Love Horoscope Today, October 25, 2026: Today brings a romance, emotional clarity, and some challenges for all signs. Gemini, Taurus, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn, and Aquarius are likely to see positive growth, deeper relationships, and opportunities for romantic involvement or commitment.
Aries, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Pisces may face emotional fluctuations, confusion, or instability, but open communication and emotional understanding can ease tensions. Cancers should be especially cautious, as unresolved issues can cause emotional tensions.
Overall, the day encourages heartfelt conversations and thoughtful actions in love and relationships.
Aries Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, the love situation for Aries is better than average. In terms of love, you have to proceed with caution today. Some challenges may come in your love life. Your partner may quarrel with you. So control your anger and speech. Today will be a very romantic day for lovers. Today you will get time to express your love feelings in front of your partner. Today will be a very auspicious day for you in terms of love and relationships.
Taurus Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, Taurus people can get a chance to spend loving time. You will feel that love has flowed in your life, and you have a chance to spend more time with your partner. You can get a special opportunity to create a romantic atmosphere with your partner. You can get a chance to go on a short trip or a movie date with your partner.
Gemini Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today is going to be a very auspicious and pleasant day for Gemini people. The ongoing dispute between you and your spouse will be resolved today, and happiness will increase between you two. Today, you will be able to express your feelings well and explain your feelings to your partner. People around you love you very much, and you should spend time with them.
Cancer Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today will be a very worrying day for Cancer people. The ongoing dispute with your spouse will be very painful for you. You will feel that you are not able to express your feelings properly. For a good relationship with your partner, you should listen to your heart. You need to be emotional to keep your relationships stable. Today you will get time to share your feelings with your partner.
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that the love situation can be a little worrying for Leo people. You may feel that something is going wrong in your life or that there is some confusion in your relationship. But you have to keep in mind that these small things in your life scare you the most. Your relationship with your spouse will be deeper than before, and you will be able to understand each other’s feelings better.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that your relationship with your partner will be stronger, and the distance between you will be less. You have to focus on the problems between you and work together to solve them. Today is a good time for those who want to get married. Today’s horoscope will prove to be very auspicious for you, and you will get success in expressing your love.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope shows that your love life will be good today. You will enjoy a happy and stable relationship with your spouse. Today, some auspicious work may start in your life, or you may get a chance to start a new chapter with your spouse.
Scorpio Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that your love horoscope may be a little worrying for you today. You may have many feelings in your mind, which may make you unstable. Today, it is very important for you to spend time with your partner, which will make your relationship even stronger. You should act wisely and firmly in your relationship so that you are happy with your partner. You should be a little more sensible about your relationship and show more trust in your relationship.
Sagittarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, you may get a proposal due to which you may be confused about what to do. Before this, you should listen to your heart and do what seems right. One should not rush into any relationship. One should move forward slowly and wisely. There is hope of happiness and joy in your relationships. You should try to strengthen your relationship with your spouse.
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s love horoscope is very good for Capricorn people. Today, your love will be better for you. You will have to support your partner in every work, and you will not have any difficulty in getting the support of your spouse. Your spouse will leave no stone unturned to bring happiness to your love life. Today you may get a chance to enjoy a romantic evening with your partner.
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today your love life will be normal. A new relationship can be formed with your partner in your life, which will be full of experiences for you. Goodness and affection will increase in your relationship, and you will start a new chapter with your spouse. You will understand the feelings of both and will be successful in sharing your love.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope can be partially worrying for you. There may also be some instability in your love life. You have to maintain communication with your partner and sort out the agreements between you. This is an auspicious time for your marriage, and there is a possibility of a new beginning in your life.
Quick Answers
For Gemini, October 25, 2026, is described as a very auspicious and pleasant day. Any ongoing disputes with a spouse will be resolved, and you will be able to clearly express your feelings and spend quality time with loved ones.

item.title: [niagarafallsreporter.com] Was Brandon Newport Framed by Dr. Yvonne Pierpont? Part 2
item.dc:creator: Frank Parlato
item.description: Was Brandon Newport Framed by Dr. Yvonne Pierpont? Part 2 Part 2 examines the locked folder only she saw, the life coach who secretly recorded him, and the forensic questions police never pursued. Part 1 laid out the case: Dr. Yvonne Pierpont’s accusation that her husband, Delta pilot Brandon Newport, drugged and sexually assaulted her; his denial; a “confession” he says she coached, after telling him to confess or she would divorce him; lab results that settle nothing; and a police investigatio
item.content:encoded:
Was Brandon Newport Framed by Dr. Yvonne Pierpont? Part 2
Part 2 examines the locked folder only she saw, the life coach who secretly recorded him, and the forensic questions police never pursued.
Part 1 laid out the case: Dr. Yvonne Pierpont’s accusation that her husband, Delta pilot Brandon Newport, drugged and sexually assaulted her; his denial; a “confession” he says she coached, after telling him to confess or she would divorce him; lab results that settle nothing; and a police investigation that tested his story but not hers.
Since May 19, 2026, Newport has been in the Pinellas County Jail, awaiting trial.
More charges followed. One for violating an injunction. Six for possessing child pornography. He denies them all.
Part 3 will examine those charges.
In jail, Newport says, a scan showed that the cancer he had spent two years fighting had returned. He has chondrosarcoma, a bone cancer in the pelvis. Newport says his Mayo Clinic oncologist warned that without surgery, he could die within a year.
He cannot get to the surgeons at Mayo from a jail cell.
A PILOT, A VETERAN, A PRISONER
Newport is 41. He says he joined the Army in 2005 and served in Kuwait, Iraq, and Afghanistan. He came home a veteran, rated 100 percent disabled from his service.
He went to Texas A&M, taught flying at the Florida Institute of Technology, and became a Delta pilot.
He was also a Federal Flight Deck Officer, trained and deputized by Homeland Security to carry a gun in the cockpit.
Then cancer grounded him. He fought it for two years. Newport says his doctors did not expect him to fly again. On April 22, 2026, he flew for Delta again.
He had been back at work for four weeks. Then, a few houses from home, St. Petersburg police stopped his pickup truck and arrested him for sexual battery.
Much of the following account comes from his wife's statements to St. Petersburg police detective Dagni Closser in March 2026.
2023: SHE TELLS HIM TO MOVE OUT
Pierpont told Closser that during a Thanksgiving 2023 camping trip, she awoke to Newport "sodomizing" her. She said she ordered him to leave their home. He moved into a rental house that November.
Two months later, in January 2024, doctors found aggressive cancer in his pelvis.
Pierpont was a Mayo Clinic surgeon. She told police she found him "help with the right doctors." He spent two years relearning to walk.
THE LOCKED FOLDER
In February 2025, acting on what she called a “gut feeling,” Pierpont examined Newport’s iPad without asking him.
The folder was locked. She knew his passcode. She opened it.
Pierpont told police the folder contained videos showing her and another woman, both apparently unconscious, being sexually abused. She also described photographs of fully clothed young girls in public places.
She told police she sent the videos and photos to herself.
She texted him photos of clothed girls in public places, which is not a crime. He denied wrongdoing. She did not send him the video she says showed him abusing her while she was unconscious, which would be one. By her account, she never confronted him about that video at all.
Shame or shock might explain it. But it means the most serious thing she says she found is the one thing no one else has ever seen.
Pierpont said he caught her looking through the iPad. They argued.
The police report says that Newport then took her laptop and “presumably deletes everything she had saved in the cloud.”
“Presumably.” No one says they saw him delete anything.
The photos survived because she had texted them to him. She says the videos were lost.
Yet she says she had sent the videos to herself. Files sent that way usually leave copies: on the phone that receives them, on the servers in between, and in a deleted-items folder for 30 days.
Police seized 11 of Newport’s devices in May. The available file identifies no recovered video depicting Pierpont or the other woman.
The file shows no forensic examination of the iPad for the folder Pierpont described. It shows no request for her Apple records. Either could show whether the folder existed, and whether anything was deleted.
Newport says there was no folder. "She just completely made it up," he said.
No one but Pierpont says they saw the videos of her or the other woman.
HER BROTHER'S PLAN
Pierpont did not initially go to the police. She went to her brother, Brandon Pierpont, who warned her that divorce would likely give Newport partial custody of the boys.
The advice, as Closser later documented it, was explicit: "It was recommended that she will allow Brandon to think they are getting back together and therefore she can control Brandon's interactions with the children."
She told Newport she needed a year to "reflect." There were rules. He could not live in the house. He had to leave by 9:30 p.m. No electronics at home or at the boys' games.
THE COACH WHO RECORDED HIM
Around then, Newport began working with Sarah Eva Michielson, a life coach who describes herself as an "attachment theory coach."
But Pierpont met Michielson first, in a therapy group. Michielson told police she offered to help Newport.
In one Zoom session, according to the detective, Newport asked whether HIPAA protected what he said. Michielson told him, "Sure." She was secretly recording him.
What he told Michielson, she told his wife.
She called herself his coach. In reality, she was his wife's spy.
At her first meeting with Detective Closser on March 3, Pierpont repeated what Michielson had told her: Newport had been "kicked out of the dark web." Eight days later, Closser interviewed Michielson.
Michielson told the detective that Newport admitted to masturbating to a video of a 12-year-old girl, fully clothed, ice skating.
Closser listened to Michielson's recording. She wrote: "I heard him specifically say he had not masturbated to her."
Closser's word for Michielson's statements was "inconsistent."
Police did not ask why the coach told them something her own tape contradicted. They kept building the case.
Newport says he paid Michielson for the sessions, and that she presented herself as a therapist. She told police she is not a licensed therapist. On her own recording, when Newport asked whether their talks were protected under HIPAA, she told him, “Sure.”
In Florida, where Newport was, practicing therapy without a license is a felony. Whether coaching him over Zoom from Wisconsin crosses that line is a question no one has yet asked.
PIERPONT SAID SHE FEARED NEWPORT
Pierpont told police she felt unsafe and believed he should not be alone with their sons.
By her account, she had watched a video of her husband abusing her. She did not seek a divorce. She did not go to the police.
The family's routine continued. Newport came to the house each night to put the boys to bed. He says that while Pierpont worked in Wisconsin, he cared for them alone for two weeks of every month.
Newport says the arrangement continued for more than three years, both before and after she says she found the folder. Several friends have confirmed it.
She also told Closser that in May 2025 she woke with her shirt pulled up and Newport "looming over" her.
She still did not go to the police.
Newport said he was looking for his cancer medication, which she kept at the house. He said he had told her he was coming over. "It is a complete falsehood," he said.
A private hair test later found Ambien from about that time. Newport says Ambien prescribed in his name was meant for her, and that she took it. Police found a prescription bottle in the house filled on May 7, 2025, the same month.
DECEMBER 23
Newport cooked dinner on December 23, 2025.
By her own account, she already believed he had drugged her and abused her in her sleep. She ate the dinner he cooked anyway.
At bedtime, Pierpont felt "overwhelmingly tired." She said she believed he had drugged her food.
Her son was asleep beside her. Pierpont did not call 911 or leave the room. She did not wake anyone or move the child. She turned on her phone's recorder, placed it face down on the nightstand, and went to sleep.
She says the recording captured sounds of masturbation. Newport says it is her snoring.
Pierpont told police Newport admitted the following day that he had raised her shirt, masturbated beside her, and "finished on" their son's comforter.
That evening, some 22 hours after the dinner, on December 24, Pierpont underwent a sexual assault examination at the Suncoast Center in St. Petersburg. Pierpont did not make a police report. Her examination kit went to a state laboratory in Tallahassee and sat untested.
TEN WEEKS
For the next 10 weeks, Pierpont gathered evidence instead of going to police. She did three things. First, she secretly recorded him at a restaurant.
She told police that on the recording, Newport admitted giving her melatonin, not Ambien. Melatonin is an over-the-counter sleep aid. She told police he denied having sex with her, but said he would have if she had been in a better position.
The police file does not show that the detective ever heard that recording.
Second, she had her hair tested. Pierpont's brother arranged a private hair analysis. It reported no Ambien corresponding to December, the month of the alleged assault.
Third, she weighed a deal. A civil lawyer suggested a possible agreement over the children. Closser wrote that they "could offer to leave out all of the criminal activity he has been doing if he agrees to all of her parameters with the kids."
The file does not show whether that proposal became an offer. Newport said she never made such an offer.
Pierpont gave police two explanations for delaying reporting him.
She told them she was afraid that reporting would lead to "Brandon getting access to their children," and her brother had told her the laboratory would not test her examination kit without a police report.
Her second explanation does not match Florida law. A victim can request testing of her kit without a police report. Pierpont did not ask.
Neither does her first, if Newport is telling the truth: He says she kept leaving the boys alone with him in Florida two weeks a month, right up to his arrest, while she worked at the Mayo Clinic in Wisconsin.
He says he also made meals three times a day until the day of his arrest.
MARCH 2026: SHE GOES TO POLICE
On March 2, 2026, Pierpont went to the police. She said she had recordings and other evidence that Newport had been drugging her.
Pierpont told Closser she planned a “disclosure” session with Newport. Police had been told it was one “in which he is supposed to talk about his deviances and what he had been doing, criminally, to her.”
She proposed having the life coach, Michielson, listen.
Closser advised against involving a third party. Instead, she proposed a controlled call in which Pierpont would speak with Newport while the detective secretly recorded the conversation.
Pierpont did not want the controlled call, which would have given police their own recording.
Closser decided Pierpont could record Newport herself. That left Pierpont in control of the recording and what the police received. The detective was not there. Pierpont secretly recorded a five-hour session with Newport.
She gave a recording to police. Newport says it was an edited copy, not the original.
Pierpont never gave the detectives the original recording. A third party edited the recording and made changes to the recording, highlighting the "relevant parts of the recording," and then uploaded it to evidence.com.
WHAT HE THOUGHT IT WAS
Newport thought the “disclosure” session would help save his marriage.
The word comes from marriage counseling after infidelity: one spouse tells the other everything he has done, often with a therapist present, so the couple can start over on the truth. Newport says that is what he was told this was. He says a therapist was supposed to be there. She was not.
He says Pierpont set the terms. He was to admit every wrong he had done in the marriage. If he refused, she would file for divorce at once. He says he believed that if he got through it, they would have a chance to begin again.
He did not know she had gone to the police. He did not know a detective had told her she could record him. He did not know he was being recorded.
He says she told him beforehand what she needed to hear. “I need you to say that you put stuff in my chicken,” he says she told him.
THE CONFESSION AND THE LAB
The State's case rests heavily on that recording. In her summary, Closser reported that Newport admitted putting 5 mg of Ambien in Pierpont's chicken, touching her and ejaculating "on her stomach and her vagina."
Five milligrams is the standard starting dose of Ambien prescribed for women. It is meant to help someone fall asleep, not to keep them unconscious.
The Pinellas County crime laboratory also contradicts the story:
No semen was detected on the tested swabs, including those collected from Pierpont's navel and genitals, or on the underwear she submitted.
The lab detected male DNA on her cervical and vaginal swabs, but too little to identify whose. A trace like that cannot show how or when it got there. It does not prove penetration, and it does not rule it out.
Newport's DNA was detected on Pierpont's breast, pubic area, buttocks, and the waistband of her underwear. The couple was married, and Newport says they had intimate contact when she was awake that night but did not have intercourse.
The sample from Pierpont's buttocks contained DNA from three contributors: Pierpont, Newport, and an unidentified person.
DNA from an unidentified male was detected on Pierpont's navel. The laboratory excluded Newport as its source. According to the detective, Newport's "confession" said he ejaculated on her stomach. The male DNA found there was not his.
Her blood and urine were tested. The lab detected zolpidem, the active ingredient in Ambien. But the report did not say whether it came from blood or urine, or how much was present.
Newport says she took Ambien on her own, from prescriptions in his name.
TWO STORIES, NO SEMEN
Pierpont gave police two versions of the same act.
First, she told Closser that on December 24, the day after, Newport told her he "finished on" their son's comforter.
Then came the March recording. According to the detective's summary, Newport said he ejaculated "on her stomach and her vagina."
The comforter, or her body. The record does not say which.
Either way, there should have been semen somewhere. The lab found none on her: not on her stomach, not on her genitals, not on her underwear. The comforter, the one place she first said it went, was never tested.
Newport says neither happened and that she coached the confession on tape and he said it to save their marriage.
WHAT NO ONE TESTED
Pierpont told police she wore a sports bra, shirt, sweatshirt, sweatpants, and underwear. Her examination kit held a gray bra, a Christmas sweater, and blue leggings. The lab tested her underwear. The file shows no testing of the bra, the sweater, or the leggings.
Two blankets from her exam went into evidence, and police collected a third blanket on March 4. The file shows no lab test of any of them.
Pierpont told police Newport had said he "finished on" their son's comforter, which meant he had ejaculated on it.
Blankets from her exam went into evidence. The file shows no lab test of any of them.
Semen can remain detectable on fabric for weeks. Testing the comforter could have supported her account, or undercut it. The file does not say whether investigators collected that comforter.
She saved her dinner. The county lab told Closser it “would not meet criteria to be analyzed.” The food had been in Pierpont’s hands for three months. She had her hair tested at a private lab. She never had the food tested. And when the county lab said no, nothing in the file shows police tried anywhere else.
Add it up. They never tested the clothes she described. The blankets were never tested. Her dinner was never tested. Her iPad folder was never examined. Her cloud records were never requested. Her phone was never searched.
Every one of those tests could have confirmed her story or undercut it. Police ran none of them. They tested his bank accounts, his crypto accounts, and his phone.
That is not an investigation of what happened that night. It is an investigation of him.
SHE KEPT EATING HIS COOKING
Newport says he cooked and cleaned and kept the house. He says Pierpont and the boys ate his meals and drank his milkshakes from December 23 until the night before his arrest. His father and friends saw it, he says, and can confirm it.
If he is telling the truth, she believed her husband drugged her food, and she kept eating it for five months. She also let her sons eat it.
On May 18, he says she ate the dinner he cooked. Police arrested him the next morning.
WHAT SHE STOOD TO GAIN
I do not know whether Pierpont is telling the truth. I do know she had reasons to want Newport out of her life and her sons' lives.
The first reason is custody. A divorce could give Newport partial custody. Florida law also starts from an equal split of marital property. A typical divorce would likely give him about half.
A man in jail does not get partial custody. Newport says that in their divorce, she is asking for full custody of their two sons and 100 percent of their property.
There was also the matter of life insurance. Pierpont was the beneficiary of coverage worth several million dollars.
THE TIMING
The brother's plan came in February 2025, while Newport was sick. Pierpont went to the police in March 2026 as he recovered.
On April 22, 2026, he returned to Delta. Newport says that within a day of his return to Delta, Pierpont accessed his employee benefits account and increased his life-insurance coverage to the maximum available amount.
Newport recalls Pierpont telling him: "You never know if cancer comes back." He describes two additional transactions: an April 30 property listing on which she signed his name without authorization, and a transfer of 51 percent of a rental property to her mother about two weeks before his arrest.
Four weeks after he went back to work, he was in jail.
Now, Newport says, the cancer is back. He cannot get to the surgeons who saved him the first time. His doctor, he says, warned that without surgery he could die within a year.
If he dies in jail, there will be no trial. Pierpont keeps the boys. She keeps the property. And, if Newport is right about the insurance, she collects the maximum.
No one has to intend that outcome for it to happen. But no one at the St. Petersburg Police Department asked who stood to gain.
QUESTIONS
Why did police never examine the iPad for the folder Pierpont described?
Why did they never ask Apple for her cloud records?
Why were the clothes she described, and the blankets, never tested?
Why did the detective accept her refusal of a controlled call?
Why did police not question a coach whose statement contradicted her own recording?
What changed between April, when the lead detective found no probable cause for child pornography, and August, when the State filed six counts?
Why did police not run the DNA of the other man found on Pierpont's naval to determine who else may have been with her that night?
None of this establishes that Pierpont fabricated her allegations.
Delayed reporting, continued contact, and private evidence gathering can all occur in genuine abuse cases.
The unanswered question is whether police subjected the competing accounts, and the motives of the people offering them, to equal scrutiny.
Part 3 will examine what police found in Newport's home. And what they did not.
Disclosure: People who support Brandon Newport hired me. I agreed to publish what I find, regardless of which side it favors. The disclosure is in Part 1.

item.title: [The Good Men Project] Psychologists Finally Put the 5 Love Languages to the Test — The Results Surprised Almost Everyone
item.dc:creator: Shara Amore
item.description: My friend Tessa and her husband Greg took the love languages quiz on their third anniversary. Tessa got “Quality Time.” Greg got “Acts of Service.” For a while, it was great. item.content:encoded:
My friend Tessa and her husband Greg took the love languages quiz on their third anniversary.
Tessa got “Quality Time.” Greg got “Acts of Service.”
For a while, it was great. Greg stopped buying her flowers and started putting his phone away at dinner. Tessa stopped planning date nights and started doing his laundry.
Then, last spring, Tessa had a brutal week at work. She came home, collapsed on the couch, and cried.
Greg, trying very hard, said: “Want me to clean the kitchen?”
“I don’t want the kitchen cleaned,” she sobbed. “I want a hug.”
“But… hugs aren’t your language.”
She told me this story and laughed until she cried again. Then she asked me something I couldn’t answer at the time:
“Is the whole love language thing even real?”
It turns out psychologists had been asking the same question.
Where the Love Languages Came From
In 1992, pastor and counselor Gary Chapman published The 5 Love Languages. It became one of the best-selling relationship books ever.
The five: words of affirmation, quality time, gifts, acts of service, and physical touch.
The idea is simple and appealing. Everyone has one primary way they feel loved. Learn your partner’s language, speak it, and your relationship thrives.
And honestly? Part of it is lovely. It got millions of couples talking about what makes them feel cared for.
But it wasn’t built on research. It came from Chapman’s counseling experience. So eventually, scientists checked.
What the Research Actually Found
In 2024, relationship researchers Emily Impett, Haeyoung Gideon Park, and Amy Muise published a review of the scientific evidence on love languages.
Their conclusion was gentle but clear: the core assumptions didn’t hold up well.
Most people don’t have one dominant love language. When researchers measure it, people tend to value all five, often quite a lot.
And the evidence that couples are happier when they “match” or speak each other’s specific language was weak.
Instead, the researchers suggested a different metaphor.
Love isn’t a language you need to translate.
It’s more like a balanced diet.
You don’t just need protein. You need a bit of everything. Some days you need more of one thing than another, depending on what’s going on.
Tessa doesn’t only need quality time.
On a bad night, she needs a hug.
On a big day, she needs words.
Always, she needs all of it.
What Actually Makes People Feel Loved
Relationship scientists often point to something bigger than any single “language”: responsiveness. Feeling that your partner understands you, values you, and cares about what you need right now.
Not what a quiz said three years ago.
Right now.
- Ask, don’t assume. “What would help most tonight?” beats any personality result. Needs change with the day.
- Offer a little of everything. A kind word, a few minutes of undivided attention, a hand on the shoulder, a small favor. Variety is the point.
- Watch for the moment, not the category. Stress often calls for comfort. Good news often calls for celebration. Read the room.
- Use the quiz as a conversation starter, not a rulebook. It’s great for learning what your partner tends to appreciate. It’s not a reason to withhold a hug.
- Notice what they light up about. People often show you how they want to be loved by how they love others.
…
What Happened With Tessa and Greg
They still joke about “the kitchen incident.”
But Greg changed his approach. Now, when she walks in looking wrecked, he asks one question: “Fix it, hug it, or talk it?”
Most nights, she picks “hug it.” Sometimes all three. Occasionally, “fix it,” which usually means pizza.
“It’s not that the love languages were wrong,” Tessa told me. “It’s that I’m not just one thing.”
If You Take One Thing Away…
We think love means finding the one right language.
Research says it means paying attention to what someone needs today.
Love languages matter because they got us talking about how we feel cared for. But no quiz can replace actually asking.
Don’t speak one language.
Speak the moment.
Awareness always comes before change.
If this stirred something in you, that’s worth paying attention to.
Do you really have just one love language? Or do you need a little of everything?
I write more about the psychology of emotional safety, attraction, and modern relationships in my newsletter, Great Life for You.
You’re welcome to join if this resonated.
This space is for people who want depth over performance.
—
This post was previously published on medium.com.

item.title: [Deseret News] Opinion: Hookup culture isn’t working. Young people are hungry for something better
item.dc:creator: Tim Rarick
item.description: While presenting at a Princeton conference on the impact fathers have on romantic and sexual relationships, a male student asked me: How do men learn to build healthy, lasting relationships with women? “I’ve tried hooking up,” he said. “It isn’t working.” When I shared some basic research on how trust and love are built between two people, I expected hope. item.content:encoded:
While presenting at a Princeton conference on the impact fathers have on romantic and sexual relationships, a male student asked me: How do men learn to build healthy, lasting relationships with women?
“I’ve tried hooking up,” he said. “It isn’t working.”
When I shared some basic research on how trust and love are built between two people, I expected hope. Instead, he grew visibly frustrated: “Why has no one ever shown me this?”
“All I’ve ever been shown is sex, with commitment and intimacy being optional,” he continued. “I don’t know anything else, and it isn’t working!”
This young man was right to feel deceived. Modern dating culture routinely promotes physical hookups while skipping the foundations of intimacy and trust, leaving young men and women primed for sex but completely unprepared for long-term, committed love.
Sexually active and profoundly lonely
This is the quiet tragedy beneath a very loud national conversation. Was this student an outlier? Or was he simply honest enough to say out loud what many of his peers are feeling?
Since that day, I have heard numerous versions of his frustration from students on campuses across the country. They are bright, ambitious and sexually liberated … or so they’ve been told.
Yet many of them are silently lonely. Ironically, a generation raised on the promise of sexual freedom often finds itself less free to build the very relationships it most wants.
An ‘old-fashioned’ idea
Saying the word “chastity” on most college campuses today is likely to result in laughter, mocking or even contempt. For many in the Western world, it sounds hopelessly behind the times — a prudish list of restrictive “don’ts” handed down from a repressive age.
But this caricatures a profoundly rich idea. At its heart, chastity is not merely the absence of sex before marriage. It is a vision of what sex is for: the conviction that physical intimacy belongs within a relationship of trust, commitment and genuinely knowing another person. Chastity is where two people seek each other’s good, not just each other’s consent.
Chastity is not the enemy of love. It is love’s partner and protector. And contrary to popular perception, this timeless truth is as needed as ever.
Chastity is where two people seek each other’s good, not just each other’s consent.
In “How to Avoid Falling in Love with a Jerk,” John Van Epp identifies five areas that build deep attachments between two people: knowing, trusting, relying on, committing to and touching one another. Healthy relationships build these bonds in that order, and the rule is simple: never go further in one area than you have in the one before it.
Hookup culture makes a mess out of this sequence, elevating touch first, the deepest bond of all, which can give both parties a false sense of knowing and trusting each other while leaving reliance and commitment optional. Through this lens, we see that chastity isn’t arbitrary or naive. It honors the order in which love is actually built.
Consent is essential, but it’s a floor, not a ceiling
One of the groups best positioned to hand a healthier sexual script to the next generation is fathers. But their message needs to go beyond “Make sure she says yes.”
Consent, of course, is essential. Columnist Christine Emba insightfully described consent as “the floor,” the minimum that separates a sexual encounter from a crime.
But a floor is not a ceiling. Consent can tell us whether something was a violation. It cannot tell us whether it was good, wise, loving or dignifying. A culture that knows how to ask only “Was there consent?” has forgotten how to ask everything that sits above it, including intimacy, trust, commitment, sacrifice and dare I say: love.
“As long as both consent” is the sexual script the Princeton students had been handed. They were given the floor and told it was the whole house.
Consent can tell us whether something was a violation. It cannot tell us whether it was good, wise, loving or dignifying.
The consent conundrum
One detail from the recent Cornell sexual assault lawsuit was especially disturbing. In the early morning hours, one of the men allegedly posted to the fraternity’s group chat that sex was available upstairs, using words too crude to print here. He described the young woman as “free.”
It is hard to imagine a darker distortion of the freedom the sexual revolution promised. A message like that is a failure of more than consent ethics — seeing a young woman not as a person to be known, protected or honored but as an available commodity.
On social media, dads are asking why not one of the seven young men had the guts to respond, “No! That is not how we treat a woman!”
Questions about consent, burden of proof and accountability are important. But they are all about the floor — asking whether a line was crossed. None of them asks why a group of bright young men at an Ivy League school would see a young woman that way in the first place.
While there are many influences on perception, the widespread use of pornography among young men is hard to ignore. Research on fraternity members finds that those who view pornography are significantly less likely to step in to stop a sexual assault.
Tragically, whether we like it or not, pornography has become sex education for a generation, with the power to shape developing minds and hearts.
Dad power
Courts can punish and Title IX offices can sanction, but neither can shape a young man’s heart. That work happens much earlier and ideally much closer to home.
The father-son relationship may be one of the most overlooked tools we have for preventing sexual violence. The presence and warmth of a father growing up is one of the strongest predictors of how a man handles his emotions, including aggression and how he treats women.
A boy learns what a man does with his strength, his desire and his power by watching the man closest to him. Does Dad speak of women with respect or with lust and contempt? Does he honor his wife or use and mistreat her? Does he show his son that real men protect the vulnerable rather than exploit them?
Sons are watching, and they are taking notes long before they are old enough to join a fraternity. That’s where a young man’s moral intuitions are formed — not in a mandatory university orientation session at age 18.
Mothers, of course, also have an enormous influence on sons. And the father-daughter relationship carries its own enormous potential. Wake Forest psychologist Linda Nielsen says a father has “the greater influence on his daughter’s ability to trust, enjoy and relate well to the men in her life.” Young women whose fathers were highly involved tend to report more intimacy, commitment and trust in their own romantic relationships.
None of these findings places the burden of preventing assault on young women. Responsibility for sexual violence and exploitation belongs entirely to those who commit it. But a daughter who knows her worth from the inside out, because she has been loved well by the first man in her life, is more likely to have emotionally fulfilling relationships and to recognize real love when it comes.
Show them how
Fathers can teach a better way, but first and foremost, they have to live it. Children absorb what they see long before they understand what they hear. A father who builds genuine trust and commitment with their mother earns the credibility to explain why it matters. More than just words, his life becomes the lesson. So fathers, two big things you can do:
- Treat your children’s mother, and every woman, with respect. Your sons and daughters are learning what love looks like by watching you.
- Show your daughters in words, time and attention that they are loved unconditionally and deserve to be treated with dignity.
Also, be a father figure to those who don’t have one. Fatherlessness, the absence of men who model and teach a better way, has left a generation to learn about love from a script written by the culture rather than the home.
It’s been said that a society can have sexual freedom or strong families, but not both. Consent and law enforcement will always matter, but they are the floor — not the whole house.
There’s a much bigger, more beautiful picture for our children to understand. And that’s on us as parents. Let’s make sure no child of ours ever has to ask, “Why has no one ever shown me this?”

item.title: [Yahoo] Is LinkedIn the New Hinge? Why People Are Using Job Apps to Find Love and Dating Apps to Network
item.dc:creator: Lisa Milbrand

item.content:encoded:
You'd think that all these hyper-focused social media apps would make us more successful at reaching our goals, whether we're looking for love, connecting with friends, or trying to get a leg up in our career. But quite a few people are taking a more unconventional approach. Think using LinkedIn to find prospective dates—or swiping right for professional networking, not a hot date.
In fact, a recent Resume Builder survey found that one in three dating app users opted to use it for professional networking—including nearly half of those in the highest income brackets (earning $200,000 or more). And in the other direction, one in eight LinkedIn users have found romance on LinkedIn—even though 65% of those surveyed by Zety were concerned that it would damage their reputation.
So should you be seeking love (or a new job) in all the wrong places? Experts aren't so sure.
Stacie Haller, chief career advisor at Resume Builder
Kristen Zavo, career expert and author of Find Your Job Joy
Why People Are Shaking Up Social Media App Use
If you've been ghosted on dozens of job applications—or on dating apps—you can probably understand the appeal of trying something new to reach your goals.
"Traditional job-search methods can feel crowded and impersonal, and many job seekers struggle to get results," says Stacie Haller, chief career advisor at Resume Builder. "Candidates compete for attention on LinkedIn, while online applications often go unanswered, leaving people struggling to get noticed. Dating apps create a more natural setting for conversation, giving people the chance to establish a personal connection before professional goals enter the picture."
And people have been finding success with it—the Resume Builder research found that 88% of respondents who used dating apps for professional reasons successfully made a professional connection.
"Many job seekers are already familiar with these platforms, making them more comfortable reaching out to others and starting conversations—and that rapport can make networking feel less transactional and lead to genuine professional relationships," Haller says. "A conversation that starts around shared interests can lead to career advice, a referral, or an introduction to someone who can help open doors to new opportunities."
Why Experts Are Conflicted on Mixing Up Your App Game
Just because some people have found success with this unconventional approach doesn't mean it's a brilliant plan, and it can just as easily backfire on you.
"When we use a platform, there's an implicit understanding about why we're all there," says Kristen Zavo, career expert and author of Find Your Job Joy. "People are on LinkedIn to build professional relationships and explore career opportunities. They're on dating apps to find romantic connections. When someone approaches you with a completely different agenda, it can feel disingenuous and erode trust before a relationship even begins."
That can be especially true with reaching out for romance on a career website, which has been a major ick for many women. "I've personally experienced unsolicited romantic advances on LinkedIn, and I find them offputting," Zavo says. "Just because someone is accessible doesn't mean they're inviting every kind of interaction."
Bottom line: It's a risky move. "I'm all for creativity when it comes to building relationships and finding opportunities," Zavo says. "But there's a difference between thinking outside the box and approaching people with an ulterior motive."
How to Reach Your Goals the Right Way
Whether you're seeking personal or career fulfillment, there are ways to use this controversial approach in your favor—or find other methods that could be just as successful for you.
Be transparent about what you're doing
If you're using a social media account in an unexpected way, you need to be honest about that fact. "The key is transparency," Haller says. "Anyone using a dating app to make professional connections should be up front about their intentions rather than risk misleading someone. Not everyone on the app is looking to network, so it's important to respect those boundaries."
In either direction, it's a bad idea to start off in bad faith. "If someone is genuinely interested in getting to know you romantically, but you're primarily interested in accessing their professional network, you're starting the relationship on the wrong foot," Zavo says.
Be realistic about what you can achieve this way
Making a connection in an unexpected way may only get you so far. In job hunt terms, think of it more like an informational interview, where you may be able to add another point of contact that could get you closer to the job or relationship you want, rather than completely across the finish line.
"Expanding networking beyond traditional career platforms can help people connect with others who may play a role in their job search," Haller says. "Building relationships can help candidates get advice, secure referrals, and learn about roles they might not find on their own."
Shake up your job (or romance) hunt
If you aren't finding success with what you're doing, take a good hard look and see if there are ways to approach it differently, beyond reaching out on a different platform.
"When the job search starts to feel hopeless, the answer usually isn't sending out more applications, it's getting more intentional," Haller says. "Go after the roles you're genuinely a fit for, take the time to tailor your resume, and get your application in early. Most of all, talk to people. Someone who can vouch for you will get you further than a stack of cold applications ever will."
You may have better luck reaching out to people who are already in your network, Zavo says. "Rather than trying to turn a dating app into a job board, think about how you can expand your network in ways that create genuine connections. That might mean reconnecting with former colleagues, joining professional or community groups, attending events, or reaching out to people whose work genuinely interests you."
Take your hunt offline
We're all looking for a little (or a lot) less screen time, so put down the phone and mix and mingle toward your goal in a more expected setting—like an in-person speed dating get-together or a networking event, where you can more readily make the kinds of connections that you're seeking.
"Even as technology changes how people apply for jobs, personal connections remain an important part of how people get hired," Haller says.
"I absolutely encourage job seekers to prioritize relationship-building over simply submitting applications online, but there are much more authentic ways to do that than using a dating app as a networking tool," Zavo says. "My advice is simple: Be creative about how you meet people, but be genuine about why you're connecting with them. The best opportunities, whether personal or professional, often come from relationships we didn't initially expect—but those relationships need to be built on trust."
Read the original article on Real Simple

These moments can reveal how comfortably your relationship fits into your wider life, without requiring you to make a decision before you are ready.
Single: An old friend or familiar face could bring a pleasant surprise. Enjoy the interaction and see whether the connection has room to grow.
In a relationship: You may want your partner to meet your family or join a gathering. Talk about the idea openly so you both feel comfortable with the next step.
Married: Spending time with relatives could bring warmth to the day. Share responsibilities with your spouse so the gathering feels enjoyable rather than exhausting.
Also Read: Sagittarius Horoscope 2026| Sagittarius October Horoscope|Sagittarius Weekly Horoscope
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
You do not have to win every disagreement to feel secure. A small difference of opinion could become more significant if you focus only on getting your way. The better approach is to understand why the other person sees things differently, particularly when family matters are involved.
Single: Social events may give you a chance to meet someone outside your usual circle. Be open to conversation without feeling obliged to pursue every connection.
In a relationship: If you and your partner disagree about plans, ask what matters most to each of you. You may discover a compromise that neither of you considered initially.
Married: A family gathering or an outing could lift your mood. Avoid overthinking a passing comment, and give your spouse the benefit of the doubt.
Also Read: Capricorn Horoscope 2026| Capricorn October Horoscope| Capricorn Weekly Horoscope
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Do not let other people's opinions decide what happens in your relationship. Friends and relatives may have something to say about your personal life. Listen if their advice is useful, but avoid reaching conclusions based on incomplete information. Your relationship deserves a fair conversation between the people actually involved.
Single: A friend could introduce you to someone interesting. Stay open to meeting them, but make your own judgment rather than relying entirely on someone else's recommendation.
In a relationship: If an outside opinion has unsettled you, discuss it with your partner before letting it affect your behaviour. Ask questions instead of assuming the worst.
Married: Family concerns may require a sensitive conversation. Respect other people's perspectives while making sure you and your spouse decide important matters together.
Also Read: Aquarius Horoscope 2026| Aquarius October Horoscope| Aquarius Weekly Horoscope
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
You can support everyone else without forgetting your own emotional needs. With the Moon in your sign, feelings may sit closer to the surface. You might be busy helping others while privately worrying about something of your own. Give yourself permission to explain what you need instead of pretending everything is fine.
Single: Someone's kindness or thoughtful advice may leave a lasting impression. Enjoy getting to know them, but allow the connection to develop at a pace that feels comfortable.
In a relationship: Your partner may be willing to help with a problem you have been handling alone. Let them in, and be honest if you need comfort rather than advice.
Married: Family responsibilities could keep you occupied, but shared effort can make the day easier. Spend some time with your spouse without letting every conversation turn into a discussion about duties.
Also Read: Pisces Horoscope 2026| Pisces October Horoscope| Pisces Weekly Horoscope
Conclusion
The love horoscope for October 24, 2026, puts emotional support and everyday partnership in focus. Singles may find new possibilities through friends and family, while couples can strengthen their bond by sharing responsibilities and handling disagreements with care. With the Moon in Pisces and Venus retrograde in Libra, use the day to reflect on what makes you feel valued and how you show that appreciation to others. Love becomes stronger when both people feel heard.
Written by: Tanya Singh of Astropatri.com.

item.content:encoded:
The ‘non-toxic’ dating app that’s been built in Brunswick
Developer promises his app will deliver a ‘kinder and gentler’ dating experience
Does the world really need another dating app?
Alistair Kitchen thinks probably not – but it could do with a better one.
Fed up with the “enshittification” of popular apps like Hinge, Tinger and Bumble, the Brunswick writer has invented his own called One.
Touted as a kinder, gentler app, One has just been launched upon the world.
“The dating apps that are currently out there are causing a lot of pain and dissatisfaction in the world,” said Kitchen, who settled in Brunswick last year after returning from living in the United States for more than half-a-decade.
“They are, without exception, toxic, harmful, and extractive, and that’s because they’re all built on the same business model, and that business model causes these downstream effects, which incentivises the apps to keep people swiping, keep people alone, keep people single.
“I think the situation right now is dire, and we have an opportunity to replace these pretty toxic models with something a bit healthier, a bit less toxic, and a little bit kinder on single people.”
Kitchen says several aspects differentiate One from the other apps.
Most significantly, while it is currently free, users will eventually pay a one-off, lifetime fee to use the app rather than monthly subscription fees.
Kitchen promises that One will also provide a deeper, curated matchmaking experience based on a five to 10 minute verbal questionnaire to determine compatibility with potential matches.
And rather than swiping left or right based on a person’s brief profile and/or photo, One users will only be provided with three to five potential matches each day and will be restricted to choosing just one of them.
“The big difference is those apps are uncurated, and this app is heavily curated, so people can spend a lot less time swiping and a lot more time connecting,” Kitchen said.
Now 34, Kitchen has been a user of dating apps since Tinder arrived on the scene during his first year of university.
“I came of age and was thrown into this new world and, like I think a lot of people, found the dating apps in that era – 2012 through to, you know, 2018 – to be really additive and interesting and kind of vibrant,” he said.
“And then pretty soon after that they rapidly started to enshittify.”
‘Enshittification’ is a phrase coined by the Canadian writer Corey Doctorow to describe the process of how online and mobile products and services degrade over time as financial realities mean their developers are forced to compromise on their original principles.
“My personal experience was these incredibly useful, interesting, vibrant technologies degraded before my eyes,” Kitchen continued.
“And it got to a point where I thought, well, someone should build a business model which will not incentivise the apps to enshittify.”
One took about six months to build before a low key launch to a local inner northern suburbs market. It has gained about 500 users in its first few weeks in Apple’s and Google’s app stores.
After it reaches about 1000 users, Kitchen will broaden marketing of the app and introducing a price (probably $100), although he has no aspirations for global domination.
Kitchen’s name may be familiar as he was in the news last year after he was detained and refused entry to the United States because of what he alleged was his political activities.
Kitchen lived in the US for six years, including a period studying creative non-fiction writing at Columbia University in New York City.
According to reports at the time, Kitchen had been travelling from Melbourne to New York to visit friends when he was detained and interrogated for 12 hours at Los Angeles airport about blog posts he wrote on protests at Columbia University against the war in Gaza during his time as a student there.
But the US Department of Homeland Security said the reason why he was sent back to Australia was for giving false information on an entry form.
The incident gained attention because it was during the Trump government’s crackdown on immigration and dissent.
Kitchen has lived in Brunswick for about a year, choosing an apartment in the area because “it was the closest thing to my life in New York”.
Despite developing an app, he said he was first and foremost a writer and was working on a book of essays about gender and masculinity in Australia, which he had begun writing and researching while he was studying in the US.

item.content:encoded:
Trendy Gaaner Story celebrates romance with a song that captures its innocence and intimacy
Trendy Gaaner Story
Created by indie music band Chirkut, Trendy Gaaner Story is a romantic comedy number based on the spirit of Durga Puja. Dropped at the onset of the festive season, it presents the continuation of the love story between a young couple that was shown to have blossomed in the music video of last year's Puja release Ashtami te tomar paray by the same band.
A lively and joyful duet, it expresses how love, emotion and innocence always finds a way into our hearts during this time of the year. Released as a sequel to Ashtami te tomar paray, the song captures the anticipation, excitement of pandal-hopping and romantic association of Durga Puja in Kolkata. Also titled Ashtami 2.0, the song stars actors Soumya Mukherjee and Arunima Halder as the pair of young lovers, depicting how their love story has stood the test of time across the year gone by. Its lyrics by Prameya and Team Chirkut express the playful and relatable nature of modern romance, blending trends of digital dating with a desire for old-school romance. The track pokes fun at a stubborn girlfriend whose anger doesn't melt easily even during Durga Puja, capturing lighthearted banter, puppy love and youthful flirting.
The visuals capture the festive energy of Kolkata during Durga Puja — it is full of warm festival lights and the glowing ambience of colourful, decorated pandals that mirror the mood of the season. The visuals follow a persistent, bumbling, or earnest young lover who chases after and dreams about his beloved through the days of the festival, getting dressed up on Saptami and finally mustering the courage to head to her neighbourhood on Ashtami, hoping to rebuild their love story.
The song takes a dig at superficial modern dating trends like taking quick selfies just to post a 'trending story' which fades in a couple of days. It contrasts this with genuine, old-school devotion that is tinged with nervousness and excitement but withstands the test of time. Beyond just the story of a young couple in love, Trendy Gaaner Story celebrates the vibrant, collective joy, music and carefree spirit of celebrations by young people in Bengal during Durga Puja.
Blending a traditional Bengali culture with modern, upbeat and social-media-friendly energy, Trendy Gaaner Story appears designed for social media reels on festive themes and is expected to be a popular anthem among the new generation of Bengali music lovers.

item.dc:creator: Abigail Van Buren
item.description: Dear Abby: Our 24-year-old daughter, “Becca,” and her 26-year-old boyfriend, “Jason,” (the father of our 7-year-old granddaughter) recently bought a home. Jason works only part time — if he works at all — and has no interest in a full-time job. One issue, however, really weighs heavily on our minds. item.content:encoded:
Dear Abby: Our 24-year-old daughter, “Becca,” and her 26-year-old boyfriend, “Jason,” (the father of our 7-year-old granddaughter) recently bought a home. Jason works only part time — if he works at all — and has no interest in a full-time job.
One issue, however, really weighs heavily on our minds.
Whenever we pick up our granddaughter (which we do quite often) we are almost knocked over by the smell of marijuana in their home. My husband and I have voiced our concerns about this more than once, to no avail. Our other children have mentioned the strong odor in her home as well.
My husband and I can’t stand the thought of our granddaughter living in that environment, but we don’t know what we should do about it. Abby, what do you advise? — Worried About the Weed in Indiana
Dear Worried: You and your husband should continue having a serious conversation with your daughter about this. Tell her you smell a strong marijuana odor when you pick your granddaughter up, and that you are worried about her inhaling the smoke, because it’s unhealthy for children. Perhaps she and her boyfriend can choose to smoke outside their house when they feel the need to get high.
Inform them that if the child ever inhales enough secondhand smoke to test positive for THC, there could be serious legal repercussions (beyond the fact that — as you probably know — cannabis use is still illegal in Indiana).
Dear Abby: My husband, who is 86, has an indirect communication style. He’ll say something like, “I need to do some pruning on the climbing rose, but it’s too high for me to reach.” I ask specific questions to determine what exactly, if anything, he wants me to do, but his responses are often vague. An example: I will ask, “Are you asking me to set up the ladder for you?” to which he might reply, “I can’t reach the top of the roses.”
No matter how many questions I ask, he resists giving me a direct answer. This frustrates me, and it frustrates him that I don’t get his meaning instantly. Is there anything I can do to cut to the chase so I’ll know what he’s asking me to do? I’m happy to help him; I just want to know what he wants without the interrogation. — Verbal Dance Partner
Dear Partner: What you have described is normal in households or regions (including East and Southeast Asia and parts of Europe) where people are taught to prioritize the comfort of others. In those cultures, it’s considered rude and aggressive to make a direct request, even of a loved one.
Because he may have learned these values from his parents, know that this may be a lifelong habit that would be hard for him to break. If you ask him directly to change his ways, he may regard that as overbearing. Fortunately, you seem to have mostly cracked the code. You know his offhand remarks are actually requests, so do your best to help in ways that make sense to you. If you sometimes don’t deliver exactly what he’s looking for, it’s up to him to clarify.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.dc:creator: TOI Astrology; Oct

item.content:encoded:
Each sign of the zodiac has its own set of traits that help to define their personalities and set them apart from each other. Wouldn't it be nice to know what the universe has planned for you at the beginning of the day? Keep reading to find out if today will be lucky for you.
ARIES
Old patterns of thought may surface now, but they are not there to hurt you. Singles, take a moment to recognize the prior patterns you seem to keep walking into again and again. Let them go, a little. If you have a partner, start the talk about what still rests in your heart. You don’t have to solve everything today, but at least it will help move you in the right direction. When you both recognize a little of the old grief, there is opportunity for a new relationship to grow.
Taurus
There may be something that feels stuck in your romantic life today. Single Taurus, think about what’s stopping you from expressing a clear yes or no. Not often is silence the safer option. If you are serious about someone, get it off your chest when something has been bugging you. Holding it inside will just construct a wall between you and others. You don't have to holler, just tell. Love must act. So if not fast, then slow.
See yourself. Hear yourself. That could be the first step to loving again.
GEMINI
There is something that may feel trapped in your romantic life today. Single Taurus, consider what prevents you from saying a clear yes or no. Shutting up isn't always the safer option. If you care about someone, get it off of your chest when something has been upsetting you. Holding it inside will just create a wall between you and others. You don't have to yell; just tell. Love must move. So if not fast, then slow. See and listen to yourself. That could be the very first step to loving again.
CANCER
Today you will be uncertain about things. If single, Stop guessing. Ask that question and don't be a victim of overthinking. If it has already happened, a little talk could go a long way in clearing the air. Don't sit around waiting for your partner to bring it up. You can move things with clear words only. When truth comes confusion goes. Keep it simple and honest. It can change far more than you think.
LEO
There may be a sense that you aren't being heard on matters of the heart today. If you are single, you should not waste your time explaining yourself to someone who is not actually paying attention. Just let them go. If you are in a relationship, watch out for repeating yourself too much; in this case, step back and allow the quiet fill the distance between you. You do not have to try to understand it deliberately every time. “The right person will try to get you without you doing all the talking.
VIRGO
What love looks like to you now can be totally different. Singles will find an admirer appearing from nowhere. They won’t be the traditional candidate but they certainly deserve a try. If you are in a relationship, romance will likely have a totally different form from presents and dates. It could be a helping hand, a surprising grin or a splitting-up chuckle. Find it with love there if it's not loud. Be open to this other type of coming together.
LIBRA
Love invites you to select what feels real, not what seems thrilling, today. If you are single, don't go for someone who keeps you in the dark. Both spark and tranquility are good to need. If you are in a relationship, you may be trying too hard to have fun. You should have it easy. Comfort is the enemy of fun, not short lived fun. Breathe relief in your longing for something more than delight. Love has to feel safe and exhilarating.
SCORPIO
You could be highly aware of the back-and-forth of emotional signals today. That’s your indicator as a single who previously identified the feeling that someone can calm you and give you some form of steadiness. But if you're in a relationship, create some place for that, instead of holding back how you really feel. Let your partner do the same. Trust is formed when both sides feel safe to be who they are. It doesn't have to be the right words.
Sagittarius
A feeling may occur in your love life. If you are single, stand by for those red flags even when the person appears entertaining. If you are in a relationship, this tiny quarrel may be the emergence of a major issue. Don't just brush it off; talk about it. The reality that this period will bring you will assist you to move on easily. Tension is not so horrible if it is honest; sometimes love is a helpful hand to set its course.
CAPRICORN
You are probably on the very brink of anything real in love. If you're still single, your intellect could say, 'wait,' but your heart says it's time to try. Listen To. If you are committed, take some moves toward what you have been avoiding. Have a hopeful conversation or make plans for the future. You’re more prepared than you know. Fear will come and go, but love has to travel through you. Don’t lose it today.
Aquarius
Look at what individuals do today, not what they say. Actions speak louder than words and if you are single then the actions one takes may demonstrate whether he/she has any interest in you more so than any promises. If you have already committed, notice the little things the individual does for you. Maybe your partner has been silently trying. Let them see you observe. Love talks in nice deeds. Just go with it. Forget about it.
PISCES
The energies today are asking you to show up precisely as you are. If you’re single, don’t wait until you’re all ready or entirely perfect. Someone may be liking you just how you are right now. If you are in a relationship be present, don’t do everything properly. Release the pressure to mend or plan. Your attention is worth more than any flawless move. This is what counts today: Be here, present with imperfect love."
This article is written by, Sidhharrth S Kumaar, Registered Pharmacist, Astro Numerologist, Life & Relationship Coach, Vaastu Expert, IKS Expert, I Ching Expert, Energy Healer, Music Therapist, Author of “Think like a Sage Lead like a CEO” series and Chief Astro Strategy Officer (CASO), NumroVani.

item.content:encoded:
Horoscope Today, October 23, 2026: Keep your heart open and let mutual trust grow through steady actions today
Horoscope Today, October 23, 2026, read predictions for all sun signs
October 23 brings a powerful blend of swift action and grounded focus. Some signs will see long-stalled plans take off at high speed, while others are guided to protect their space and build steady foundations. Trust that today offers the exact clarity you need to handle every challenge without feeling rushed. Keep your mind steady, because the choices you make now will open clear paths ahead.
Aries Horoscope Today
Focus on your stability, finances, and physical well-being today. Taking a practical approach will help you manage daily responsibilities while creating space for personal comfort and genuine connections. Instead of scattering your energy, give your long-term goals the steady attention they deserve. Building security starts with small, daily choices that support your peace of mind.
Love Focus: Choose the connection that brings both warmth and quiet emotional stability.
Taurus Horoscope Today
Curiosity brings fresh opportunities your way, so stay observant and open. An unexpected conversation or discovery could prompt you to look at an old plan with fresh eyes. Ask clear questions before jumping to conclusions or taking on new commitments. Gathering facts right now will help you spot genuine potential from temporary distractions.
Love Focus: Let genuine curiosity guide your talks instead of making quick assumptions.
Gemini Horoscope Today
Life moves at a brisk pace today, bringing sudden messages, fresh deadlines, and exciting prospects. Stay organized so you can respond promptly without losing your focus or accuracy. Use this swift momentum to clear pending work and follow up on promising leads. Pacing yourself ensures you enjoy the excitement without feeling drained.
Love Focus: Enjoy the lively momentum in your love life without rushing heavy commitments.
Cancer Horoscope Today
Clear boundaries and direct communication are your best tools right now. Handle sensitive topics by looking at the facts rather than letting emotional pressure cloud your vision. You can express your expectations with complete kindness while keeping your standards intact. Standing firm in your worth earns respect and keeps your mind clear.
Love Focus: Speak your emotional needs directly with calm confidence and warmth.
Leo Horoscope Today
Your natural warmth and creative spark draw supportive energy into your day. Nurturing your personal ideas and key relationships brings a rich sense of fulfillment. Focus on steady, sustainable progress rather than chasing instant results. Give your projects time to develop organically while accepting help from people who support your vision.
Love Focus: Give affection freely while creating space to receive the same care back.
Virgo Horoscope Today
Looking beyond immediate routines helps you map out an exciting future path. Your steady daily efforts are quietly setting up opportunities for broader professional and personal growth. Outline clear long-term ambitions, break them into manageable steps, and remain patient. Real progress takes time, so trust the process you have started.
Love Focus: Keep your heart open and let mutual trust grow through steady actions.
Libra Horoscope Today
Strong motivation drives you to tackle tough tasks and voice your perspective. Decisive action clears lingering confusion, but rushing through details could cause minor missteps. Pause long enough to verify key facts and consider outcomes before making firm promises. Clear, thoughtful communication will keep your relationships running smoothly.
Love Focus: Be transparent about your feelings while giving others room to respond.
Scorpio Horoscope Today
A wave of enthusiasm inspires you to step outside your usual routine and try something new. Channel this vibrant energy into concrete action steps toward a goal you have delayed. Avoid impulsive financial choices or promising more than you can practically deliver. Balancing passion with realistic planning brings lasting success.
Love Focus: Let natural chemistry bring you close, but let real trust guide your steps.
Sagittarius Horoscope Today
Unshakable determination helps you tackle heavy workloads and reach key milestones. Keep competing priorities under control by focusing entirely on your single most important goal. Spreading your energy or finances too thin will only slow your momentum. disciplined, focused effort carries you past any minor obstacles in your way.
Love Focus: State your romantic intentions clearly without trying to force or control outcomes.
Capricorn Horoscope Today
You may need to defend your ideas or hold firm lines around your workload. Trust the experience you have gathered, but stay receptive to useful feedback. Choose your battles wisely so you do not waste precious energy on irrelevant drama. Protecting your time keeps your progress steady and grounded.
Love Focus: Protect your personal standards without putting up defensive walls against affection.
Aquarius Horoscope Today
Weighing new possibilities reveals clever paths forward that you had not considered. Look closely at your future options to see which directions align with your real ambitions. Stepping away from familiar habits can open doors to sustainable growth. A well-thought-out strategy today turns quiet vision into actual success.
Love Focus: Select a connection that honors your individuality while fostering genuine closeness.
Pisces Horoscope Today
A sudden burst of creative inspiration encourages you to launch something exciting. Follow your curiosity, but give your ideas a solid structure so they develop into lasting results. Check practical details before investing heavy time or money. Taking small, realistic steps today brings your creative dreams into concrete reality.
Love Focus: Take a gentle romantic risk while staying completely true to your own needs.
(Inputs by Kishori Sud)

item.content:encoded:
Each reading is based on a fixed rashi tarot anchor and a six-card daily spread covering overall energy, love, career, money, health, and spiritual guidance.
MESHA RASHI / ARIESToday's Theme:
Pause before the leap, today's energy works best with courage plus better timing.
Best Area:
Career feels smoother when creativity and diplomacy lead the conversation.
Watch Out For:
Money temptations and sharp words can create avoidable stress today.
Card Reading:
The Emperor is your fixed anchor, while today's overall card, The Fool reversed, turns bold leadership toward caution, timing, and self-control. For Mesha, the day isn't about stopping action, it's about checking where impulse or hesitation is distorting the next move.
General | Card: The Fool reversed
You're ready to move fast, but the day works better when you slow the first step. The Fool reversed can feel like one part of you wants a fresh start while another part keeps second-guessing it. That can create stop-start energy, especially during a commute or while replying to a pending message. Keep plans simple. Don't announce too much too early. Progress comes from checking details, not from dramatic moves.
If something feels exciting and risky at once, give it a second look before saying yes.
Love and Relationship | Card: King of Swords reversed
Conversations in close relationships need extra care today. With King of Swords reversed in love, blunt truth can easily turn into coldness, or someone else's words may feel controlling. If you're waiting on a WhatsApp reply, don't build a full story from silence. Couples should avoid turning a small issue into a courtroom debate. Singles may meet someone intelligent yet emotionally unavailable, so stay observant. Clear words matter, but tone matters just as much. Say what you mean without trying to win.
Education and Career | Card: Knight of Cups upright
Work gets a softer, more imaginative flow through Knight of Cups upright. A client call, pitch, creative task, or even a difficult follow-up can go better when you bring charm instead of force. People respond to sincerity today. If you've been pushing too hard, change the approach and make the message more human. Students also do well with subjects that need expression and interpretation, not just speed. A good idea may arrive in a quiet moment, so note it before the rush returns.
Money and Finance | Card: The Devil upright
Money needs strong boundaries today. The Devil upright can pull attention toward compulsive spending, status pressure, or holding on too tightly to something that isn't useful anymore. Check that online shopping cart before you hit pay. A UPI payment made in haste may not be the best choice. This isn't a bad money day, but it is one where habits speak loudly. Keep your budget visible, avoid emotional purchases, and don't let urgency decide for you.
Health and Well-being | Card: Page of Cups upright
Your wellbeing improves through gentleness, not intensity. Page of Cups upright connects health with emotional softness, hydration, and small comforting routines. If your mood has been jumpy, a lighter schedule and better food timing can help. Give yourself a little breathing space between tasks. Music, journaling, or even a calmer lunch break may restore more energy than a power push today.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: Six of Wands upright
Six of Wands upright reminds you that right action builds quiet confidence. Spiritual strength grows when you notice where you've already handled things better than before. Stand before your prayer corner for one minute and let that small inner victory register.
VRISHABHA RASHI / TAURUSToday's Theme:
Home, stability, and long-term thinking feel strong, even if work shifts suddenly.
Best Area:
