A family dinner, office chai break, or kind message from a friend can reset your mood more than expected. If you’ve been too much in your own head, shared space will help. Still, choose company that feels easy and genuine. Joy is available today, but it works best when you don’t ignore your emotional limits just to fit in.
Love and Relationship | Card: Justice reversed
Something in love needs honesty, especially where balance has gone missing. Justice reversed can point to mixed accountability, one-sided effort, or a conversation where facts are being bent to avoid discomfort. If you’re partnered, don’t smooth over unfairness just to keep things pleasant. Say what felt off, but say it calmly. If you’re single, pay attention to whether someone’s words and actions match. Your compassion is beautiful, but today it needs boundaries beside it, not in place of it.
Education and Career | Card: Two of Pentacles upright
You may be handling more than one thing at once, and that’s where your strength lies today. Two of Pentacles upright suits a schedule with shifting demands, changing priorities, and quick adjustments. Work, study timetable, and personal tasks may all need space on the same day. Instead of trying to do everything perfectly, stay flexible. This card rewards rhythm over rigidity. If plans move around, don’t take it personally. Keep the essentials moving, and let smaller tasks wait their turn.
Money and Finance | Card: Five of Swords reversed
Money tension can soften if you stop replaying an old frustration. Five of Swords reversed is good for making peace with a recent expense, ending a stubborn disagreement, or moving on from a draining financial back-and-forth. If there’s a pending payment, shared cost, or overdue clarity, aim for resolution rather than winning. A practical tone works best. Keep records clear, settle what you can, and don’t let ego turn a small issue into a bigger one.
Health and Well-being | Card: Page of Swords upright
Your mind may be more active than your body can comfortably carry today. Page of Swords upright often points to mental restlessness, too much screen time, scattered focus, or sleep getting disturbed by constant thoughts. If your commute or evening routine feels overstimulating, cut down the extra noise. Short breaks, lighter scrolling, and a proper meal at the right time can help more than you think. Curiosity is high, but your nervous system still needs gentleness.
Spiritual Guidance | Card: The Fool upright
A fresh inner step is possible now. The Fool upright opens a simple path, less fear, less over-reading, more trust in the next small move. You don’t need a full map for today. Be grateful for one person, one sign, or one quiet feeling that reminded you you’re not alone.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Thursday, October 22: Libra Season Comes To An End
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 22, 2026. Libra season is coming to an end on Thursday, as the Sun prepares to move into Scorpio.
This deep and transformative water sign doesn’t just rule your emotions, but also your desire to find true love. While Libra season was about balance and partnerships, Scorpio season is about connecting on a soul level. Embrace the depth and meaning this time brings, as it will help you choose your fate and find the love that's destined for you.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Thursday, October 22, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Let yourself believe in all that love can be, Aries. Don’t worry about keeping your feet on the ground on Thursday, as the Sun prepares to move into Scorpio. Instead, let your soul get carried away.
Ask your guides or tarot cards for guidance. Sit and share your most intimate desires with that special person. Don’t be afraid of falling into a love that has no end.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Do something about it, Taurus. Great love doesn’t always just find you. Sometimes, you must be the one to go out and find it.
On Thursday, be willing to shake up your routine. Do something that signals to the universe that you are open to a new kind of love, and don’t hesitate to make the first move. You are on the verge of an exciting new romance, but you must take action.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You are normally one of the most social and talkative zodiac signs, Gemini. But this time is about you returning to your inner self.
You might feel quieter or more contemplative during Scorpio season. Pay attention to how you feel on Thursday, and validate your needs. This is also a perfect time to work through any lingering issues or challenges in your relationship as you commit to a new and healthier connection.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Let yourself start over, dear Cancer. As the Sun leaves Libra for Scorpio, you have the chance to start a new and serious relationship. This season also helps you see the difference between a toxic love and one that actually possesses the depth you’ve been searching for.
You may need to give someone a chance who you wouldn’t have in the past. Looking past the surface and into the soul will be important on Thursday and in the weeks ahead.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It's up to you to save this, dear Leo. Anything is possible during Scorpio season, but you will need to step up. On Thursday, be sure your words and actions align so you can do whatever it takes to save your relationship and maybe even your family.
Just because you made mistakes in the past doesn’t mean this situation is doomed. Yet, you need to start showing those in your life just how much they mean to you.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Take time to sort through any confusion, Virgo. On Thursday, you must finally address some confusion or hurt feelings in your life. This may involve a relationship in which you are together for different reasons, or there is a discrepancy in your feelings.
Don’t worry about how this person will take your truth. Just allow yourself to be honest. You can’t avoid the truth any longer, so it’s better to sort through it all.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Spoil yourself, Libra. Regardless of your romantic status, this season is all about you setting the bar for how you want to be loved.
This might mean redoing your bedroom or booking that spa appointment. You could plan that trip you’ve always wanted or simply take yourself out to dinner and validate your own feelings. Talk to yourself with love and buy yourself flowers. Let October 22 be the start of a love affair with yourself.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You are ready to begin anew, Scorpio. The Sun is moving out of Libra and into your sign, and you can finally see the path opening up in front of you. Even if it doesn’t seem like there is romance to be found, it doesn't mean that you won’t end up finding it.
Answer the call of your soul on Thursday. Take a chance on your dreams and leave your past behind. As you begin your zodiac season and solar return, this is the new beginning you’ve worked hard to establish.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Surprise yourself, Sagittarius. Scorpio season activates your intuition and connection with the spirit in a way that no other time of the year does. And it’s in perfect timing, because this is when you want to take a chance.
Surprise yourself with the risks that you allow yourself to take. Don’t worry about logic or what the outcome will ultimately be. On Thursday, instead of trying to play safely by the rules, see just how amazing life can really be.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Make time for the people who are there for you, Capricorn. While you always seem to be focusing on your career, Scorpio season shifts your priorities. This may not feel easy, at least once Venus retrograde moves back into Libra on October 24. But it is part of what you’re meant to do during this time.
Prioritizing the people you care about, including a partner, isn’t just about them. It's also about knowing you deserve to connect and have fun. You deserve to enjoy a life outside of work too.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Get ready to take action, Aquarius. Scorpio energy governs what you need to feel good. This time often brings significant and positive changes to your career, but it’s also about knowing what you truly need in life.
With the Sun moving into this water sign, you are encouraged to take action towards creating the life that you want to live. Change your job and set better boundaries. Say yes to love, as there is no limit to what you can create.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You don’t need to be afraid, dearest Pisces. Scorpio season brings opportunities for abundance and new love into your life. With Mercury and Venus still in retrograde, this may also bring some second chances
Don’t let fear guide your decisions. On Thursday, choose from the heart and know that not all opportunities will stick around for when you feel ready.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.content:encoded:
In this episode of Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing, Motley Fool personal finance expert Robert Brokamp and Motley Fool employee Amanda Kish discuss:
- Maxing out tax-advantaged savings accounts.
- Tax-loss harvesting.
- Donating appreciated stock and new rules for deducting charitable contributions for 2026.
- Getting your withholdings right to avoid penalties.
- Roth conversions.
To catch full episodes of all The Motley Fool's free podcasts, check out our podcast center. When you're ready to invest, check out this top 10 list of stocks to buy.
A full transcript is below.
This podcast was recorded on Oct. 3, 2026.
Robert Brokamp: What you can do to lower your tax bill for 2026, this week on the Saturday Personal Finance Edition of the Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing Podcast. I'm Robert Brokamp, and it's the first Saturday of the month, so it's time for the next installment of the 2026 Financial Planning challenge, which we're calling a year well planned. Speaking of the year, it’s now three-fourths over, making now a good time to do some fourth-quarter tax planning and make sure you are paying as much as you’re supposed to, but not a penny more. Here to answer eight questions that will help you optimize your taxes for 2026 is my Foolish colleague, Amanda Kish. Amanda, thanks for joining us again.
Amanda Kish: Thank you so much. I'm glad to be back.
Robert Brokamp: I will ask each of the questions. Amanda will explain why the question is important, and then I may add a thought or two. Let’s start with Question No. 1, which is: Are you on track to max out or at least meaningfully increase your tax-advantaged retirement contributions this year?
Amanda Kish: Great place to start. That is important because assuming that you're making pretax contributions, every dollar that you put into a 401(k), 403(b), or traditional IRA is $1 that doesn't get taxed this year. Just as a refresher for 2026, the 401(k) and 403(b) contribution limit is $24,500 with an additional $8,000 catchup if you are 50 or older. Then if you're between the ages of 60 to 63, there's an even higher super catch-up limit to be aware of. Then for IRAs, the annual contribution limit is $7,500 or $8,600 with the catch-up. If you have been contributing a flat percentage since January on autopilot, like most of us, now is really the time to actually run the math. Pull up your last few pay stubs, see what you've contributed year to date, and then compare that against the annual limit. If you've got the cash flow to do it, you can often increase your contribution percentage for just the last few paychecks of the year to close that gap. Some employers will also let you make a true catch-up lump-sum contribution before Dec. 31, so that is worth checking with your plan administrator or HR to see if that's possible.
Then, if you’re self-employed, of course, this question gets even more interesting because if you’ve got a SEP IRA, solo 401 (k), those have much higher limits. Let’s go into the tens of thousands of dollars, and the deadline for funding some of those extends past year-end and into your tax filing deadline. Ultimately, no matter what kind of plan you have, it's worth a quick check toward the end of the year just to make sure that you're on track to max out those contributions if possible.
Robert Brokamp: I'll extend this to a couple of other tax advantage accounts. Of course, there's the health savings account, which any contribution will lower taxable income this year. Then I'll also point out 529 college savings accounts, which don't really have an annual limit and a deadline per se, but most states offer a deduction on the state tax return for contributions to a 529. Every state has their own rules, so make sure you look into your state's rules. But if you want to take that, it does have to go in before the end of the year. If you want to take a distribution from your 529 for any qualifying expenses, you need to take that in the year that you incurred the cost. Question No. 2, have you reviewed your taxable accounts for tax loss harvesting opportunities this year?
Amanda Kish: Tax loss harvesting is the process of selling an investment. And again, this only applies to taxable accounts: selling an investment that is currently worth less than what you paid for in order to realize that loss for tax purposes. That loss can then offset capital gains that you've realized elsewhere in your portfolio this year. Then if those losses exceed the gains after everything's all totaled up, up to $3,000 of that excess can offset ordinary income such as your salary. Now anything beyond that $3,000 can then carry forward to future years indefinitely.
Tax loss harvesting matters most, I think, for people who are holding stocks or funds that have had a rough year, but it is also relevant if you have rebalanced a taxable account and realized gains, let's say earlier in 2026, as those gains might now have an offsetting loss sitting somewhere else in the portfolio. Of course, if we're talking about tax loss harvesting, I have to throw in there, the important thing that everyone needs to keep in mind here is the wash sale rule. If you sell a security at a loss and then you buy the same security or something that the IRS considers substantially identical within 30 days, either before or after the sale, that loss then gets disallowed for tax purposes. That’s a 61-day window that can trip people up from time to time, especially with ETFs or exchange-traded funds because two similar-sounding funds may be considered to be substantially identical, sometimes even if they are from different providers. If you do want to stay invested in that same general asset class after harvesting a loss, look for a similar but not identical fund to swap into temporarily.
Robert Brokamp: I will add that tax loss harvesting isn't just for stocks and funds; it really can be just about for any type of investment, including bonds which have had a rough year. In fact, the Vanguard Total Bond ETF, which is the biggest bond ETF in the world, is currently around $70 a share, so it's well below its all-time high of almost $90 a share set in 2020. You could do some tax loss harvesting with your bonds as well. Amanda talked about a couple of ways to violate the wash sale rule, and I want to highlight a few others. First of all, you can't buy that investment back during that 61-day window, and neither can your spouse. You can't do it in another account. You can't take the loss in your brokerage account and buy it in your IRA or 401(k) or your spouse do it. One way that people accidentally buy shares of the investment is through automatic dividend reinvestment if they hold it in some other place. That's something to keep in mind. Then one final thing to keep in mind is that there are lots of rules around options as well. You can't buy a call option on the investment, and there's some other options strategies that could violate the wash sale rule. make sure you know all of those.
Robert Brokamp: Let's move on to question number 3. Do you know whether your bonds, REITS, REITS being real estate investment trust, and other income-heavy holdings sit in the account type that makes sense tax wise?
Amanda Kish: Yes, this consideration is something called asset location, which is different from asset allocation. Allocation is about what percentage of your portfolio is in stocks versus bonds versus other categories. Asset location is about which account each of those pieces lives in. Taxable brokerage account, your traditional IRA, your Roth IRA, and all of these pieces and where you have your investments can meaningfully change your after-tax return without changing your actual investment mix at all. Brokamp, you mentioned bonds, REITS, other holdings like that that tend to generate a lot of ordinary income. Those get taxed at your regular income tax rate every single year. That's even if you never sell them, you never touch the cash, that income is going to show up on your 1099. If those holdings are sitting in a taxable brokerage account, you're paying tax on that income annually, year after year.
Now move the same holdings into a traditional IRA or 401K, and that income compounds tax deferred until you eventually withdraw it. Now, meanwhile, if we consider your more typically tax-efficient holdings, so these are things like broad market index funds that very rarely distribute large cap gains or individual stocks you may be holding long term, those tend to do relatively little damage sitting in a taxable account because you're not paying tax on that unrealized depreciation. The exercise here is simple. Pull up your account statements across all of your accounts, taxable, traditional and Roth, and look at what's actually sitting where. So if, for example, your bond funds are concentrated in the taxable account, and let's say your growth stocks are concentrated in the IRA, you may be able to swap the two around so long as you're not triggering any kind of unnecessary capital gains taxes to do that.
Robert Brokamp: I agree that most income-generating investments should likely be in your traditional IRA. I’ll just point out, though, that some bonds do have built-in tax advantages that you may lose once they’re in a retirement account. Municipal bonds, for example, could be completely tax-free, state and federal, if you do it right. Generally, you probably want to have those outside of the IRA. Treasuries are taxable at the federal level, but not state level. It probably still makes sense to keep them in your traditional IRA. I just want to point that out. Again, I think most experts would agree with putting the bonds in the traditional IRA.
The Roth is a little different. That's the tax-free account. It's the one you want to grow the most. Really, you would use that account for your highest-returning assets. Now, those are stocks, of course. Ideally, hopefully, you could choose what stocks you think will have the highest returns; you would put them in your Roth. Of course, it's not easy to do, but it's definitely a way to think about it and you would generally not hold bonds or cash in a Roth account. Let's move on to question number 4. If you give to charity, have you looked at giving appreciated stock or using a donor-advised fund instead of writing a check?
Amanda Kish: Yes. If you're planning to donate to charity, anyways, gifting appreciated stock that you've held for more than a year may be more efficient than giving cash. When you donate stock directly, you avoid paying capital gains tax on that appreciation entirely, and then you still get to deduct the full fair market value of the stock at the time of the gift, not just what you originally paid for it. Conversely, writing a check certainly gets you that deduction, but you do miss the CAP gain savings because you never had a taxable event to begin with. A donor-advised fund then takes that a step further. Here you contribute a lump sum. That can be cash, stock or other assets into the fund in one tax year, and then you take that full deduction immediately, even though the money doesn't need to go to any specific charity right away. Then from there, you can distribute grants to charities over the following years on your own timeline.
This is something that can be especially useful if you’re having an unusually high income year and you want to bunch several years’ worth of that planned giving into this year to maximize the deduction against this year’s income rather than spreading those smaller deductions across future years when your tax bracket might be lower. One more wrinkle worth mentioning: if you take the standard deduction most years, if you bunch several years of giving into a donor-advised fund in one year, that may be what pushes you over the threshold to itemize that year, which is where really a lot of the tax benefit of charitable giving actually gets unlocked.
Robert Brokamp: Yeah, I'll build on that by pointing out that to deduct the donation of appreciated stock, you do have to itemize. There's a limit on how much you can deduct in any single year for really any charitable deduction with excess amounts carried forward up to five years. But even if you can't take the deduction, you're still getting the tax benefit by donating appreciated shares because you're passing that capital gain onto the charity and they don't care because they're tax exempt. Then with the cash you would have donated to the charity, you can just buy back the stock immediately. You don't have to wait 30 days or anything like that, and you've set yourself to a higher cost basis. In my opinion, if you regularly give to charity, there's almost no reason not to donate appreciated shares rather than donate cash. It says we're talking about deduction, I do want to highlight two new rules that took effect this year. You can deduct up to $1,000 of charitable donations, $2,000 for married couples filing jointly without having to itemize.
But the money does have to go to a qualified 501(c)3 organization. Any donations to a donor-advised fund or private foundation is not eligible for this other deduction. Now, for those who do itemize, you're not going to be able to take quite the deduction you have in previous years because starting this year, only charitable deductions in excess of 0.5% of your adjusted gross income will be deductible for those who itemize. For example, if your AGI is $150,000, you'll only be able to deduct contributions in excess of $750. Let's move on to question number 5. Are you confident your withholding or estimated payments will avoid a surprise tax bill or penalty next April?
Amanda Kish: Yes. Unfortunately, the IRS generally expects you to pay tax on your income as you earn it throughout the year, and not all at once when you file annually. If you've had any kind of life change in 2026 and this could be a bonus that you've received, a new job, a home sale, freelance or 1099 income, a large capital gain from selling investments, there's a real chance that your withholding hasn't kept pace with what you'll actually owe. Here, it's important to keep in mind the safe harbor rule. What that means is that generally, you can avoid an underpayment penalty if you've paid through a combination of withholding and estimated payments, at least 90% of this year's tax liability or 100% of last year's liability. Although it's a caveat that increases to 110% if your prior-year income was above $150,000.
If you're not sure where you stand with your current withholdings, the IRS does have a free withholding estimator tool or this is something that your tax preparer, if you use such an individual can run a projection based on your income year to date. If it does look that you're behind, you basically have two levers at your disposal. You can increase withholding from your paycheck for the remaining months of the year, which the IRS will treat as if it were paid evenly throughout the year, even if it's a little bit more concentrated in Q4, or the other options to make an estimated quarterly payment directly. That fourth estimated payment deadline for 2026 is January 15th of 2027. You do still have time to true that up even after year end.
Robert Brokamp: I'll just add that there could be a benefit to doing this to making sure that you are paying enough taxes because if you experience some change, maybe your income was lower or you had something happen that will qualify you for a tax credit or deduction, it could be you're overpaying taxes. I know everyone loves to get a refund when they file their taxes, but the truth is you're basically losing the use of that money. It could be in your bank account earning interest, it could be in your retirement accounts growing. You definitely don't want to overpay if you can help it. I’ll just re-emphasize that if you don’t pay enough and you don’t fall under those safe harbors, you are going to pay a penalty and maybe interest. You definitely want to make sure that you get this as close to right as possible. Let's move on to question number 6, which is, if you're subject to required minimum distributions, have you planned this year's amount and whether a QCD makes sense?
Amanda Kish: If you are 73 years or older—or, Bro, I've sometimes heard you say 73 years or wiser—the IRS requires you to withdraw a minimum amount from your traditional retirement accounts every year. That's your required minimum distribution or RMD. That amount is calculated based on your account balance as of December 31st of the prior year. To calculate the 2026 R&D, you would look at the December 31st, 2025 balance, and that is divided by a life expectancy factor from IRS tables. If you miss the deadline or you withdraw less than required, the penalty can be pretty steep. That's about 25% of the shortfall, although that can be reduced to 10% if this is something that is corrected promptly. Keeping that in mind, here's something to consider. If you are charitably inclined, a QCD or qualified charitable distribution, lets you direct some or all of your RMD, that's up to $111,000 in 2026, straight from your IRA to a qualifying charity.
Now, that amount counts towards satisfying your RMD, but it does not count as taxable income. You compare that to taking the RMD yourself and then donating the cash afterward, where that distribution is going to show up as income first, and then the charitable deduction only helps you if you itemize. A QCD sidesteps that entirely and it's one of the few moves in the tax code where giving money away can directly lower your reported income, not just your deduction. But just as a note, the mechanics here do matter how you carry that QCD out. QCD has to go directly from the custodian to the charity. If that money touches your hands first, it no longer qualifies. If this is something you're thinking about, it's worth setting up with your custodian well before year end rather than waiting till the final days of December.
Robert Brokamp: I'll just highlight that what might happen is sometimes your custodian will send you the check, and you have to hand-deliver it to the charity. That's OK as long as the check is made out to the charity and not to you. That's just another aspect about doing the QCD. Getting back to RMDs, one thing to know is, if you're married, you have to calculate them separately from your separate accounts. You can't calculate the RMD and then just take it from one spouse's account or the other. However, if you personally individually have multiple IRAs, you have to calculate the RMD for each account, but it only has to be taken out of one IRA. 401(k)s are different. If you have multiple 401(k)s, you have to take the RMD from each. Then you might also have to take an RMD from an inherited account. That's a complicated topic. It depends on your relationship to the person who you inherited the account from and your age and various other criteria, but just know that you might be in a situation where you have to take an RMD from an inherited account.
ADVERTISEMENT: Spotify, it's Jay Sheri. Are you one of those media strategy people scrolling through spreadsheets, searching for an audience that pays twice as much attention to your ads than they do on social? Let me introduce you to fans. They're here with me on Spotify. Trust me, I know fans. They don't skip, they stay for hours. They don't move on, they manifest. They're not a demographic group. They're fans.
Robert Brokamp: Moving on to question number 7. Do you know which federal tax bracket you're likely to land in this year and whether that changes any moves worth making before year-end?
Amanda Kish: Your marginal tax bracket is really the thread that runs through almost every other tax strategy that we're talking about today. It determines how much Roth conversion will actually cost you, whether harvesting a gain versus a loss makes more sense, how valuable a charitable deduction is, whether extra retirement contribution is worth more to you now or might be worth more taken as income in a different year. The reason this deserves its own dedicated check is that a lot of people are estimating their bracket based on a typical year when 2026 might not have been typical for you. If there was something like a bonus, a promotion, layoff, a severance pay, a big capital gain from selling a business or a home, spouse, starting or stopping work, any of these things can shift you into a different bracket than you might assume from habit and from what has been true for you in the past.
These federal brackets are also adjusted annually for inflation. Even without any big life changes, the income level at what you cross into that next tax bracket has moved from last year. The practical step here is to pull together a rough estimate of your total taxable income for 2026. That includes wages, investment income, any one off events sometime before the year closes so that you're acting on real numbers rather than a guess. That single number is what makes questions like the Roth conversion or charitable bunching decisions answerable with any real confidence.
Robert Brokamp: You can use online tools to help you with these calculations. Most of the online tax prep providers also provide free calculators for folks, so, like TaxAct, H&R Block, Intuit. You'll find other calculators at other places like dinkytown.net has a 1040 calculator. I would say, actually, that's probably my favorite. It's the most intuitive to use. Just make sure that if you're going to use these tools that you choose 2026, sometimes the default is 2025. In some cases, they haven't come out with the 2026 tool yet, so you definitely want to use one that can calculate your tax bill for 2026. I would not use them and base my actual tax return on it. I think they're best used as getting a rough idea of what the consequences could be based on certain decisions such as, like Amanda said, doing a Roth conversion or contributing to a traditional account versus Roth, those types. What's the value of any kind of deduction right now? It can give you a rough idea, put some numbers to it and if you put it in the information correctly, it will give you an idea of what your tax bracket will be this year. Let's move on to our final question. Does a Roth conversion make sense for your situation?
Amanda Kish: This is a good one. A Roth conversion means moving money from a traditional IRA or 401K into a Roth account and paying that ordinary income tax on the converted amount in the year which you do it. In exchange, that money grows tax free from that point forward, qualified withdrawals and retirement are also tax free. There's no RMDs on the Roth side either, which can matter for estate planning as well as your own retirement income. The typical scenario where Roth conversion makes sense is in if you are in a lower income year, if you are between jobs in your early retirement before Social Security or pension income starts or any year where your taxable income is temporarily depressed relative to your normal working years. Converting while you're in that lower bracket means that you're paying tax on that money at a cheaper rate than you likely would either during your peak earning years or later in your retirement once RMDs and Social Security kick in and push your retirement income back up. That's not always universally the right move, though.
A couple of things to consider. You need enough cash outside the retirement account to pay the tax bill on the conversion. Using the IRA itself to pay for that tax really defeats a lot of the purpose of the exercise. Then equally important, converting a large amount can push you into a higher bracket for that year. You have to run the numbers, and it may make more sense to then do that conversion in smaller, more deliberate slices over several years rather than all at once. That's exactly where that bracket estimate from earlier becomes essential. Converting an amount that fills up your current bracket without spilling into the next one is usually as a sweet spot and a good target to aim for.
Robert Brokamp: I'll just point out that doing a Roth conversion doesn't just increase your tax bill itself. It increases your adjusted gross income, and there's a lot of things in your finances that are based on your adjusted gross income, such as your eligibility to take some deductions and credits, make Roth IRA contributions, maybe it could affect you if you're on an income-based student loan repayment plan, could affect how much you pay for premiums through the Affordable Care Act or through Medicare. You definitely want to have an idea of the whole picture when you're doing these Roth conversions. Amanda, what are your final thoughts when it comes to tightening up your taxes for 2026?
Amanda Kish: Thank you, Brokamp. I would say that I think for a lot of us, taxes are usually treated like an April problem. But the thing to keep in mind is that by April, most of your options are already gone, and you're basically just reporting what has already happened. If we're talking about December and where we currently are October, November, and December—that's a different picture. Every one of these tax strategies that we've talked about represents a decision that you can still make for 2026 with weeks to actually implement it. Whether that is contributing more to your retirement accounts, harvesting a loss, gifting stock instead of cash, converting to a Roth, what have you. You don't need to act on all of these that we've talked about, but even identifying two or three that genuinely apply to your situation and following through before December 31st can make a real difference in what you own next spring.
Robert Brokamp: I'll add as the final note for me that everything we've talked about here is true for federal taxes, but state taxes can be different. In most situations, your state tax situation is going to be similar, but there are a lot of one offs. For example, we talked about QCDs being excluded from your income. That's actually not the case in New Jersey. New Jersey doesn't exclude a QCD from your income. There are other little things like that. Like if you have leftover money in your 529, you can transfer it to a Roth IRA. If you do it right, it's a tax free transfer on the federal level, but California, it's not tax free. Just understand what the rules are for your state. With that, that's the end of our show. I want to thank Amanda for joining us once again, and thanks to Bart Shannon, the engineer for this episode.
As always, people on the program may have interest in the investments they talk about, and The Motley Fool may have formal recommendations for or against. Don't buy or sell investments based solely on what you hear. All personal finance content follows Motley Fool Editorial standards and is not approved by advertisers. Advertisements are sponsored content and provided for informational purposes only. See our full advertising disclosure; please check out our show notes. I'm Robert Brokamp. Fool on, everybody.

Love Horoscope Today, October 22, 2026
October 22, 2026 brings positive, stable love energy. Taurus, Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Capricorn enjoy romantic moments and deeper connections.
Love Horoscope Today, October 22, 2026: In terms of love relationships, today will bring generally positive and stable energy for most zodiac signs. Taurus, Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Capricorn will enjoy romantic moments, deepening relationships, and opportunities to move forward in relationships, even towards marriage.
Aries, Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius, and Pisces will go through a more neutral or balanced phase, with an emphasis on communication, emotional understanding, and planning for the future. Overall, this day is favorable for open conversations, making informed decisions, and strengthening love relationships.
Aries Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today will be a normal day for you. There will be nothing special in your love life. There will be good coordination between you and your partner. You will get a chance to spend a good time with your love. But you have to control your anger. You should respect your partner and try to understand his/her feelings.
Taurus Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that this day is going to be very good for Taurus people in terms of love and affection. Your partner will be ready to plan the future with you. You can take your relationship a step forward, which will give you a chance to make an important decision related to your marriage. Those who have recently gotten married can plan to go on a trip with their partner.
Gemini Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that Gemini people, today is going to be a very good day for you. Today, your love life will be very romantic. Today, someone can propose to you, and you will be confused about what to do. But you have to listen to your heart and do what feels right. Do not rush into any relationship; you have to be patient.
Cancer Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today your love life will be normal. There may be a lack of activities in your married life. There may also be a lack of mutual coordination. You may need to reduce the distance between you by talking to your partner. Today is a good day for those who want to get married. There can be a new beginning in your life.
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today is a normal day for you. There will be no special change in your love life. You can work to strengthen your relationship with your partner. You will get time to express your love in new ways. This can be a time to talk deeply about your relationship, which will give you a chance to understand your partner more. You will get time to share your feelings with your partner, which will deepen your relationship.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope is very good for Virgo people. Today, there will be happiness and love in your married life. You will feel as if the flower of love has bloomed in your life. Today you will spend very romantic and sweet moments with your boyfriend/girlfriend. This day will be full of love for you, and you will get love in return.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today will be a very good day emotionally for Libra people. Today, your love and relationship situation will be very good. You can share your plans with your partner and take your relationship with each other a step forward. Today can be the day for you to make important decisions related to your marriage. Those who have recently gotten married can plan a trip.
Scorpio Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s love horoscope is good for Scorpio people. There is not going to be any special change in your love life. Your relationship will be a little distant from you, and you will need to focus on your relationships. You have to talk to your partner and reduce the distance between you. Today is a very good day for those who are going to get married. A new chapter can start in your life.
Sagittarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope will be special for your zodiac signs. Today, there will be happiness and love in your married life. You will feel that love has blossomed in your life. This time will be very romantic for you, and you may get many love proposals. If you are single, then today you may get a chance to go on a romantic date with someone special. This time will be full of love for loving couples, and you will also get love in return.
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today is likely to be a good day for you. Your love life is ready to take you to a new level today. There is a possibility of a deep relationship between you and your love. You can share your feelings with your partner and deepen your relationship with them. Today, there can be talks of trust and hope between you and your partner, which can make your relationship even stronger.
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, the horoscope of love and affection is absolutely normal for you. You can make plans with your partner. You can take your relationship forward, and today you can make some important decisions related to your marriage. Those who are recently married can plan to go on a trip.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope shows that the state of your love relationship is normal. There are no new ups and downs in your relationship, but it is also true that your love still rules the hearts. Today, you will get a chance to plan the future with your partner. Today, you can take your relationship a step forward, which will increase the depth and trust in your relationship. Today, you can make an important decision related to your love, like planning a wedding.
Quick Answers
According to the love horoscope for October 22, 2026, Taurus, Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Capricorn will enjoy romantic moments, deeper relationships, and opportunities to move forward toward marriage.

But underneath so much of that is really a deeper question. In our families, do we feel safe and known and loved and connected to the people that are closest to us? And that question takes us into the world of science and attachment theory. Now, for those of you who are not familiar, attachment theory emerged from developmental and psychological research that examines how our earliest relationships, particularly relationships with our primary caregivers as we're born and grow through childhood. How do those Relationship shape our expectations about safety and trust and connection in relationships. Now, over time, researchers have identified patterns of attachment that influence how people respond to closeness, how they respond to conflict, how they respond to rejection and separation and vulnerability. And while attachment theory is a psychological framework rather than a biblical doctrine, it. It raises some profoundly important questions for Christian families. That's what we're going to look about. What does scripture have to say about the human need for connection and security and belonging and redemption? Our guest today is not a stranger to the show. We welcome back Dr. Ryan Rush. He is pastor of Kingsland Baptist Church in Katy, Texas. And we're going to be really thoughtful about looking at it from both sides. Ryan, so glad to have you back here. Thank you so much for joining us, Jessica.
Dr. Ryan Rush It's always a pleasure to be on. And when you sent out the request that we talk about this, I got really excited. So I, look forward to this conversation.
Dr. Jessica Peck Me, too. I'm telling you, I was taking notes so fast while you were talking, my paper was catching fire because I'm like, yes, yes, and amen. So let's start at the beginning. And so from our earliest days, we're asking those questions and receiving the answers through the cues that we get from our parents. And so here's what's especially interesting about attachment, I think in light of the family and in light of so many narratives in scripture, but also just everyday life, is that we don't leave those lessons behind when we turn 18. It's not just something that we connect with our parents over. It impacts all of our other relationships, how we lead, how we parent later on.
Dr. Jessica Peck You know, when you're talking, I'm thinking of the proverbial, you know, therapy couch and, and the therapist is taking notes and it's like it all goes back to my mother. We all recognize this. Anybody who's ever dropped a child off at the nursery has seen attachment wound. When a child cries and longs for mom or dad in that moment. So we see that. Dr. Jessica Peck I'm gonna hold you right there, Dr. Rush. Dr. Ryan Rush Sure. Thanks, Jessica. So if anxious attachment is reduced to a message of I'm not worthy, you could imagine that avoidant attachment is really reduced to the point, they're not able. And now we know through the science of neuroplasticity, your mind can change. Like you can literally change your belief system in this regard and bring it back to healthy relationships.
Dr. Jessica Peck And these, the ways that we process this, the attachment that we have, the ways that we see our parent, we know it does reflect the way that we view God. So how do we, how do we have a balance here that's healthy, Ryan how do we recognize the ways that attachment woundedness may impact us while not sitting there and ah, just like blaming people or, or just like you know, saying our parents were terrible. Like, how do we recognize that and move forward in a hopeful way?
Dr. Ryan Rush Yes, it's so important, Jessica, because explanation is not the same thing as excuse. Dr. Jessica Peck And you know, when we think about the ways that we respond in attachment, often, you know, we think that our way of seeing the world is the best way, is the normal way. item.title: [The Brussels Times] For Brussels activists, speed dating is about more than finding love
item.dc:creator: The Brussels Times
item.description: Dating as an activist can be difficult in Brussels. It’s a small, professional bubble where potential dates could share mutual friends or be current or former colleagues. If your political views are important to you, dating apps and singles nights don’t make it any easier when there’s a growing political polarisation between the left and right. “In the end, you spend most of your time just trying to filter out hundreds of people that you don’t have shared values with,” Cass Heldon, the organiser
item.content:encoded:
Dating as an activist can be difficult in Brussels. It’s a small, professional bubble where potential dates could share mutual friends or be current or former colleagues.
If your political views are important to you, dating apps and singles nights don’t make it any easier when there’s a growing political polarisation between the left and right.
“In the end, you spend most of your time just trying to filter out hundreds of people that you don’t have shared values with,” Cass Heldon, the organiser of the third Speed Dating for Activists event, told the Brussels Times.
“And it’s not to say that you can never date beyond your political spectrum, but it’s such a key part of your identity.”
Speed dating for activists has been met with high demand in Brussels. The event is organised by the Green Fix, a six-volunteer climate initiative that began as a newsletter by Heldon with over 5,500 subscribers on Substack. It describes itself as “your bullshit-free roundup of climate justice, feminist and decolonial news and opportunities in Europe and beyond.”
Previous speed-dating editions had long wait lists, and attendance is capped at 50 participants. Tickets sold out last week, though the wait list was again left open, and the event will take place at an undisclosed bar in the Brussels city centre to prevent any unwanted crashers.
Dating in the age of political polarisation
However, the event has faced criticism. Heldon described getting comments online, typically from what she described as "angry men," arguing that the events are exclusionary and contribute to growing political polarisation and division between the left and the right.
“Of course, we do need a lot of dialogue across the political spectrum and we do see governments and corporations kind of propelling this polarisation,” Heldon said.
While she acknowledged the need to break down these barriers, she argued that not every aspect of life needs to be devoted to bridging a political divide. “And when it comes to dating and personal relationships,” Heldon said, “it really matters what your partner thinks about your views, your values.”
Third time's the charm
The Brussels Times spoke with Louis, a 29-year-old from Brussels who works in a shelter for victims of domestic violence and attended the previous speed-dating events. Though none of his matches led to romantic relationships, for Louis, the event was still a success.
Even if they don’t find love, activist speed dating is a way for people in Brussels' activist and NGO circles to meet outside their professional networks. For an introvert like Louis, these events can make future networking and building community easier.
“I was like, okay, I'm not going to date those people,” he said, “but I know I'm going to meet them at some events afterwards, and it would be nice to see them again and to have discussions.”
Success stories
When asked about any success stories, Heldon admitted that she couldn’t name any long-term relationships that arose from previous events. “You know, I’m not entirely sure because they don’t tell me,” she said. “They should keep me in CC.”
However, there were matches who continued to go on several dates, and there are previous participants who didn’t register for the third event because they’re now in relationships. Even if it wasn’t because of the speed-dating event, Heldon said, she would like to think it was a step in their journey.
However, new friendships have certainly been formed, and attendees continue to go to other events the Green Fix hosts, “so I count that as a success,” she said.
And for the speed-dating events overall? She said they've been a success.
“I think, you know, when you go to a speed dating, the success isn't necessarily in whether you find someone that you fall in love with and stay together forever. The success is whether you had a good time and whether you hung out with good people.”

item.content:encoded:
Minka Kelly Shares Cryptic Quote About Moving On From a Soulmate After Dan Reynolds Breakup
Minka Kelly is speaking out in a cryptic post following her recent breakup.
The 46-year-old Ransom Canyon actress and musician Dan Reynolds were revealed earlier this month to have split up “recently” after four years of dating.
Two weeks after their breakup was reported, Minka took to Instagram to share a photo dump, and the last slide featured a quote about soulmates.
“Soulmates, or partners of destiny, can be people that come into your life and change your life. And ideally, it’s not about holding on to it, but understanding what they brought into your life – what did you learn and how did you change? It’s about seeing these people and these situations as a gift, as steps in your own personal development,” the quote reads.
Last summer, Minka opened up about how Dan “healed wounds” in her that “he did not inflict.”
“His benevolence, his priorities, his values, and his honesty are all rooted in love. And as a result, we all feel safe and at ease in his orbit,” she added at the time. “Thank you for loving me. Thank you for blessing my life in ways I never thought possible – but always dreamed of.”
Minka sharing a quote about soulmates comes on the heels of Dan being photographed hanging out with Chantel Jeffries last week.
If you missed it, find out more about Minka Kelly‘s dating history.
Posted To:Minka Kelly

item.content:encoded:
Lioness Star Thad Luckinbill Played Kaley Cuoco's Boyfriend On A Hit Sitcom
Long before Thad Luckinbill stepped into the role of Kyle on "Lioness," he played Kaley Cuoco's boyfriend on a hit sitcom. We're talking about Luckenbill's role as Donny Doyle on "8 Simple Rules," which was originally titled "8 Simple Rules ... for Dating My Teenage Daughter." Donny played the romantic interest of Cuoco's character, Bridget Hennessy.
Luckinbill's first appearance on "8 Simple Rules" (one of Cuoco's best TV shows) was Season 1, Episode 26, titled "The Doyle Wedding." The episode revolves around the Hennessy family — led by Paul Hennessy (John Ritter) — attending a wedding of their neighbors, the Doyles. It also serves as the very beginning of Bridget's romantic spark with Donny. Although she first used to think Donny was a little bit of a dork, she sees him in a new light during the ep.
Luckinbill's last appearance was Season 2, Episode 3, titled "Donny Goes AWOL" — and a lot of big things happen in between. In addition to Donny returning to the Naval Academy, Bridget now has another romantic interest to juggle. She also uses a video postcard set up by Donny's family to break up with him, leading to drama. "Donny Goes AWOL" is notable most of all because it served as Ritter's last appearance before his tragic, untimely death.
Thad Luckinbill also dated Kaley Cuoco
Thad Luckinbill and Kaley Cuoco didn't just play sweethearts on TV — they also dated in real life. According to Us Weekly, they were romantically linked in 2002. That said, not much is known about their relationship, or the reason why it ultimately ended. There are a few press photos of the pair posing together on red carpets, and not much else.
As of 2026, both Cuoco and Luckinbill are worlds away from their early '00s romance. Luckinbill, for his part, has been married to Amelia Heinle, his "The Young and the Restless" co-star, since 2007. They have two children. And although Luckinbill initiated divorce proceedings in 2017, they've since reconciled and are enjoying marital bliss, per Hello!.
Meanwhile, Cuoco is currently in a relationship with her fiancé, actor Tom Pelphrey. In October 2026, she gave birth to their second child together. "Philomena Carmine Bobby Pelphrey ... 10/12/26," Cuoco posted to Instagram. "There are no words to describe this feeling once again. What a blessing." She continued, "We are so grateful for the crazy wild up and down journey that brought us to our little Philo. Family officially complete. Time to bring Matilda's baby home! @tommypelphrey life exploded the minute we met, and the gifts keep coming."

item.title: [Athol Daily News] Speed dating-style session helps voters prep for nine ballot questions - Athol Daily News
item.dc:creator: Erin-Leigh Hoffman
item.description: GREENFIELD — Before going to the polls on Nov. 3, the League of Women Voters of Franklin County made sure voters got to know the nine ballot questions better during a speed dating-style information session. item.content:encoded:
GREENFIELD — Before going to the polls on Nov. 3, the League of Women Voters of Franklin County made sure voters got to know the nine ballot questions better during a speed dating-style information session.
Thursday’s event, hosted by the league and Greenfield Community College, saw volunteers provide information to the roughly 30 attendees about what it means to vote “yes” or “no,” and the arguments for and against each ballot question. While the League of Women Voters of Massachusetts has taken a stance on some of the questions, Thursday’s event was explicitly nonpartisan and informational only, according to Marie Gauthier, president of the League of Women Voters of Franklin County.
Tables were set up at GCC, acting as stations for all nine questions. Each round gave five minutes for the presenters to share their information and take questions before Gauthier rang cowbells to signal the transition.
This style of voter engagement is something that Gauthier said is not new for the league, which hosted an event called “Candi-dating Night” for voters to get to know candidates for the 2017 municipal elections in Greenfield. She added that it’s a “fun and interactive” way to learn.
“There are a lot of ballot question events, and I just wanted to do something that was more engaging and might get people out,” Gauthier said, noting that the program also helps members of the league learn about the questions.
According to Commonwealth Beacon, this year’s number of ballot questions is nearly record-breaking, as the 1994 election also had nine questions, the most in the state’s history. During that election, five of the nine questions were accepted by voters. If a MassINC Polling Group and CommonWealth Beacon poll from September ends up reflecting the results in November, eight of the nine questions would receive a “yes” vote, while Question 8, the recreational marijuana repeal, would be the single “no.”
The ballot questions will ask voters to tackle a range of themes in legislative accountability and personal liberties. Question 1 seeks to expand public records law to the Legislature and governor’s office. Question 8 asks to repeal recreational marijuana legalization. The format of primary elections is up for change in Question 3, along with tax reform in Question 5.
Gauthier said the hope is that even if attendees didn’t have their minds made up, they would “have the tools to make those decisions” by the end of the night.
The presenters used numerous sources in their research, Gauthier said, including CommonWealth Beacon and the Tufts University Center for State Policy Analysis.
At the tables, some presenters, like Nicola Shipman, used visual aids to help best describe the question they were presenting. Shipman was tasked with Question 7, known as the starter-home question.
Question 7 asks voters if they’d like to relax zoning regulations for single-family homes in areas with public water and sewer, which would streamline the permitting process for homes to be built on smaller lots.
With her posters in hand, one for “yes” and one for “no,” she detailed some of the key arguments for both sides while taking questions from those at the table. Some of the discussion for one group with Shipman was about the state movement toward encouraging creation of accessory dwelling units and if this question impacts those goals, or skepticism about the question’s relevance to western Massachusetts, whose communities are more spread out and with private water and sewer, compared to out east.
One of the voters in attendance, Patricia Stevenson of Shelburne, said she came to the speed-dating event with her mind made up on some of the questions, especially Question 9, which she plans to vote “yes” on. This question seeks to uphold the state’s 2024 gun law, and a “yes” vote would preserve that law, while a “no” vote would repeal it and bring the state back to pre-2024 gun regulations.
“I’m not opposed to people owning a gun, but those assault rifles should be banned as far as I’m concerned,” Stevenson said. “That’s a question I have no problem [with].”
Stevenson expressed her gratitude to the League of Women Voters of Franklin County for hosting the event and educating people.
“I think these ballot questions, the way they’re written, they’re very legal-like and it’s very hard for people to understand,” she said, “so I think having this really helped inform us to be a better voter.”
Those seeking to register to vote, check their voter registration status or access the red booklet from the Secretary of State’s Office detailing each of the nine ballot questions can visit sec.state.ma.us.

item.content:encoded:
*This content was translated by AI.View Original
Singer Soyou, a former member of the group SISTAR, shared her thoughts on cohabitation before marriage.
On the 19th, a video titled "Wow. You're really bad... | Soyou's Gossip Counseling Office 'Dating' Edition" was uploaded to Soyou's YouTube channel, "Soyouki."
Soyou spent time answering dating-related consultations sent in by her subscribers.
One subscriber shared their dilemma: "My boyfriend doesn't want to get married but wants to cohabit. He wants us to buy a home together, with him covering more of the cost and putting it in my name. I don't necessarily have to get married, so should we cohabit?"
In response, Soyou answered "Yes" without hesitation. Soyou said, "My boyfriend doesn't necessarily want to get married but wants to cohabit. He's paying more of the cost and putting it in my name—doesn't that show trust in me? Putting something in someone's name isn't easy. That is love."
Soyou added, "I am a proponent of cohabitation before marriage. There are already plus points to this. When you cohabit, you start to notice things about each other that are different, and there is also the fun of adjusting to those differences."
She continued, "If everything matches up, you end up getting married. You start thinking about marriage. But unless you dislike it when your boyfriend says, 'I will absolutely never get married. I will only cohabit,' I think it would be fine to cohabit. It's just dating for a long time and then moving in together, isn't it?"
Meanwhile, Soyou was born in September 1991 and is 35 years old by Korean age reckoning.

item.title: [New York Post] Dating apps getting desperate after ‘huge exodus’ of users deciding swiping won’t find them true love
item.dc:creator: Rikki Schlott
item.description: Dating apps aren’t delivering when it comes to finding a life partner. Single people are getting sick of swiping and abandoning dating apps in droves. That’s left the apps themselves desperately attempting to pivot amidst public backlash against their business premise — to the point of turning their backs on what made them successful in the first place. item.content:encoded:
Dating apps aren’t delivering when it comes to finding a life partner.
Single people are getting sick of swiping and abandoning dating apps in droves. That’s left the apps themselves desperately attempting to pivot amidst public backlash against their business premise — to the point of turning their backs on what made them successful in the first place.
Tinder, which made billions on the idea that people want to meet one another easily online, has taken to hosting in-person events. Bumble, which just made a deal to go private after years of its stock price tanking, has turned its back on its feminist mission, which used to require women to make the first move.
They’re trying anything to keep public trust, despite the fact three-quarters of Americans now believe dating apps have made romance feel transactional, per a 2026 Harris poll.
“[The apps] took the friction out of finding someone, but they also took the friction out of exiting, which means that you weren’t getting the depth of the experience,” Boston University business professor Marshall Van Alstyne told The Post.
“Initially, they were creating a lot of value to get folks on board [lots of people to potentially date], but now they’ve entered the extractive phase [charging subscription fees], and I think we’re now seeing the consequences.”
Business is looking pretty grim. Match Group, which owns Tinder, Match.com, OkCupid, and many other platforms, laid off 13% of their workforce last year, and Bumble 30% last June.
Bumble once had 12.5 million users who spent an average of 100 minutes a day swiping, but the app’s paying users fell by almost 17% year-over-year, and revenue dropped 15% during the same period.
Since going public in 2021, Bumble has lost 90% of its market value. The struggling app made a deal last Tuesday to go private for $1.3 billion — chump change compared with its $14 billion valuation at its initial public offering.
To New York City matchmaker Maria Avgitidis, part of the problem was going public in the first place — shifting obligations away from hooking users up to line shareholder pockets: “[The apps] had to find the equilibrium between providing a good product and also providing positive returns to their shareholders. And sometimes those things are not going to align.”
When Bumble was founded in 2014, it positioned itself as a feminist alternative to Tinder, led by a female CEO who put women in control by requiring them to send a message to their matches first.
As of August, the app had turned its back on that fundamental premise, and now anyone can send the first message — making it virtually indistinguishable from competitors.
Even the female founder and CEO herself, Whitney Wolfe Herd, is stepping aside to make room for two incoming male CEOs upon going private. Bumble did not respond to request for comment.
Amy Andersen, the self-described matchmaker of Silicon Valley, believes the apps’ contraction is part of a larger disillusionment with the idea that romance could be made simpler by algorithms.
She told The Post she’s noticed a “huge exodus from the apps” that’s escalated in the last three years — even among the techies who literally founded them.
“I have had clients literally be the ones who have built the app, but they’re not using it when it comes to their own personal lives,” she said. “The machine professionally dominates their lives, yet when it comes to the intricacies of their personal lives, they’re choosing the human.”
Another app trying to reinvent itself is Tinder, which has seen monthly active users decline 7% year-over-year as of March and whose parent company Match Group is increasing Tinder’s marketing budget by $50 million this year.
After almost fifteen years in the business of matching people seamlessly online through a swipe, they’re moving into the events space and offering users in-person gatherings on a new tab in the app. Tinder told The Post that they’ve facilitated over 1,700 events so far and hope to reach 75 cities by the end of the year.
They seem to have reached an unlikely conclusion: that staying alive in the online dating space might require recreating the sort of social scenarios apps were originally aiming to replace.
Tinder has also tried to get people together in groups, rather than on one-on-one dates. They launched “double date mode” in 2025, and last month added group hangouts to their offerings. “We’re building ways to lower the pressure on Tinder,” a spokesperson told The Post.
“Ultimately, our goal is to make finding a spark feel more fun, authentic and connected to real life.”
The move comes as singles are flocking to more old school methods of finding partners. They’re joining running clubs and pickleball leagues in hopes of finding the one, and setting up their friends with potential matches. Meanwhile, in-person singles events hosted on Eventbrite literally doubled between 2022 and 2025.
Disillusioned singles are also trying out good old-fashioned matchmaking — tasking a human, rather than an algorithm, with finding them love. Chris Kumar, CEO of the country’s largest online matchmaking service Tawkify, said his platform has grown 30% year-over-year.
The upswing, he says, is part of a larger story of “dating app fatigue” and singles desperately looking for a more substantive alternative.
“The apps lost the elegance of what it means to be online and have that spark of connection with someone who swipes on you. That just isn’t exciting anymore,” he said. “So [the apps are trying] to find ways to reinvigorate that hope and that excitement from singles.”
The whole transformation seems to point to an uncomfortable conclusion: the future of dating apps may be one where the apps themselves take the back seat, and let singles find one another on their own terms. Its the clearest proof yet that Cupid’s mysterious ways can’t be distilled into an algorthim and true love remains as unpredictable and sometimes elusive as ever.

item.title: [The Times of India] Zodiac Love Horoscope, 19 October 2026: Aquarius Moon Brings a Need for Space, Greater Freedom Inside Relationships
item.dc:creator: Neeraj Dhankher
item.description: Two heavy Capricorn days are done. The Moon moves into Aquarius, and people want air. Your partner may head out with old college friends tonight. Let them. Singles will probably click faster with someone who feels like a mate first. How to Navigate Today's Energy The Aquarius Moon trines the Sun in Libra. Fair, easy talk flows well under this. Friendship sits at the centre of love today. But there is a catch. The same Moon opposes Mars in Leo, and Venus, still retrograde in Scorpio, squares it.
item.content:encoded:
Two heavy Capricorn days are done. The Moon moves into Aquarius, and people want air. Your partner may head out with old college friends tonight. Let them. Singles will probably click faster with someone who feels like a mate first.
How to Navigate Today's Energy
The Aquarius Moon trines the Sun in Libra. Fair, easy talk flows well under this. Friendship sits at the centre of love today.
But there is a catch. The same Moon opposes Mars in Leo, and Venus, still retrograde in Scorpio, squares it. So one person craves attention while the other wants a quiet evening with a book. Jealousy can flare over small things, like a laughing emoji on someone else's post. Space works only when it comes with a message. Tell your partner where you'll be and roughly when you'll be home.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Leo: With the Moon opposite your sign, your partner's attention drifts elsewhere for a day. Sulking won't bring it back. Suggest a plan for Wednesday instead.
Taurus: A changed routine bothers you more than it should. If the usual Sunday-night call doesn't happen, there's likely a dull reason behind it.
Scorpio: Venus retrograde in your sign clashes with the Moon. Asking who someone was texting at midnight will start a row you don't need.
Cancer: You want closeness, and others want distance. Give it. Comfort will come back on its own.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Aquarius: The Moon in your sign makes you easy to be around. A single Aquarius could meet someone through a hobby group or a volunteering shift. Couples get to talk like best friends again.
Gemini:
Long chats suit you today. An honest friend might admit feelings, and the timing feels right.
Libra: Your partner gives you room without being asked. That small kindness matters more than flowers.
Aries: Saturn in your sign gets support from the Aquarius Moon. You feel calm about commitment, and someone notices.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Virgo:
Skip the questions about every hour your partner spent away.
Sagittarius: Freedom is your comfort zone. Share some of it.
Capricorn: Yesterday's serious mood can ease into lighter chat.
Pisces: A group outing works better than a dinner for two.
Lucky Action of the Day
Plan one evening this week where you both do your own thing, then meet late for tea and swap stories.
