item.dc:creator: ABU DHABI
item.description: Al Masraf (Arab Bank for Investment & Foreign Trade) has announced that it has inked a major project financing deal with Innovo Group, an industry leader in construction and development across the built environment. This funding will help Innovo in delivering a significant project. The agreement reflects Al Masraf’s continued commitment to supporting major businesses and projects that contribute to the UAE’s economic growth and development. The agreement represents one of the largest project fin
item.content:encoded:
Al Masraf (Arab Bank for Investment & Foreign Trade) has announced that it has inked a major project financing deal with Innovo Group, an industry leader in construction and development across the built environment. This funding will help Innovo in delivering a significant project.
The agreement reflects Al Masraf’s continued commitment to supporting major businesses and projects that contribute to the UAE’s economic growth and development.
The agreement represents one of the largest project financing facilities Al Masraf has extended to a corporate client, highlighting the bank’s growing capability to provide tailored financing solutions for complex, strategically significant projects.
The media ceremony, held at Innovo Group’s head office in Dubai, brought together Fuad Mohamed, Chief Executive Officer of Al Masraf, and Bishoy Azmy, Chief Executive Officer of Innovo Group, to mark the milestone and highlight the organisations’ collaboration.
Speaking on the occasion, Mohamed said: "This milestone reflects Al Masraf’s commitment to supporting the UAE’s ambitious infrastructure and development agenda and to building long-term partnerships with leading organisations across the country."
"Our collaboration with Innovo Group demonstrates the strength of our corporate banking capabilities and our ability to provide tailored financing solutions that support projects of strategic importance. We are proud to play a role in enabling the delivery of major developments and look forward to strengthening our partnership with Innovo Group as we continue to support its growth and ambitions," he stated.
The project financing agreement underscores Al Masraf’s commitment to empowering future legacies by supporting businesses and projects that contribute to the UAE’s continued growth and long-term prosperity.
On the deal, Azmy said: "Al Masraf has been a valued banking partner to Innovo, and we welcome the opportunity to deepen our engagement. As our business evolves, we see scope to broaden our collaboration and work together on new opportunities."
Through its Corporate Banking business, Al Masraf continues to strengthen its role as a trusted financial partner to businesses contributing to the UAE’s economic development, providing tailored solutions designed around the needs and ambitions of its corporate clients.
"We look forward to building on the strong foundations of our relationship in the period ahead," he added.-TradeArabia News Service

item.title: [Honeycombers] Dating events in Singapore: Romantic gatherings and meet-cutes where you might find The One
item.dc:creator: Ashe Liao
item.description: We’ve got a one-stop guide to find out about all the dating events happening in Singapore – from speed dates to intentional dinners. Dating events in Singapore happen more frequently than you think! With the rise of in-person social events, we’re clearly not the only ones craving some real-life socialising. And for the members of the lonely hearts club, you’ve likely exhausted your dating app matches. How about trying something new with a little in-person chit-chat? All you have to do is find on
item.content:encoded:
We’ve got a one-stop guide to find out about all the dating events happening in Singapore – from speed dates to intentional dinners.
Dating events in Singapore happen more frequently than you think! With the rise of in-person social events, we’re clearly not the only ones craving some real-life socialising. And for the members of the lonely hearts club, you’ve likely exhausted your dating app matches. How about trying something new with a little in-person chit-chat? All you have to do is find one that catches your eye (the same way your new beau will).
Culture Sg never disappoints when it comes to social events in Singapore. Branching out from Above 30 Club comes SomeoneNew, a place for all 30-somethings and up to meet like-minded people. Because we all know as you get older, making friends gets ridiculously harder. The collective is hosting its first singles’ event, and you have two ways to meet your match – approach the cutie across the bar or leave it up to fate with a questionnaire. And there’ll be plenty of games to keep things interesting along the way.
When: 21 October 2026, 7.30pm to 10.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $30; includes one drink
Where: SomeoneNew: Love edition, Rasa Space, 9 Raffles Place, Singapore 048619
Hey, Gen Zs. We haven’t forgotten about you, and neither has the team at Type Mixers. What started as a desire to ditch the dating apps and to “do it for the plot” soon turned into regular themed gatherings to put singles into a room to see what happens. And then, strangers became friends while sparks flew. Sounds like a pretty magical journey to us! You can also join the fun by keeping an eye out on the team’s social media pages for updates.
For the month of October, it’s no surprise that we’re getting another Halloween-themed mixer! This time, you’re getting a mystery match, secret identity, and a hidden mission. Come dressed as either a devil or an angel and enjoy tarot reading, snap photos at a photo booth, sip Halloween-themed drinks, and meet a special someone along the way.
When: 30 October 2026, 7.30pm to 11pm
How much: Tickets start from $48 for ladies and $55 for men; pre-registration required
Where: Type Mixers: Angels & Devils, location revealed only to confirmed attendees
After its launch in 2024, the demand for Never Strangers events skyrocketed and clearly has no signs of coming down! As one of the first offline social event collectives to come about, the team has hosted a number of social events, from dating mixers to platonic dinners. If you want to be part of this cool kids club, register your details on the website, and you’ll be added to the guest list! Events are curated based on age, vibe, and interest, so you’ll be hand-picked for an event that’s catered to you.
The next edition of Never Strangers will be hosted on a yacht. AKA, the perfect opportunity for you to break out a cute swimsuit that hasn’t seen water in a hot minute. Sailing out of Keppel Bay, you’ll get to enjoy free-flow cocktails by Garage, games, and the classic algorithm match reveal before returning to the dock.
When: Hosts events monthly; yacht event on 24 October 2026, 3pm to 7pm
How much: Varies with each event
Where: Never Strangers, register online
Let us introduce you to Thursday; the biggest IRL dating app in the world. It’s less about the dating app itself and more about the in-person events. Because they care about getting you out the door to meet someone rather than spend your time endlessly matching. All you have to do is pick your city and you can pick from a tidy list of events happening in your area.
We’ve already spotted a variety of singles’ mixers you can join depending on what your vibe is! Enter a game of mystery mini golf, head to a rooftop bar for conversations with stunning city views, or enter a Halloween-themed encounter.
When: Various dates
How much: Ticket costs vary with each event
Where: Thursday, locations vary
From the same crew who brought you the dating series Maybe It’s You is The Stupid Cupid. The team will be hosting its first singles mixer, taking the dating experience offline, putting the same thoughtfulness and love into it. There is a strict vetting process you’ll have to go through if you want to participate. But this means the crowd will be extra curated to ensure a good vibe.
When: 1 November 2026, 7pm till late
How much: Free admission; registration required, closes 18 October 2026
Where: The Stupid Cupid’s Singles’ Mixer, location revealed to confirmed attendees
You’d be surprised at how good the vibes are at a TCM-inspired bar. So good, that you’ll even spot The One sitting across from you! The bar will be hosting a specially curated singles’ day dinner for a small group of curious bar-goers. As you chat over food, you’ll participate in shared activities and little acts of service that keep the conversation flowing. More details are set to be released, so stay tuned.
When: 11 November 2026, 6pm
How much: To be confirmed
Where: Singles’ Day at Synthesis, #01-643, Suntec City, 3 Temasek Boulevard, Singapore 038983
Think you’ve got what it takes to help your friend bait a date at Fishbowl? Then sign yourselves up for the latest singles’ pitch event happening in October. You, as your BFF’s wingman, have to convince a crowd full of strangers why your friend is the best date candidate out there. Prepare a three-minute presentation and sell ‘em with your best elevator pitch. Psst: show off your Coffee Meets Bagel profile, and you can get 10% off your drinks!
When: 23 October 2026, 7.30pm to 9.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $30 (includes one free drink)
Where: Flying Fish: Singles’ Pitch Night, Wingman Edition, Rasa Space, 9 Raffles Place, Singapore 048619
Let’s be real here – we could all use a session of puppy yoga to relieve some stress. But this session is specifically for the single dog parents out there. Use this as an excuse to get your pupper out for a playdate, but with yoga mats and (hopefully) no awkward small talk. Get to know other yoga participants as you stretch, or wait till after the session during your own social hour. Who knows, maybe your furkid could find the love of their life here too.
When: 21 November 2026, 4pm to 5.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $70
Where: Dog Owners Yoga Date, Gravity by Noir, 144 Robinson Road, Singapore 068908
Expect a little sugar and a lot of spice in this Dia de los Meurtos-esque singles’ mixer. Come dressed in theme with touches of marigolds, skulls, and dark romance to impress and let the night unfold. If you’re attached, feel free to come find friends too! You’ll be given traffic light-style wristbands that indicate your status so people know what you’re looking for. Then simply let the night unfold and see what it has in store for you.
When: 22 October 2026, 8pm to 10pm
How much: $55 per person (includes 2 alcoholic drinks and snacks); pre-registration required
Where: Deadly Chemistry: A Mexican Singles’ Night, Mami’s Tamales, 55 Keong Saik Road, Singapore 089158
For singles aged 30 to 50 years old, this is a dating event in Singapore for you. This isn’t any ordinary rooftop bar in the city. It’s actually about to turn into a venue for conversation where sparks come alive. If you need a sign from the universe, turn to the tarot reading corner and get a mini reading on love and romance. And as you bathe in the golden hour light, prepare yourself for side quests! Prompts will be sent to your phone, giving you an excuse to talk to the stranger you’ve been eyeing all evening.
When: 22 October 2026, 6pm to 9pm
How much: Tickets start from $60 for ladies & $50 for men; includes one free drink
Where: Rooftop Connections at Truth or Dare, 11 North Canal Road, Singapore 048824
Everyone talks about small and intentional groups, but what about a social night for those of us who love being in a crowd? One Tile Away frequently hosts mahjong games meant for singles looking for love or players looking for extra mahjong kakis. The upcoming socials are hosted in larger groups, and you’ll be split into your tables to meet some new people. And yes, beginners are welcome to attend and facilitators will be on-site to guide you through the game.
When: 21, 28 & 29 October 2026
How much: Ticket prices vary with each event
Where: One Tile Away: A Social Mixer, multiple locations including Enclosed and *Scape
Give your creative side an opportunity to shine at this neon singles party happening just before Halloween! This glow-in-the-dark art jamming experience doesn’t even need you to be a painter. You’ll be guided by instructors the whole step of the way, and walk home with a glowing masterpiece. And while you’re at it, mingle with fellow singles and get a conversation flowing.
When: 30 October 2026, 7.30pm to 9.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $58; all art materials provided
Where: Singles Neon Party, #02-01, Scuro, 79 Kampong Bahru Road, Singapore 169377
We already know the pickleball trend is here to stay, so why not use your new hobby to meet some new people? Come for a social game and meet new people through a mix of friendly games and off-court conversations. No experience necessary! You’ll be rotated through different groups to meet different players, and have plenty of time to mingle after the games. Paddles and balls provided, so just come as you are.
When: 6 November 2026, 8pm to 10.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $18 for ladies & $58 for men
Where: Play!Pickle: Match & Mingle, #04-27, 756 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534626
You know what’s a great way to break the ice with a cute stranger? Letting your furkid do the approaching! Bettr Coffee is hosting a singles’ pitch night, and you’re more than welcome to bring your pupper to its pet-friendly space at The Foundry. Don’t have a pet or don’t intend to bring them along? No worries, because you’re still welcome to join and meet new people regardless. Seeing all the pets in one place is a fabulous bonus.
When: 16 October 2026, 7pm to 9pm
How much: Tickets start from $25
Where: Singles Pitch Night: Pets & Pawrents Edition, Bettr Coffee, The Foundry, 11 Prinsep Link, Singapore 187949
If you need an excuse to enjoy a date and some good wine, look no further than Vivino’s singles’ day mixer. You’ll be treated to three glasses of wine to help smoothen things along. And don’t worry if you’re a little shy, because a dating coach will be on-site to help provide some structure! Think: activities that’ll actually get you talking and real dating tips.
When: 11 November 2026, 7pm to 8pm
How much: Tickets start from $45
Where: Vivino Singles Mixer, #01-44B, Raffles City, 252 North Bridge Road, Singapore 179103
We think Goodbye, Alibi’s cosy space makes for a fab date night spot – so why not use it to try finding The One? Cure hump day with a cheeky drink and meet-cute with a small group of strangers. This means conversations will go beyond the usual small talk, with curated ice breakers, and ice cold drinks. This event is also all-inclusive, so feel free to come as you are and with an open mind.
When: Every first Wednesday of the month; 4 November 2026 & 2 December 2026
How much: Tickets start from $10 for ladies and $35 for men
Where: Small group dating at Goodbye, Alibi, 53A Duxton Road, Singapore 089517
Looking for love? Let’s see if dating events in Singapore can help you out!
Speed dating is an event structure where you’ll have short, one-to-one conversations with potential matches. Each round lasts only a few minutes before you rotate to the next person. After the whole session is over, you’re usually invited to speak with people who you’d like to see again.
Prices vary depending on what kind of activities are being hosted and the venue. You can expect dates to cost anywhere between $30 to $50 if they involve activities. For curated dinners, you may pay upwards of $100.
Yes, feel free to join even if you’re not ready for a serious relationship. Dating events are meant for people to meet, and not everyone will commit to something long-term. However, it’s important to communicate this with the people you meet.
You’d be surprised by the number of dating events catering to people aged 30 and up! Keep your eye out for collectives like Never Strangers and SomeoneNew, which host gatherings for people above 30.
Yes, there are! Most dating events welcome people of all orientations, and often disclaim it in the event descriptions. If you’re uncertain, you can message the organisers to double check.

item.content:encoded:
Love Horoscope Today, October 19, 2026
October 19, 2026, brings heart-centered opportunities and emotional growth for all zodiac signs. Many may receive love proposals or experience deeper connections.
Love Horoscope Today, October 19, 2026: Today is heart-centered and filled with opportunities for emotional growth, loving connections, and meaningful conversations. Many zodiac signs, such as Aries, Virgo, and Aquarius, may face a love proposal or a moment of emotional decision where listening to the heart is a must.
Taurus, Gemini, Libra, and Scorpio enjoy deepening connections and affectionate experiences, while Cancer, Leo, Sagittarius, and Pisces are encouraged to develop understanding and harmony in love and family relationships. Capricorns can expect a wave of romantic energy and meaningful conversations. Overall, this is a favorable day for love, but clarity, patience, and heartfelt dialogue will help move things forward.
Aries Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you should try to understand the importance of your partner and try to move the relationship forward by leaving your ego aside. Today, you may also get a proposal that may put you in a dilemma whether to say yes or no. In such a situation, you should listen to your heart and do what you feel is right.
Taurus Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you will share your feelings with your partner and try to understand each other better. Your love will become a source of new enthusiasm and happiness in your life. To understand your love, you have to listen to your heart. Your horoscope advises you to experience happiness and prosperity with your love today.
Gemini Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you should listen to your heart and do what you feel is right. Do not rush into any relationship and study patiently. Because of your love and understanding, your relationship will become even stronger today. The time spent with each other today will be very special for you. You will get a chance to come closer to your spouse, and the relationship between you will become even sweeter. Today will be a very suitable day for you to express your love.
Cancer Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you may need to bridge the distance between you and your partner by talking to them. If you want to get married, then today can be very auspicious for you. A new chapter can begin for you, which can be ready to bring happiness to your life. Your relationship with family can be very sweet today. Do not quarrel with anyone unnecessarily today, and try to understand your love.
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you will get time to make your relationship with your boyfriend/girlfriend even more romantic. Today you will get a chance to talk lovingly to your boyfriend/girlfriend and spend time with them. This can make your relationship even stronger. If you go on a short trip with your boyfriend/girlfriend, you will get a chance to make your relationship even more beautiful.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that someone can propose to you today. You will be in a dilemma whether to say yes or no. But you should listen to your heart and do what feels right. You should not rush into any relationship. Today will be a very happy day for you, and you will get even more happiness in your love relationship.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today will be a very pleasant and happy day for you. The feeling of depth and love will increase in your relationship. Your relationship with your partner will deepen, and you will get a chance to understand them more. Today will be a very auspicious day for you. You will experience romantic situations with your partner, and your relationship will deepen. Today will be a day full of happiness and love for you.
Scorpio Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that lovers can also think of converting their love into marriage. A relationship can start between you, which will bring you and your lover closer to each other. Your relationship may deepen, and both of you may be ready to give more importance to each other’s love. To understand your love, you should try to understand his/her feelings.
Sagittarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that your love will bring new enthusiasm and new beginnings in your life. Your relationship with the family will also strengthen, and you will get their support and cooperation. Do not quarrel with anyone unnecessarily today, and try to understand your love and family relationships.
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you will feel as if the flower of love has bloomed in your life. Those who are unmarried may get many love proposals today. This time will be very romantic for you, and you will get a chance to share your feelings with people around you. This time will be full of love for your loved ones. You will get love in return and get a chance to communicate better with your partner.
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you may get good proposals for marriage, which can be very auspicious for you. But today, there may be some minor disagreement in your love life. Before things get worse, try to solve the problem by talking to each other. Be honest in your behavior and try to understand your partner. Your partner will help you understand your feelings and solve the problem.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you should share your life experiences with your lover to improve your relationship. Today, a new chapter of your life can begin, and you can get a chance to fulfill your dreams with your lover. Today, you will get a chance to understand your lover and your relationship better. Today you will get time to share your feelings with your boyfriend/girlfriend, and you will get a chance to connect more deeply with the two of you.
Quick Answers
On October 19, 2026, many zodiac signs such as Aries, Virgo, and Aquarius may face a love proposal. Additionally, unmarried Capricorns can expect multiple love proposals, and signs like Aquarius and Scorpio may receive good proposals for marriage or think about converting their love into marriage.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope For Monday, October 19: You Might Be The One Getting Better Today
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 19, 2026. The Aquarius Moon squares retrograde Venus in Scorpio on Monday, helping you see where you can do better.
It doesn’t matter whether you’ve been in love for years or just met someone you can see a future with. Relationships are based on self-growth, which means there is always another lesson to learn that can help you become better. And when you become better, your relationships do too. That's what this transit is all about.
Love horoscopes are here for each zodiac sign on Monday, October 19, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t be afraid to need someone, Aries. You are the most independent zodiac sign by nature. Understanding that you’re allowed to receive support, and even ask for it, is one of your core lessons, but on Monday it goes even deeper.
Just because you may be surrounded by people doesn’t mean they can take the place of love from a partner. Honor your needs and know that relying on someone else is a part of what you deserve.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Love isn’t a checklist, sweet Taurus. Monday brings a reminder of the difference between love and work.
With your grounded and practical nature, you tend to approach all aspects of your life methodically. However, that doesn’t mean you can apply that same energy to your love life. You must be vulnerable and hold space for what both you and your partner want.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t run away from this, Gemini. Acknowledging what you’ve done in the past doesn’t mean you’re not ready for something different now.
In the past, you have run from relationships, especially when they got difficult or challenged your sense of independence. But you can’t do that this time. Instead, do the real work of relationships, which may also include seeking counseling for this phase you’re currently in.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It’s not always about what you do, Cancer, but what you hold space for. On Monday, your mind may feel especially active as you ponder all the choices available to you. But you need to slow down and start being in your feelings.
Just because you may feel exhausted from always feeling doesn’t mean you can shift out of them, especially with this ongoing Venus retrograde. Lean into what you feel and why, and worry about any possible changes later on.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
A new love isn’t going to make this any better, Leo. You may have recently separated from a long-term partner or be in the midst of a divorce and even custody proceedings. As much as you may want to fill that space and live your best life, getting into a new relationship won’t serve you right now.
Instead, on Monday, deal with matters in your personal life. As much as you wish you could, you can’t just gloss over this important chapter.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You aren’t meant to hold anything back, dear Virgo. On Monday, you will be in touch with your emotions and what you need from a relationship and your life as a whole. However, you may be hesitant to bring it up to your partner or those you’re entwined with.
Don’t let yourself shut down when you are meant to speak up. Advocate for yourself, and don't worry about how anyone else will react.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t ignore what surfaces on Monday, dearest Libra. You often diminish your own needs or what you deserve to receive in a relationship. By being so focused on what you can give and making it work, you overlook the most important parts of what it means to love.
October 19 asks that you sit in your feelings. Honor how you haven’t been treated or loved in the ways you deserve and start setting a new bar for yourself. If you’re single, don’t forget that you can give yourself that kind of love too.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You are in progress, Scorpio. This means that you have to hold space for multiple possibilities.
On October 19, the Aquarius Moon invites you to reflect on themes in your personal life and home, especially involving hyperindependence. While independence is a key part of love, hyperindependence keeps out what you most want. Try to let someone in on Monday. Be receptive to love and recognize that how you love yourself sets the standard for everything else in your life.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
The truth has a way of changing things, Sagittarius. But you’re being guided to let it.
Monday brings a new awareness from the depths of your soul. This may involve a current relationship or a particular one from the past. It won’t feel convenient, but that’s all the more reason you’re meant to lean into its purpose. Honor this feeling and the truth that comes with it, as you will need to trust yourself to take action.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be willing to challenge yourself, Capricorn. On Monday, you are asked to reflect on a particular relationship in your life to see if you still feel the way you once did.
You may find that your feelings have grown; however, you could also realize that you’ve outgrown this connection. Be sure you're honoring the kind of relationship you truly deserve and not settling for less.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t stop now, Aquarius. You’ve come this far, which means you are meant to keep going and see where this phase of your life leads.
On Monday, the Moon in your sign helps you become aware of and honor your authentic feelings. This will be essential as you are asked to think about how you’ve lived your life and if your priorities actually align with what is most important to you. Be honest with yourself and don’t be afraid to make the changes you know you need.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your dreams are meant to become a reality, dearest Pisces. With Venus retrograde in Scorpio, you are getting a second chance at your destiny. This energy helps you hold space for people and opportunities from your past. However, you must let your inner self decide what to do about it.
On Monday, lean into your intuition or connect with your spirit guides. The choices you’re being guided to make won’t seem logical, but they will help you make your dreams come true.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.dc:creator: Jeon Hyeong-u

item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (Republican-Pennsylvania), a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, stated that the South Korea-U.S. alliance is in the process of being "reset," describing it as couples counseling rather than a divorce.
According to the U.S. think tank Hudson Institute on October 18 (local time), McCormick made the remarks during a conversation held in Washington, D.C., on October 16 with Mike Gallagher, former chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.
"We are resetting the relationship," McCormick explained. "When you reset a relationship, feelings get hurt and friction occurs."
"Even in a marriage, sometimes the balance gets out of sync, leading one side to tell the other that adjustments are needed," he emphasized, adding that the South Korea-U.S. relationship is "going through couples counseling, not getting a divorce."
He added, "We need more from our Asian allies. The relationship was imbalanced, and they acknowledge that too," and expressed his belief that "we are on the path to a much deeper and stronger relationship."
McCormick recently returned to the United States after visiting Japan and South Korea.
During his trip to South Korea, he visited the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and Hanwha Ocean's Geoje shipyard.
He also met with Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul.
Citing the massive investment pledges in the U.S. made by both South Korea and Japan as prime examples of the alliance realignment, McCormick noted, "I heard no controversy (during our meetings in Korea). The conversations were entirely focused on where to invest that capital and how to utilize it."
Mentioning South Korea's pledge to purchase USD 25 billion worth of U.S. military equipment and its plans to increase the defense budget, he evaluated, "We haven't reached the necessary level yet, but we are moving in a direction that aligns with bearing our fair share."
McCormick argued that the United States and its allies must innovate technology faster than China and produce more defense materiel in the long run, asserting, "We must train, plan, and fight with our allies as a single military force and a single military capability."
"If we get this right, China will look across the Taiwan Strait every morning and conclude, 'Not today,'" he said.
(Photo: Yonhap News)
※ Please note: This article was translated by AI and may contain errors.

item.title: [La Voz News] Dating apps: a tool, or a trap
item.dc:creator: Yosselyn Garcia Rodas
item.description: In the digital age, the dating scene has drastically changed; instead of meeting in bars or through mutual friends, many people meet their partners-to-be on dating apps. This includes San Francisco-based dating coach Alan Chan, who said he spent about a year and a half on dating apps after a long-term relationship from the age of 20 to 26, until he met his fiancée on Tinder. “I was very new to the dating app scene,” Chan said. “By the time I matched with my fiancée, I was so tired of it. I was l
item.content:encoded:
In the digital age, the dating scene has drastically changed; instead of meeting in bars or through mutual friends, many people meet their partners-to-be on dating apps.
This includes San Francisco-based dating coach Alan Chan, who said he spent about a year and a half on dating apps after a long-term relationship from the age of 20 to 26, until he met his fiancée on Tinder.
“I was very new to the dating app scene,” Chan said. “By the time I matched with my fiancée, I was so tired of it. I was like, ‘Let’s just go on dates and have fun.’”
A 2019 Pew Research Center poll found that three in 10 surveyed U.S. adults have used a dating site or app; although Chan recommended dating apps as a tool, he said people shouldn’t solely rely on them to find a partner.
“Dating apps are probably where you’re going to meet someone,” Chan said. “I would also recommend attending parties, … especially if you’re a full-time worker, which most of us are, it’s very hard to meet people.”
Since meeting his fiancée, Chan started coaching others in finding partners, including one client who found a girlfriend after two weeks.
“Every day you’re out is an opportunity to meet someone,” Chan said. “All it takes is eye contact, a smile and a conversation.”
Communications major Sophie Everett, 22, said they met their current partner of three years on Hinge; however, they said they wouldn’t push dating apps onto others just because of their good experience.
“I wasn’t looking for anything serious,” Everett said. “He (my partner) was kind of plopped into my lap.”
Everett also said they believe dating apps can be good in some ways.
“You can meet people (on dating apps) that you wouldn’t have met (otherwise),” Everett said.
Julia Le, 19, accounting and film production major, said dating apps aren’t for her.
“I definitely see the value in them,” Le said. “Personally, it just doesn’t work.”
Le said she hasn’t been on dating apps for a while and prefers meeting people organically, but has tried them before.
“I never had a serious relationship that came out of a dating app,” Le said. “People have really good experiences there, but the good experiences are few and narrow compared to the vast majority.”
A 2024 Computers in Human Behavior study found that people who meet on dating apps have less stable marriages.
Accounting major Larry Maciel, 20, said he thinks dating apps are horrible.
“People have unrealistic expectations whenever they go on one,” Maciel said. “They expect to find the love of their life or they think that the app is going to solve all their problems.”
A 2024 Pew Research Center study found that while U.S. adults’ perceptions on dating apps skew positive, only 10% of partnered adults met their current significant other through a dating site or app.
Pew’s survey also found that 24% of partnered lesbian, gay or bisexual adults and one in five partnered people under 30 met their partners on dating sites, a far higher rate than other demographics.
Despite his thoughts on dating apps, Maciel also said he has found cool people on them.
“It (a dating app or website) is an OK way to meet people, especially if you’re shy or have anxiety,” Maciel said. “Know what you’re getting into when you download it, and go in without any expectations.”

item.title: [Boston Herald] Dear Abby: I love my daughter, but not her abuse
item.dc:creator: Abigail Van Buren
item.description: Dear Abby: I have three grown children and seven grandchildren. I have solid relationships with my oldest and youngest, their spouses and their children. My middle daughter, “Hope,” has always been distant. I’ve tried for years to build a relationship with her and her children. Hope has suffered from mental and physical illness most of her life, and I’d like to be able to help her. The problem is that she keeps a house full of animals, and the place is unwelcoming to say the least. I’ve also tri
item.content:encoded:
Dear Abby: I have three grown children and seven grandchildren. I have solid relationships with my oldest and youngest, their spouses and their children. My middle daughter, “Hope,” has always been distant. I’ve tried for years to build a relationship with her and her children.
Hope has suffered from mental and physical illness most of her life, and I’d like to be able to help her. The problem is that she keeps a house full of animals, and the place is unwelcoming to say the least. I’ve also tried keeping in touch via phone calls, but they always end up with her being critical and accusing me of things that happened a long time ago — some of which I wasn’t even aware of. She has no relationships outside of her two children and no contact with her siblings.
I love Hope and her children, but I’m tired of the abuse. I have quit pushing myself on her, but I miss her so much. Is there any hope for us? — Losing Hope in Alabama
Dear Losing Hope: You don’t want the door to close forever, so it’s important to keep the lines of communication open. You can continue to call Hope and visit occasionally without enduring the abuse.
Each time she tries to steer the conversation in a negative direction, use the opportunity to introduce the idea of family counseling. Frame it as your desire to understand the past events she is still unhappy about. If you can get Hope to attend a few sessions with you, it may be a big step forward.
Dear Abby: A dear friend is obsessed with death and the grieving process. While her fixation is not entirely unusual, her actions are. She attends area funeral services two to four times a week for people she does not know. She sits in the back, rarely talks to family and friends, and leaves quietly, so she says it isn’t a big deal. I disagree. I feel it’s disrespectful to attend the funeral services of a stranger even if you are unobtrusive. What do you think? Am I wrong? — Perplexed in Arkansas
Dear Perplexed: It’s hard to label a behavior disrespectful when it’s causing no harm or distress to anyone. I don’t know how isolated this friend of yours is, but this may be her way to be in the presence of others and cope with loneliness. Another reason could be that she enjoys hearing about people’s lives. Rather than criticize or judge her, I think you should simply ask her why she does it. Her answer may be enlightening.
Dear Abby: How can I get my nice, college-educated son-in-law to wipe his mouth with a napkin during meals instead of using his sleeve? — Father-In-Law With Manners
Dear F-I-L: There are two ways to get the message across. The first would be to “remind” him in plain English while you are at the table. The second would be to speak to your daughter about it and ask her to get the message across.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.content:encoded:
Each sign of the zodiac has its own set of traits that help to define their personalities and set them apart from each other. Wouldn't it be nice to know what the universe has planned for you at the beginning of the day? Keep reading to find out if today will be lucky for you.
ARIES
This week take a good look at what love feels like to you. If you're losing more energy than you're getting back, then something is wrong. You should feel supported, not exhausted. If you are always the one trying and trying again, take a step back and breathe. Love is meant to be a give and take, not a daily struggle. A connection is worth holding onto if it offers calm, but if it just leaves you confused or feeling unhappy, then you have to ask why. Your happiness is also very important.
TAURUS
Keep love easy this week. By all means, don’t try to plan every move or read between the lines. Just talk your heart out without any strategy. If you happen to find yourself in a relationship or getting to know someone along the way, let it flow naturally. You don’t have to win, impress or manage the situation. Just be present and kind. The real relationship has no game. It demands honesty and time.
Let that smile speak for you. If it is pure love, it will be effortless, and never forced.
GEMINI
Your energy is important, so this week, trust your instincts on who is worth it. Not everyone wants you to be all ears. Some may appear interesting, yet leave you feeling uncertain. Notice how you feel around them. If your inner voice is saying no, then trust that voice. If they bring tranquility and endeavor, then think about giving them a go. Whether you are single or attached, your best course of action is to listen to your inner voice now; do not turn it off.
CANCER
This week, remember that the correct type of love won’t leave you feeling small or confused. If someone really loves you, they’ll make you feel worthwhile. You don’t have to prove yourself or fight for their attention. If you are partnered, see if you are treated as if you are truly there. If the response is yes, you’re in the proper place. If not, think about why the spokesperson answered no. Love is intended to make you grow, not wonder if you’re worthy.
LEO
Sometimes the intimacy deepens when you give each other space. So this week, don’t hold tight. Give some room for ideas, feelings, and missing each other. If that person is really for you, distance will not sever the link. It will just make that special bond even stronger. Now if you are single, stand back from the chasing and just let love to find you in its natural flow. Sometimes a little pause can be a lot of clarity.
VIRGO
That is power when you are being true to yourself and to others. This week, feelings bubble up. You don't have to stay locked inside to make everyone else comfortable. Speak softly yet firmly. If you miss someone, say it. If you feel hurt, say so too. Being open and honest about your feelings makes you strong and authentic, not weak. Love, when shared in sincerity, grows more. Holding in the sensation builds more walls up between you and everyone else. Speak your heart.
LIBRA
Love may feel lighter this week, if you go easy with the pressure. Don't overdo every perfect moment. Let the fun come back in small doses. If you're in a relationship, try to laugh it off, not have profound chats all the time. If you are alone, let your heart be free and go with love. And again, when one quits forcing, one finds joy. Love is sometimes easy. It’s not just about repairing. Sometimes it is simply playing, smiling and just being present without any expectations.
SCORPIO
Love: An ending may show up this week. Don't frighten yourself with it. Sometimes something must end to give room for what is true. Let go of the connection which feels forced. Let the door close softly, not sadly. What left now was not meant to stay. What follows will be more honest, more steady. You are not losing the love. You are making way for something better. Trust the heart to recognize when it's time to move on.
SAGITTARIUS
And this week, don’t forget to beg for emotional maturity. You deserve love that is transparent, calm, and respectful. if it's casual dating or a totally committed relationship, think about if your feelings are being treated correctly. Do they listen? Or do they tune out? Try to be patient but don’t compromise your standards. Real love is acceptance, not disagreement. Keep your heart open, but be strong. You deserve love from an adult, not guessing.
CAPRICORN
Watch how people listen to you this week. Notice not only their words, but their listening, their silences, even their gaze. What matters is the response. If people really hear you they don’t need you to say it twice. A suggestion is also being disregarded or misconstrued. Listening is love, silent love. It is caring. It is patience. It is work. Watch out for this one, single or taken. He that loveth, heareth.
AQUARIUS
There are no words to describe the way you feel when you walk out of someone else's presence. Take time this week to reflect on your emotional health: When you spend time with them, do you feel lighter or heavier? Do you feel safe or worn out? Your body talks before your head. If your connection gives you peace, that is your answer. Don't turn away if you feel anxious and confused. Love should be peaceful not frantic. Love makes you feel good. Suspicion makes you feel bad. You deserve to feel wonderful.
PISCES
Truth is your route to greater love this week. You could have needs you’re too scared to talk about, but now is the time to get them out. True love wants to hear the truth. Don’t stay mute merely to keep the peace. If you reveal your feelings with love the proper person will not go away. If you're in a relationship or still waiting, know what makes your heart feel safe and held. Truth leads to something permanent.
This article is written by, Sidhharrth S Kumaar, Registered Pharmacist, Astro Numerologist, Life & Relationship Coach, Vaastu Expert, IKS Expert, I Ching Expert, Energy Healer, Music Therapist, Author of “Think like a Sage Lead like a CEO” series and Chief Astro Strategy Officer (CASO), NumroVani.

item.title: [swiowanewssource.com] Are dating apps to blame if you’re still single? Expert says no
item.dc:creator: Talker News
item.description: By Ben Barry A relationship coach says dating apps are not to blame if you're single - and reveals her four tips to find love on them. She believes that dating apps aren't inherently the problem with modern-day dating and argues that users' expectations and how we use them are to blame. item.content:encoded:
By Ben Barry
A relationship coach says dating apps are not to blame if you're single - and reveals her four tips to find love on them.
Sabrina Zahar, 36, is a dating and relationship coach with four years of experience in the field.
She believes that dating apps aren't inherently the problem with modern-day dating and argues that users' expectations and how we use them are to blame.
Sabrina compares dating apps to casinos, saying that the house is always going to win.
She says people need to be discerning, recognize that others are at different stages of life and take breaks when dating burnout sets in.
Sabrina also said that modern life has exposed humans to more rejection than ever before, and that the reason people stay single while using the app is because of their expectations and how they are using it.
Sabrina, from Los Angeles, California, said: "The way I look at apps is kind of like a casino.
"The house is always going to win, but do I blame the casino for people having a gambling problem?
"No, because that's an internal situation that people are coming into.
"Of course, are we at a time where it's a bigger, better deal? You can swipe and find new people, absolutely.
"But I also think that we have to hold space for the fact that we are getting rejected so much more than we ever have simply by having these phones, right?
"I think what I start to see is the issues people have with the dating app are more about their expectations and how they're using the apps than it actually being the apps."
Sabrina said she was on and off the dating apps from the age of 19 until she met her partner.
While she was on the apps, Sabrina said it was more about "who was good looking" and "who was picking me".
She said: "I have been on and off the dating apps most of my adult life.
"When I first used the apps, it was more just who's good-looking? Who's picking me? And things like that.
"It wasn't actually about anybody choosing me; it wasn't me choosing people. I was more bothered about people choosing me."
Sabrina admits she "slept my way through Manhattan" and realized that she needed to "reframe" her approach to dating apps.
First, she turned off all of her notifications on the apps and turned her focus onto men who were matching with her.
"I was in a dopamine-rewarded loop with the apps. I was constantly checking and checking them," Sabrina said.
"I realized that I need to reframe not only my expectations of apps and then how I used them.
"I turned all off the notifications off; I focused on people who were matching with me so that I could see if they were people I was interested in, so I didn't feel like I was constantly overperforming.
"I didn't chat with people for more than a couple of hours; I didn't get into texting loops with people.
"I was very intentional with the way I created my profile to showcase what I was looking for, and turning off the notification allowed me to create boundaries for how often I went on."
Sabrina said buzzwords like "red flag" and "attachment style" are harming dating culture.
She argued that people are too quick to label behaviors as narcissistic, avoidant or red flags, rather than recognizing the difference between personal preferences and genuine behavioral patterns.
Sabrina said the constant analyzing can lead to hypervigilance and fear, preventing people from trusting themselves and forming genuine connections.
She said: "We hear the word narcissist thrown around as if it's the word hello, right?
"Like red flags are patterns of behavior, not just something that you don't like or the fact that they didn't open the door for you. That's not a red flag. That might just be a preference for you.
"And I think so many people, you know, it's the same: we see the avoidant and the anxious, and people are trying so hard to consciously understand that they're not actually connecting anymore.
"They're playing detective, and they're hypervigilant, and all they're doing is looking, looking, looking and scanning for safety as opposed to actually being in connection and trusting themselves."
On Oct. 15, 2026, Sabrina launched her book "Why Am I Like This?".
Sabrina says her book combines psychology with personal experiences and hopes that readers will actively implement the lessons learned from the book.
Sabrina said: "Honestly, I was the girl that needed it. I was the hot mess, right? I slept my way through Manhattan, which is a very nice way of me saying I was finding myself, right? You said jump, I said on who.
"I was the girl that had so much anxiety and core beliefs and didn't believe in myself. And once I started to do this work and realized it.
"Now here's the harsh reality: a lot of the concepts in the book, they're not revolutionary because psychology hasn't changed that much.
"Humans are still humans, but what I've done is I've created a narrative and a story throughline with my own experience as well as the clients that I've worked with for the last four years to create a very clear, oh, that's how this works.
"So the first half is why, but then we go into now. What are you going to do with it? The book won't change your life if you just read it cover to cover in 24 hours and throw it back on your shelf.
"The book will change your life if you stop, you implement, you do the exercises, you start to get curious, you hold yourself accountable, you set the boundaries, you learn fundamentally about these concepts for yourself."
HER TIPS ON HOW TO FIND LOVE ON THE APPS:
- Turn off your notifications
- Only focus on people who are matching with you
- Don't get into a texting loop with someone - unmatch if they don't make plans
- Create your profile to reflect what you're looking for

item.title: [livemint.com] Talaq-e-Hasan row: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response on plea challenging Muslim divorce practices | Today News
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singharia
item.description: The Supreme Court on Friday sought responses from the Centre and other authorities on a petition seeking uniform procedural safeguards and guidelines for all forms of 'talaq' (divorce) under Muslim personal law. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was informed by the petitioner's counsel that the plea also challenges the validity of 'Talaq-e-Hasan'. 'Talaq-e-Hasan' is a form of divorce under which a Muslim man can end his marriage by pronouncing
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court on Friday sought responses from the Centre and other authorities on a petition seeking uniform procedural safeguards and guidelines for all forms of 'talaq' (divorce) under Muslim personal law.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was informed by the petitioner's counsel that the plea also challenges the validity of 'Talaq-e-Hasan'.
'Talaq-e-Hasan' is a form of divorce under which a Muslim man can end his marriage by pronouncing the word 'talaq' once a month over three months.
The bench also tagged the petition with a separate pending plea filed by a Muslim woman challenging the validity of 'Talaq-e-Hasan' pronounced by her husband.
The fresh petition has sought a direction to the authorities to declare 'Talaq-e-Hasan' and other forms of unilateral extra-judicial 'talaq' an evil that needs to be banned.
It has also sought adequate economic and social protection for divorced women and their children affected by arbitrary forms of 'talaq'. The petition seeks these measures to be provided retrospectively and on an ongoing basis.
The petition has urged the Centre to "frame and implement uniform procedural safeguards and legally enforceable guidelines governing all forms of 'talaq'/divorce under Muslim personal law, so as to ensure fairness, reconciliation, transparency and protection of the fundamental rights of women guaranteed under Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution".
It has also sought a direction to declare Section 2 of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937, unconstitutional to the extent that it recognises and validates 'Talaq-e-Hasan' as a valid form of divorce.
The plea has further urged the Centre to frame comprehensive, gender-just and religion-neutral procedural safeguards for the dissolution of marriages, including divorce under personal laws.
It said these safeguards should be in line with Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution, which deal with equality before the law, protection against discrimination and the right to life and personal liberty.
While Article 14 pertains to equality before law, Article 15 deals with prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Article 21 pertains to protection of life and personal liberty.
The plea has sought to declare that "absence of statutory safeguards regulating polygamy under Muslim personal law, insofar as it permits a Muslim man to contract multiple marriages without ensuring equality, dignity, informed consent, financial security and constitutional protection to the existing wife/wives, is arbitrary, discriminatory and violative of Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution".
It also sought a declaration that contracting a subsequent marriage without the free, prior and informed consent of the existing spouse, by concealing or suppressing such intention, is arbitrary and unconstitutional.
Under 'Talaq-e-Hasan', a divorce gets formalised after the third utterance of the word 'talaq' in the third month if cohabitation has not resumed during this period.
However, if cohabitation resumes after the first or second utterance of talaq, the parties are assumed to have reconciled.
In 2017, the top court declared triple 'talaq', also a form of divorce prevalent among the Muslim community, as unconstitutional after finding it to be arbitrary and violative of the fundamental rights of women.
(With inputs from news agency PTI)

item.dc:creator: EDITOR
item.description: Lez take a look at the dating lives of queer women and non-binary people BY SOFIE ROOS, IMAGE BY DIVERSIFY LENS/CANVA The modern dating world is fascinating. But what is it like for queer women and non-binary people? Let’s take a look at some interesting facts that shed some light on the realities of lesbian and sapphic dating.
