item.content:encoded:
Lez take a look at the dating lives of queer women and non-binary people
BY SOFIE ROOS, IMAGE BY DIVERSIFY LENS/CANVA
The modern dating world is fascinating. But what is it like for queer women and non-binary people? Let’s take a look at some interesting facts that shed some light on the realities of lesbian and sapphic dating.
For sapphics, love often begins with friendship
According to a 2022 article, as many as 85% of queer people said that their relationship began with friendship.This older study, found that friendship is the start of many lesbian relationships. It’s obvious that the line between being just friends and being something more is much thinner for sapphics!
Dating apps play a bigger role for queer women when dating
According to a 2023 article in Pew Research Center as many as 51% of American lesbian, gay and bisexual adults have at least once used a dating app, compared to 28% of straight people. It also shows that as many as 24% of queer people have met their partner online. While the research (unfortunately) doesn’t specify the exact sapphic number, it tells us that queer women are more likely than heterosexual women to look for love online.
Queer women aren’t exclusively looking for love or sex on the apps
A review of 21 studies published in 2022 found that dating apps serve more functions than just finding a sex or romantic partner for queer women. For some sapphics, dating apps are used just as much for finding new friends, building a community, or just to feel that there are others like you.
Sapphic dating can be pure detective work
The same research found that sapphic dating involves some detective work, because queer women tend to balance between visibility and privacy while dating. Sapphics want to say “Hey, I’m into women” to the right people, and at the same time. We can be careful about how much personal information we reveal. This means that sapphics have to invest more time into thinking, “Hmmm, is this person even into queer women?”.
Sofie Roos is a licensed sexologist and relationship therapist as well as author at the Swedish sex and relationship magazine Passionerad
Love media made by and for LGBTQIA+ women and gender diverse people? Then you’ll love DIVA. We’ve been spotlighting the community for over 30 years. Here’s how you can get behind queer media and keep us going for another generation: linkin.bio/ig-divamagazine
Did you know that DIVA has now become a charity? Our magazine is published by the DIVA Charitable Trust. You can find out more about the organisation and how you can offer your support here: divacharitabletrust.com

item.title: [Boston Herald] Dear Abby: Friend goes quiet when I ask about $$ owed
item.dc:creator: Abigail Van Buren
item.description: Dear Abby: A year ago, a supposed friend of mine asked to borrow some money. Her husband had left the country so he could renew his visa to come back and work. They have kids. The wife’s car was repossessed while he was gone, and she had no way to get to work. She borrowed $3,000 from me to get her car back. A few months later, she borrowed another $1,200. I was a fool to give it to her, but I was thinking of her kids. Her husband did make it back, and they are both working now. I have texted he
item.content:encoded:
Dear Abby: A year ago, a supposed friend of mine asked to borrow some money. Her husband had left the country so he could renew his visa to come back and work. They have kids. The wife’s car was repossessed while he was gone, and she had no way to get to work. She borrowed $3,000 from me to get her car back. A few months later, she borrowed another $1,200. I was a fool to give it to her, but I was thinking of her kids.
Her husband did make it back, and they are both working now. I have texted her about the money she owes me, but she just ignores me. They had enough money to take the kids to Florida recently. How do I get past the sadness? I could really use the money back. Do I just try to let it go? — Regretful Lender
Dear Lender: You should have let it go the moment you handed the money over. When a friend asks for money, it’s rarely a loan. You should always consider it a gift — and be pleasantly surprised if they ever pay you back. Despite her inexcusable behavior, I’m sure this friend appreciates your kindness in saving her family from a distressing situation. It was a good deed, and I’m sorry you’ve been repaid with silence.
Dear Abby: I lost my brother last year to a brain aneurysm. We were very close, and I am still struggling with it. His birthday was this month, and I spent the day honoring him. However, other family members are telling me I should be “over it” by now. Am I wrong for still experiencing grief? I wasn’t aware there is a time limit. — Processing It in Alaska
Dear Processing It: Grief isn’t something that people “get over” like a case of measles or flu. When a loved one dies, the pain of that loss can remain with us to a greater or lesser degree as we adjust to the ache we feel inside. This doesn’t happen on anyone else’s timetable. Some people find joining a grief support group helpful. Perhaps you should consider it.
Dear Abby: The man I thought to be the love of my life dumped me more than 10 years ago. He’s currently going through a divorce. We have been communicating for the past four years while I’ve been in a good relationship with someone. This lost love has expressed his feelings of loss, but I can’t seem to relax and express my feelings. He will soon be divorced, and I still don’t think I should give him a chance to repeat the past. Are second chances worth the risk? — Staying in Friend Zone
Dear Staying: Second chances are sometimes worth the risk, but not always. In your case, if you are still “in a good relationship with someone” other than this ex, I’m not sure why you’d even consider rocking the boat. In fact, it may be best if you have as little contact with your ex as possible. He was no good for you then, and he can only cause trouble now.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.title: [aol.com] I Just Bought Micron Stock. Here's Why - AOL
item.dc:creator: Keithen Drury; The Motley Fool
item.description: Key Points - Micron's cyclical nature is being reduced via contracts it's signing with clients. - Tight memory chip supply conditions will worsen further before getting better. Micron Technology(NASDAQ: MU) has had a great year. It's up around 230% so far in 2026, making it the fourth-best-performing stock in the S&P 500 this year. Normally, you're supposed to buy a stock before it makes a run like that, but even after the run-up, I've decided to open a position in Micron. Why? It seems as if so
item.content:encoded:
Key Points
- Micron's cyclical nature is being reduced via contracts it's signing with clients.
- Tight memory chip supply conditions will worsen further before getting better.
Micron Technology(NASDAQ: MU) has had a great year. It's up around 230% so far in 2026, making it the fourth-best-performing stock in the S&P 500 this year. Normally, you're supposed to buy a stock before it makes a run like that, but even after the run-up, I've decided to open a position in Micron.
Why? It seems as if some of Micron's old tendencies are a thing of the past.
Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
Micron is taking steps to reduce its cyclicality
Micron makes memory chips, and the industry is known to be cyclical. There isn't much that separates one memory chip manufacturer from another, so Micron has no pricing power. You can see this in action when you think about purchasing an aftermarket thumb drive or upgrading your computer's RAM. All components are about the same, but what really matters is how cheaply you can buy them.
The market goes through demand cycles that go up and down, and when it's swinging up, times are good for Micron and its peers. But when it's a downturn, they're stuck with excess inventory and can't sell any new production, so the companies, and thus the stock, struggle.
Right now, we're amid the biggest memory-demand wave ever seen, thanks to the intensity of the artificial intelligence build-out. All available production capacity for both types of memory chips (DRAM and NAND, both of which Micron makes) is currently consumed. Every memory chip company has said demand far exceeds capacity, causing prices to skyrocket.
The fear is that this demand wave will eventually fade, leaving Micron in a much worse state than it is now. However, Micron is taking steps to reduce the severity of the eventual downturn. Micron has now signed several deals with its clients that set floor and ceiling prices for memory chips, which will stabilize the market. Furthermore, these are take-or-pay agreements, so Micron has locked in an estimated 35% of its revenue through 2030. That's a huge step toward ending the cyclicality of Micron's business, as Micron is now being treated more like a true supplier rather than just a commodity dealer.
Another development is that Micron is partnering with Nvidia to create an industry-first custom memory chip for its GPUs. This will completely shift Micron's relationship with one of the biggest memory buyers in the world, which is a great thing for Micron.
Overall, Micron has taken steps to steady its business and reduce its dependence on cyclical demand. But the question remains: When will the AI demand wave wrap up?
The AI build-out just got extended
Most investors point to 2030 as the year when the AI build-out may slow, but Micron just informed investors that a few of its clients signed deals through 2031, indicating a longer time frame. Furthermore, conditions will get worse before they get better.
Advertisement
Conditions in the memory chip market were terrible for buyers in 2026, with far more demand than supply. However, Micron's management team noted that conditions will worsen still further in 2027 and 2028 due to lack of supply. While Micron is working on getting new production capacity running, it won't be until mid-2027 and into 2028 before significant supply is available. That means another couple of years of strong revenue growth, even after how much it grew in 2026.
All of this adds up to a stock that should behave like a normal big tech stock at least through the end of the decade. While I'm a long-term investor, the market is much more short-sighted, so that gives me plenty of time to invest in a company that's bound to continue growing as the AI build-out intensifies. I'm happy to own Micron shares and believe they will be highly profitable over the next few years.
But I'll also be keeping a close eye on memory chip market conditions, and if they deteriorate, I'll be moving on from the stock.
Should you buy stock in Micron Technology right now?
Before you buy stock in Micron Technology, consider this:
The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Micron Technology wasn’t one of them. The 10 stocks that made the cut could produce monster returns in the coming years.
Consider when Netflix made this list on December 17, 2004... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you’d have $380,579!* Or when Nvidia made this list on April 15, 2005... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you’d have $1,359,789!*
Now, it’s worth noting Stock Advisor’s total average return is 931% — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 212% for the S&P 500. Don't miss the latest top 10 list, available with Stock Advisor, and join an investing community built by individual investors for individual investors.
*Stock Advisor returns as of October 15, 2026.
Keithen Drury has positions in Micron Technology and Nvidia. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Micron Technology and Nvidia. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

item.title: [courant.com] Kimberly Guilfoyle will leave Athens with ‘burn book’ on Trump family: report
item.dc:creator: Martha Ross
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle may have announced her resignation Tuesday as U.S. ambassador to Greece over an expanding corruption scandal. But so far she hasn’t left. The disgraced, short-lived diplomat has yet to vacate the elegant, official ambassador’s residence in Athens, the Daily Mail reported. Guilfoyle is “gripped by the mounting paranoia” that accompanied her desperate scramble to save her job, the Daily Mail also reported. The New York Post, however, said that the former San Francisco prosecutor
item.content:encoded:
Kimberly Guilfoyle may have announced her resignation Tuesday as U.S. ambassador to Greece over an expanding corruption scandal. But so far she hasn’t left.
The disgraced, short-lived diplomat has yet to vacate the elegant, official ambassador’s residence in Athens, the Daily Mail reported. Guilfoyle is “gripped by the mounting paranoia” that accompanied her desperate scramble to save her job, the Daily Mail also reported.
The New York Post, however, said that the former San Francisco prosecutor, conservative firebrand and one-time member of President Trump’s inner circle will soon pack up and return to the United States, probably to Florida.
And, in the wake of her dramatic downfall, Guilfoyle is considering whether to get even with members of the Trump family, including her ex-fiancé Donald Trump Jr., for appearing to turn their backs on her, the Daily Mail reported. She could do so by revealing family secrets she has recorded in a “secret burn book.”
Outside the White House Tuesday, Trump seemed eager to distance himself from his oldest son’s ex-girlfriend by denying a reporter’s assertion that she was “almost a member of his family.”
“No, she wasn’t a member of my family,” Trump said. “She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago.”
But Trump’s attempts to downplay Guilfoyle’s closeness to him and his family won’t stop her from “threatening” to release contents of the diary that Trump family insiders are dubbing “The Devil Wears MAGA,” the Daily Mail reported.
“Having her back in America would be a nightmare,” one source told the Daily Mail. “Kimberly knows where the bodies are buried. She knows the people, the secrets, the fights, the relationships. Nobody wants an angry Kimberly back home with nothing to lose.”
The 57-year-old ex-wife of California Gov. Gavin Newsom became a fixture in Trump’s inner circle after she began dating Trump Jr. in 2018, during his father’s first term. Together, Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. became a MAGA power couple and known as two of Trump’s visible supporters and fundraisers. They became engaged in late 2020 — after she gave a notoriously loud and enthusiastic speech on behalf of Trump at the 2020 Republican National Convention and before she joined the president in pushing his false claims of election fraud at his Jan. 6, 2021 rally, which led to the attack on the U.S. Capitol.
Even after Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. broke off their engagement in late 2024, and he began dating his future wife, Bettina Anderson, the former Fox News host appeared to maintain close ties to the Trump family, the Daily Mail reported. News of the breakup came around the same time that Trump nominated her to become ambassador.
But Guilfoyle’s stint as ambassador only lasted only 11 months before reporting by the Wall Street Journal and the Daily Mail revealed that she had allegedly been using her position for personal gain and engaged in alleged misconduct, in order to enjoy a lavish lifestyle while working for the U.S. government.
The alleged misconduct that garnered the biggest headlines involved claims by Erik Deters, a prominent former MAGA donor from northern Kentucky. Deters shared Signal text messages with the Wall Street Journal that showed Guilfoyle begged him to pay her $100,000 American Express bill ahead of her Senate confirmation hearing, while she promised to help him get access to Trump officials who could help him with some legal and IRS business.
The White House on Tuesday confirmed Guilfoyle was asked to resign, following reports that Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were “extremely pissed off” by her alleged antics. The State Department has launched a review of the misconduct allegations, while congressional Democrats want to launch investigations if they take power after the midterm elections.
In announcing her resignation on X, Guilfoyle expressed her “unwavering gratitude and respect” for President Trump and said she will always be his “loyal supporter.”
She also insisted the accusations were “false” and vowed to “vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity.”
But behind the scenes, insiders told the Daily Mail that there was an effort to keep Guilfoyle in her job in Athens and protect her from further scrutiny over her conduct as ambassador. That’s because, contrary to what Trump said, she was very much inside the Trump family and its political operation.
“Kimberly knows everything,” the insider said. Another source added: “Keeping Kimberly happy keeps Kimberly quiet.”
But other Trump family insiders have told the New York Post they don’t think Guilfoyle will “lash out.” That’s because she may find herself in need of a presidential pardon if her scandal leads to a criminal investigation and conviction.
“She’s gonna need a pardon and if she doesn’t behave she ain’t getting one,” a person close to the White House and the Trump family told the Post, shortly after she announced her resignation.
“If I were her, I’d probably shut up and hope for it,” a second person close to the White House told the Post.
As damaging revelations about Guilfoyle began to pile up in the Wall Street Journal and Daily Mail, Guilfoyle tried to hold onto her job and began calling administration officials and people close to the president, playing down these reports and asking for their support, the Wall Street Journal reported.
When the Journal published the story about her soliciting $100,000 from Deters, Guilfoyle allegedly told White House officials that the text messages cited by the news outlet were AI-generated.
Amid concerns over what Guilfoyle could reveal about the Trump family, friends of her ex-fiancé expressed relief that he got out of his relationship with her before these scandals hit, the Daily Mail reported. One friend even insisted that he never actually proposed to Guilfoyle. She, instead, bought herself and engagement ring and began wearing it — prompting him to allow her to release a statement announcing their engagement.
It’s believed that Trump Jr. actually ended his relationship with Guilfoyle months before they officially announced their breakup. Two months before the 2024 presidential election, the Daily Mail published photos of Trump Jr., 48, hanging out with the younger Anderson and reported that Guilfoyle had been “blindsided” by the news that he was moving on.
These Trump family insiders also said that Trump didn’t nominate Guilfoyle to be ambassador to Greece because she had expertise in European geopolitics or because she possessed particular diplomatic skills. “It solved a complicated personal problem,” an insider said. “Having her thousands of miles away worked for everyone.”
This story has been updated.

item.title: [broadway.com] Billy Crystal’s 860 Is ‘A Celebration of Life,’ Says Broadway Director Scott Ellis
item.dc:creator: Jamie Kravitz
item.description: When Billy Crystal lost his home of 46 years to the Palisades fires—the house where he raised his children, watched his grandchildren grow up and shared a life with his wife, Janice Crystal—he said, "Every inch of our house was filled with love. Beautiful memories that can't be taken away." Crystal's new one-man show, 860, is named for that address and revisits those memories. Through his signature blend of humor and heart, Crystal weaves an intimate narrative that explores loss, resilience and
item.content:encoded:
When Billy Crystal lost his home of 46 years to the Palisades fires—the house where he raised his children, watched his grandchildren grow up and shared a life with his wife, Janice Crystal—he said, "Every inch of our house was filled with love. Beautiful memories that can't be taken away." Crystal's new one-man show, 860, is named for that address and revisits those memories. Through his signature blend of humor and heart, Crystal weaves an intimate narrative that explores loss, resilience and the power of community.
For director Scott Ellis, helping Crystal bring his deeply personal story to the Broadway stage meant uncovering the universal themes within it. The Tony nominee spoke to Broadway.com about workshopping the show, early audience reactions and what he discovered along the way.
When did Billy approach you about 860?
About a year ago. He was meeting with directors and I was one of them. I got a call and I said, "Sure, it's Billy Crystal. Yes." So I met him and as he tells the story, he thought we'd be there for 20, 30 minutes. We ended up being there for two hours just talking, and him telling his story and showing me photos. I was doing Art at the time, and he came to see it and then we had more conversations and he asked me to do it.
So it's been a work in progress for a while.
We started sitting at a table reading, and then the next step was the changes. It's changed quite a lot. We went into another table read where I invited 20 people in. And then we ended up doing it live in front of an audience for two nights. We took a break, came back and did it for another five nights in front of audiences. It was sort of like a tiny out-of-town tryout for us, just to start hearing it in front of people and learning what we needed to learn.
Because it's just the two of you, did you workshop more than you normally would as a director?
I guess so. He had the story. He had this incredible beginning and ending, which I walked away [from] going, "This is perfect." Then it was just what you're doing in the middle, telling more stories. It was a great journey with him. I think most important was getting it in front of people so we could hear how people were reacting and what needed to be cut, things that worked, things that didn't work.
What made you want to get involved?
What I felt. The fact that he's ultimately talking about loss—I mean, listen, he lost everything. Their family lost everything. So I thought, how do we relate to that? I've never had that experience. But when you really delve into it, what he's talking about is loss, is the next chapter. If this had happened when he was 25, it would be a very different experience, but it happened much later in life. What are the next chapters? What are those decisions? What does stuff mean to you? I kept finding things that I thought were universal, larger questions that people who didn't go through what he and Janice went through would still be able to connect with.
Like 860, Billy's first one-man show, 700 Sundays, tackled loss. Did you discuss that work?
We didn't talk too much about it. He obviously did it and knows it well, but I wanted to focus on how we were planning to tell this story. It was very different than 700 Sundays. It's a very successful, wonderful piece of theater, so you can't pretend it didn't happen. But the focus was this story.
Why do you think Billy is so adept at telling stories of tragedy through comedy?
Well, first of all, that's who he is. He talks about how important laughter is in his life. There is the framework of something horrible that happened, but he goes back into memories of stuff that was lost and that triggers some incredibly funny stories. He's a remarkable storyteller and certainly knows comedy better than most. I think when people hear it's about the loss of his home, you think, "That's going to be a really sad evening." It's poignant. There is some sadness, but there's a great deal of joy also, of what he's discovering and him moving on. And I found that incredibly moving, that despite everything he was still saying, "We're moving on, and family is so important." His family and his wife, Janice, you see that tightness and you see that's how you can survive some of this.
How have audiences responded to Billy's storytelling?
It was our first preview, and I remember thinking, "Oh, they're connecting to this." They want to listen to this story. Visually, we've done a lot of different interesting things that I wanted to put into the storytelling. So I think that helps [make it] a theatrical experience. But it just boils down to one person who's telling a story. And I don't know if there's anyone better out there who can tell a story as well as he does. So the audience leaned in immediately, and they go on this journey from beginning to end.
"I kept finding things that I thought were universal, larger questions that people who didn't go through what he and Janice went through would still be able to connect with." —Scott Ellis
How did the visuals come together?
Billy has and had in his life a lot of photos and videos. When we first met, he showed me a chunk of them. He showed me the beginning of when the fire was coming, the discovery, and he showed me the end when he went back to see what was left. That was the framework, so in between, how do you tell the story? Well, through a lot of his photos. We have the incredible Hana Kim who's doing the projections and all the art, helping to tell that story visually. Billy would come in and say, "Oh, I have this photo," and we'd look at it, or, "I have this video." So it was just finding what was fitting in this puzzle. And then Marc Shaiman coming in and scoring it, I don't think any of us thought it would go as far as it has. But I love it and it makes it for, I think, a unique evening.
And the set is a recreation of his former home office?
We decided to bring the office in a little bit of an abstract way, meaning, it is his office, but visually it's all toned down because it's all memory. He's remembering the office. Everything he talks about, I wanted it to come from the office. And, as [scenic designer] Scott Pask said so beautifully, setting this in the office helped propel why we're telling these stories. He's such a brilliant designer. You could do it without anything, just some slides and projections, but I think we've all worked hard to make it a theatrical event.
This must be emotional for Billy as well. Why did he want to share his story this way?
I think he would have to answer this. But again, because he's a storyteller, I always ask him, "Did you think at all that one day you would tell this story?" And he said, "Yes." I thought, "That's so interesting." And again, that's who he is. But somewhere in all of this, in the back of his mind, he thought, "I'm going to tell this story," and I thought that was remarkable. It's really just a reminder of how you move forward after tragedy. I think you do it with friends and family if you're lucky to have them. I know that helped him get through this and get up to the stage.
What can audiences expect from 860?
I never say, "I hope the audience walks away with this," because everyone will have a different experience with it, you know? But I do think watching, being able to connect with someone who has gone through what he and his family went through, and that he did get on the other side of it—he's changed, all of us would be. But the fact that he's gotten on the other side and still being able to move forward, I find incredibly moving. He didn't give up where I think a lot of people could have given up and said, "I've lost it all." And so there's a celebration of life during what was the hardest thing he's ever gone through—he says that. And I think that's part of getting to know him. I think that is who he is. He keeps living, he keeps moving forward.
860 is now in previews, opening October 21 at the Imperial Theatre. Get tickets!

item.title: [The Northern Daily Leader] 'Periods of love bombing': New details revealed in Tamworth businessman's bail bid
item.dc:creator: Emma Downey
item.description: New details including revelations of alleged assaults and "love bombing" have been revealed in a Tamworth court after a well-known local businessman and athlete made a fresh bid for bail. Subscribe now for unlimited access. or signup to continue reading Benjamin Edward Burrage appeared by video link in Tamworth Local Court from Clarence Correctional Centre, before Judge Justin Peach as his solicitor Benjamin Nash made a fourth bail application. Mr Nash said his client "strongly denies" the charg
item.content:encoded:
New details including revelations of alleged assaults and "love bombing" have been revealed in a Tamworth court after a well-known local businessman and athlete made a fresh bid for bail.
Subscribe now for unlimited access.
or signup to continue reading
Benjamin Edward Burrage appeared by video link in Tamworth Local Court from Clarence Correctional Centre, before Judge Justin Peach as his solicitor Benjamin Nash made a fourth bail application.
Mr Nash said his client "strongly denies" the charges.
Reading from court documents, Judge Peach noted allegations of a history of "toxic relationships ... with periods of love bombing and periods of aggressive abuse and controlling behaviour".
The alleged behaviour is said to have been committed in 2017, with one incident also in 2013.
'Will go when I'm ready'
Judge Peach detailed allegations from July 2017 when Burrage allegedly threw objects at the complainant, and refused to leave her home.
"The accused [is alleged to have] said 'I will go when I'm ready'," the judge said.
"When the complainant threatened to call the police, [Burrage allegedly] grabbed the complainant by her hair and said: 'You want to be a c***, I'll show you what a c*** is' ... and 'You will listen when I'm talking to you'."
Judge Peach said during the incident Burrage is alleged to have pinned the complainant by her left arm, leaving her fearing it would be dislocated.
"He eventually let her go ... [but] she suffered a black eye and hair loss," the judge said.
During another incident the same year, documents detailed how Burrage had allegedly grabbed the complainant by the neck, leaving her struggling to breathe, before throwing her to the ground, resulting in an injury that required six stitches to the back of her head, Judge Peach said.
Judge Peach said the allegations were "serious".
"If [Burrage] is found guilty, full-time custody is all but inevitable given his history of domestic violence," he said.
In making his bail submission, Mr Nash said Burrage was prepared to agree to whatever release conditions the court felt appropriate to gain bail.
"[Burrage] is located at Coffs Harbour and will report daily if required," the solicitor said, noting this provided a geographical barrier for the complainant.
"He also agrees to a curfew."
Mr Nash said a family member had agreed to be a person of responsibility.
Police prosecutor Sergeant Brent Robinson opposed the bail, noting concerns over potential failure to appear, risk of further offences, danger to the community, and witness interference.
Noting the matter was "reasonably complex", and Burrage would need "significant contact" with his legal team, Judge Peach agreed appropriate conditions could mitigate risks.
Strict conditions
Judge Peach granted bail with strict conditions, including a ban on entering Tamworth, except for court appearances.
Burrage must report to Coffs Harbour Police Station daily, observe a curfew, and remain at his residence unless accompanied by a nominated person.
He must not contact, approach, or interfere with the complainant or any prosecution witnesses.
Burrage is prohibited from consuming alcohol or illicit drugs and must submit to testing. He is permitted only one mobile phone, must notify Tamworth police within 24 hours of acquiring it, allow device inspections on request, and cannot access encrypted messaging services.
The matter is listed for hearing in November.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Thursday, October 15: Pluto Goes Direct In Aquarius
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 15, 2026. Pluto stations direct in Aquarius on Thursday, reminding you that you must keep growing, even if it eventually leads you in a new direction.
Pluto is the alchemist of the zodiac and the ultimate energy of transformation. When this planet is direct, we are usually meant to take action, but Venus retrograde complicates matters. For now, start preparing for the changes you want to initiate once Venus turns direct in November. Have honest conversations and don't be afraid to share your true feelings.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Thursday, October 15, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be sure you’re hiding from anything, Aries. On Thursday, take time to reflect on how you feel around those in your life, including your romantic partner. While you may worry about being alone or what will happen if you finally acknowledge this truth, you can’t keep avoiding it forever.
Instead of only focusing on what could go wrong, open yourself up to meeting new people. You might just see that it’s you who has outgrown someone and not the other way around.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Do something different, Taurus. On Thursday, don’t be afraid to take a risk and create the kind of life that truly feels good to your soul.
Your relationship deserves your time and energy. But this also means you need to have it to give. By honoring how you feel and changing your life accordingly, you'll feel more fulfilled and have more time for love, too.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Trust what you see, dearest Gemini. As Pluto stations direct on October 15, you will have a clear direction for the future and what you want for yourself.
Pluto is the alchemist, though, so you may have to leave something or someone in the past to say yes to your future. This energy will validate your intuition and help you be brave enough to embrace change. This is all leading you on an incredible journey.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You must honor the truth, Cancer. Despite your best efforts, the relationship in your life isn’t what you thought it would become. While you’ve questioned your expectations, this isn’t about you.
On Thursday, be willing to see where this person is acting in unhealthy ways, and also how you can do better. While their behavior is on them, that doesn’t mean you can't grow in how you approach relationships.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Keep evolving, sweet Leo. Pluto is going to continue moving through Aquarius through 2043. This is a time of transformation and change in your romantic life.
Everything from who you’re attracted to to the kind of relationship you create will be up for debate. While you don’t need to know where it will all lead now, you do need to keep evolving. Choose the path of growth.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Being honest with yourself is often the most difficult thing, Virgo. It can be hard, especially when you thought that your life would look a particular way.
However, it’s important that you try to acknowledge what feels off, or even like a dead end in your life. You will have time to figure out what to do about it, but not if you keep pretending it doesn't exist. Being honest with yourself is the first step.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Pluto direct in Aquarius is a free pass to choose the love that feels right for you, Libra. Thursday's energy also reminds you that there is no limit to the kind of relationship you can create. However, you must decide that for yourself.
On October 15, you feel drawn toward untraditional dynamics. Be sure you’re not limiting yourself by what everyone else is doing.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Freedom is a state of mind, Scorpio. You may have once thought it meant being able to do whatever you want, whenever you want. But you’re now seeing it’s more about how you feel rather than your specific circumstances.
On Thursday, you may find yourself returning home, or back to someone that you once saw as the problem. Sometimes all you really need is a change of perspective to understand what matters most.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Honesty never limits what's possible, Sagittarius. While you're the truth seeker of the zodiac, that doesn’t mean you always speak the truth yourself. In fact, you often think that speaking the truth limits your options or what is possible, so you try to avoid it.
But as Pluto stations direct on Thursday, you have to be honest with everyone in your life. This is especially important if you know you’ll never be able to reciprocate their feelings.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Challenge your previous plans, Capricorn. The Aquarius energy on Thursday shows you where you’re playing small and limiting what's possible. Whether it’s by the kind of relationships you allow yourself to experience or how you live your life, you must be willing to challenge yourself.
As Pluto stations direct on October 15, embrace new ideas and opportunities. That is the only way to discover what is truly meant for you.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Let yourself discover what is meant for you, Aquarius. There is no limit to the kind of life you can live, nor what you can experience through it all. But you have to let go of any expectations and set plans.
On Thursday, start embracing a mindset of transformation. Pay extra attention to where you feel guided. While this will affect the relationships you attract, it will also impact the direction you choose to take your life.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your inner self has something important to say, dear Pisces. Just because you may be seen as the quiet one doesn’t mean your mind is operating in the same way. Your mind and intuition are always thinking, always moving, and of course, always dreaming.
Instead of dismissing your own ideas, start to listen to them. Whether it’s about someone special in your life or a redirection it feels like you’re meant to take, listening to your inner self is the start of a new chapter.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.content:encoded:
Love Horoscope Today, October 15, 2026
Love horoscope for October 15, 2026, brings emotional clarity, deep conversations, and opportunities to strengthen relationships across all zodiac signs.
Love Horoscope Today, October 15, 2026: The day will bring emotional clarity, deep conversations, and opportunities to strengthen romantic relationships. Aries, Taurus, and Capricorn are encouraged to communicate openly and seek stability in love. Gemini, Cancer, and Pisces will enjoy affectionate moments and emotional satisfaction. Leo and Sagittarius may face insecurities, but mutual effort can lead to harmony.
Virgo and Scorpio will find joy in deep connections and enjoyable times spent together. Libra may face temporary distance in love, but will also have a chance for a fresh start. Aquarius will see resolution of conflicts and a renewed sense of gratitude towards love. Overall, this is a meaningful day to nurture understanding and intimacy.
Aries Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that your partner’s wisdom will give you more security and confidence. You may need to strengthen your relationship with your partner. Today is the time to share your concerns with your beloved and get them to understand you. There should be more understanding and respect in your relationship. Your partner’s wisdom will help bring stability and happiness to your relationship.
Taurus Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you have to take time to clarify your feelings with your partner. You have to pay attention to your behavior and also try to understand your partner. Spending time taking care of your family can be very important for you today. There may be some auspicious work in your house, which will bring happiness to your family. If you are unmarried, you may get good marriage proposals.
Gemini Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s love horoscope for Gemini people will be above the level. Today, there can be a lot of happiness in your love relationship. Your relationship with your partner will be very good. You will get a chance to spend a lot of good time with your love. Your partner will be very happy and satisfied with you. You will get a chance to have a very good conversation with your beloved.
Cancer Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, the love life of Cancer people will be very wonderful. You can feel full of love and excited. There may be some challenges regarding children in married life. You should take special care of the health of your children. Children’s health should be a priority for you. You may get a special opportunity to spend time with your children, which will strengthen your relationship.
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today can be a little worrying for Leo people in terms of love. You may feel that you are not getting the support of your spouse. But you have to keep in mind that your spouse will leave no stone unturned to make you happy. Today, you will get the support of your spouse in every work, and there will be a good conversation between you two. Today, you may get a chance to have dinner with your spouse. Both of you can get a good place to spend time.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that you will be able to know each other better and experience joy in this new relationship. Your love life will be better than before, and you will be able to make all the decisions together. So treat your partner with love and understanding today, this will give you happiness and satisfaction in your relationship. Today, you will get a chance to know more about your love, and you will be able to make your relationship even stronger.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope will be full of worries for you. Today, you may face some problems in your love relationship. You should talk more to your partner and reduce the distance between you and them. If you want to get married today, then this is the best time for you. There can be a new beginning in your life, and this day can also be favorable for your family relationships.
Scorpio Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today your love life will be very good. You will be very happy to spend time with your partner, and talking to them will also be fun. Your romantic and sensitive attitude will also attract your partner, and a deep bond will be formed between you two. Today you will get a chance to spend more time with your family. There will be an atmosphere of happiness and prosperity in your home.
Sagittarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, there can be an atmosphere of anxiety in your love life. You may feel that your love is going away from you and your relationship is becoming unstable. During this time, you have to understand your feelings and try to maintain communication with your partner. If you want to stay together, then you have to express your feelings openly.
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today there will be some anxiety and turmoil in your love life. You may feel that there is some ambiguity in your relationship with your partner, and you may fear that your love is going away from you. During this time, you should talk to your partner and solve your problems with them. Instead of suppressing your feelings, talk to them and share your concerns with them. You need to support each other with your partner, and you also need to express your feelings.
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today is a good day for Aquarius people. The ongoing dispute with your spouse will be resolved today, and you will be able to express your thoughts openly in conversation. Today, your love will rise from above as well as from below, and you will have to handle your love. You have to take some time to understand your love and relationships. Today, consider your love as an important part of your life and try to increase happiness and your relationship with it.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, the state of love will be at a high level in your zodiac sign. This can be an auspicious day for you when you will get the right time to express your feelings in front of your love. There can be happiness and stability in your relationship. To understand your partner’s feelings better, you should share your heart with them. Today can be a very good day for you when you are ready to make your love a part of your life.
Quick Answers
According to Ganesha on October 15, 2026, Aries will find that their partner’s wisdom brings more security, confidence, and stability to the relationship. It is encouraged to share concerns openly and foster mutual understanding and respect.

item.title: [The Mary Sue] Black woman changes her race to white on Hinge. Then her dating options completely change
item.dc:creator: Umme Tun Nessa
item.description: Black woman changed her race to white on Hinge and suddenly started matching with investors, advisors and athletes: ‘That racist’ Finding a good match on dating apps can be frustrating. But one Black woman claims her options improved almost overnight after she changed her race to white on Hinge. The difference left her questioning how the app was treating her. Before the change, she struggled to find men she wanted to date. Suddenly, her feed was filled with Harvard graduates, investors, and ath
item.content:encoded:
Black woman changed her race to white on Hinge and suddenly started matching with investors, advisors and athletes: ‘That racist’
Finding a good match on dating apps can be frustrating. But one Black woman claims her options improved almost overnight after she changed her race to white on Hinge. The difference left her questioning how the app was treating her.
Before the change, she struggled to find men she wanted to date. Suddenly, her feed was filled with Harvard graduates, investors, and athletes. Interestingly, some of those men were Black.
A video shared by TikTok account @wrekkkii, which has gained 28.6K views, captured the woman’s experiment. While she encouraged other Black women to try the same trick, commenters weren’t convinced. Some questioned whether those new options were actually any better.
Then came the questions
The woman explained that she had seen another person recommend the trick a few months earlier. The advice was for Black women to identify as white on dating apps to improve their dating options. Curious whether it would work, she decided to test it herself.
Her Hinge profile originally identified her as Black, although she had hidden that information from other users. According to her, the men appearing in her feed were mostly drug dealers, scammers, and people she had no interest in dating.
Then she changed her race to white, and the difference surprised her. “Suddenly I’m getting Harvard graduates, real estate investors, financial advisors, um, football players, black men,” she recalled.
She was particularly surprised by the attractive Black men appearing in her feed. “Where were y’all?” she asked, wondering why she hadn’t encountered those profiles before.
“Shit is that deep and that racist,” she wrote in the video’s caption, expressing her frustration with the difference in her dating options.
For the woman, the experiment raised questions about racial bias in online dating. She encouraged other Black women to try changing their race, arguing that dating apps weren’t taking them seriously.
However, commenters pointed out a potential problem with her advice. Even if the change made more desirable profiles appear, it didn’t necessarily mean those men would be interested in dating her.
Several people suggested that the men appearing in her feed might have set their preferences to exclude Black women. If that were the case, changing her race could make their profiles visible without changing their actual preferences.
“Why would you want men who are seeking white women?” one commenter asked. Another responded, “Those are men that don’t want you. Disregard them and move on.”
Others felt the experiment reflected broader dating challenges Black women face, particularly when racial preferences influence who gets considered as a potential partner.
“that’s because those men have clearly removed black women as their preferences and it’s time for black women to wake up and see it,” one person wrote.
Another pointed out that seeing someone on a dating app doesn’t guarantee romantic interest. “Those men selected to be shown white women so it probably won’t change your odds.”
One commenter raised safety concerns about appearing to men who may have deliberately excluded Black women. “My concern is if those men have their settings set to intentionally filter out black women, will changing those settings make your profile visible to some men who could be a threat to your safety,” they wrote.
Changing her race may have brought different men into her feed, but it doesn’t guarantee better dating prospects. After all, finding someone worth dating should depend on genuine compatibility, not having to pretend to be someone else.
Have a tip we should know? [email protected]

item.title: [Yahoo] $1.5 Billion Lost in Romance Scams as Fake Profile Views on Dating Apps Soar More Than 700 Percent
item.dc:creator: Brian Particelli
item.description: Be careful when swiping right, because there's a very good chance the other person could be a scammer. Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire and Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee released the results of their bipartisan congressional investigation into dating apps this week — and the findings are pretty shocking. The investigation looked into romance scams on Match Group platforms, which include Tinder, Hinge, Match, Plenty of Fish and more. Per a press release from Ha
item.content:encoded:
Be careful when swiping right, because there's a very good chance the other person could be a scammer.
Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire and Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee released the results of their bipartisan congressional investigation into dating apps this week — and the findings are pretty shocking.
The investigation looked into romance scams on Match Group platforms, which include Tinder, Hinge, Match, Plenty of Fish and more. Per a press release from Hassan's office, views of scam profiles on Tinder alone increased by more than 700 percent between May 2024 and December 2025.
According to the committee's findings, Match Group "knew that Tinder was more likely to show a profile if it belonged to a scammer or other bad actor rather than a regular user." The report also says nearly 1.5 million scammers or bad actors on Tinder and Hinge matched with another user — and nearly 500,00 of those accounts exchanged contact information with others.
The scams usually involve fraudsters forming virtual relationships over the apps, asking their victims for money or gifts. They're now considered one of the leading forms of fraud in the U.S., with the Federal Trade Commission reporting nearly $1.5 billion in losses last year to romance scams — which Hassan's office says is a nearly 650% increase since 2019.
While Hassan said Match Group has "made progress in combating scammers," she added that it "shouldn't have taken so long" for action.
"There's still more that Match needs to do," she said in a statement.
Among those improvements is a new video verification process, Fact Check, on Tinder, which Match Group said has reduced user interactions with scammers by more than 70 percent. It was deployed nationwide back in December 2025.
After the committee's "continued" followups with Match Group about their outdated AI models, they also introduced a new model in early 2026 that is said to better detect fraudsters.
In a statement to NBC News, Match Group's senior vice president of trust and safety Yael Roth said the company "is grateful the Committee recognized our significant advancements to protect our users against romance scams."
"That said, the report mischaracterizes both the historical scale of our investment and the work already completed. Alongside our engagement with the Committee over the past year, we've made the largest safety advancements in Match Group's history," the statement continued. "Trust and Safety is a foundational priority, and we intend to continue leading the industry in building tools that promote authentic, safe connections."
In September, Congress passed the Romance Scam Prevention Act, which Hassan explained will require dating apps to notify people if they've interacted with any scammers who were later banned. President Donald Trump still needs to sign it into law.
Hassan also introduced the ReportScams.gov Act, which aims to create a "centralized portal where Americans can report scams and get help."
Read More From First for Money
This story $1.5 Billion Lost in Romance Scams as Fake Profile Views on Dating Apps Soar More Than 700 Percent first appeared on First for Money. Follow First for Money on Yahoo so you don't miss what's coming next.

item.content:encoded:
Why singletons are fall-ing in love in the autumn (and snubbing dating apps)
As the evenings begin to close in and the long, hot summer is consigned to memory, some of us may find ourselves contemplating another seasonal change.
There may even be a biological component. Testosterone levels in men fluctuate seasonally and tend to be higher during winter, potentially influencing the motivation to seek a sexual partner.
Despite all this talk of coupling up, however, Graff points out that the clue is in the word ‘season’. Cuffing traditionally refers to a temporary liaison during the winter months rather than the pursuit of a long-term relationship. So perhaps hold off on clearing him a drawer.
The figures from Your Friend, My Friend point towards the latter. Keating says 82% of attendees meet somebody they are attracted to at an event, while more than 70% have gone on a date afterwards. Increasingly, she says, people are treating singles events as a genuine alternative to apps rather than something to try once for the novelty.
Among Gen Z, however, she is seeing the opposite: Men are increasingly proactive and enthusiastic about attending, and men’s tickets are now selling faster than women’s. A speed dating event for ages 22-33 run by Your Friend, My Friend in Dublin this week tellingly had the sign ‘Men Sold Out’ up.

item.content:encoded:
You reread a text 14 times to try and understand the tone the other person used. They didn’t text “good morning” like they usually do, and now you’re wondering if you said something wrong. Your partner was unusually quiet during dinner, and you’re already preparing yourself for the “we need to talk” conversation. Sound familiar? These are all signs of an anxious attachment style.
The frustrating part is that even when everything in your relationship is going fine, it’s hard to stop worrying that something’s wrong. You might find yourself feeling insecure, needing extra reassurance, or assuming the worst over something small. Sometimes, those anxious attachment triggers can make a completely normal situation feel like a MUCH bigger problem.
Recognizing these patterns isn’t about diagnosing yourself. It’s about understanding why certain situations bother you so much and figuring out how to handle those feelings when they come up.
We’ve rounded up a few Dear Media episodes where hosts and guests talk about anxious attachment, what it looks like in relationships, and how to start working through it. We’re sharing some of their most helpful advice below, without all the complicated psychology terms.
What Is Anxious Attachment and How It Affects Your Relationships
If you’ve ever spent an entire afternoon worrying about a text that went unanswered, you probably know how exhausting that can be. And when it happens regularly, even little things like a change in someone’s tone or a bit of emotional distance can leave you questioning where you stand.
Learning about anxious attachment styles can help you understand why you react this way, especially if you have a strong fear of rejection or find yourself constantly looking for reassurance. It can also help you recognize which habits might be making navigating relationships harder than it needs to be.
On Girls Gotta Eat, neuroscientist Andrew Huberman explained that attachment styles are way older and go much deeper than dating. As an infant you come into the world helpless, and attachments are how we first learn whether or not our anxiety can be soothed.
Those brain areas and chemicals used in infant attachment don’t magically change. They’re the same ones we use in adulthood for romantic attachment. In other words, your reactions are literally how you were wired.
A quick but important note:
What Is Anxious Attachment Style?
An anxious attachment style is a pattern in relationships where you want to feel close to someone else, but you’re worried that they’ll lose interest or eventually leave. And we’re not talking about occasionally feeling insecure in your relationship. Almost everyone experiences that from time to time.
The difference is how often those worries come up and how much they affect you. Maybe you need your partner to reassure you that everything’s okay, even when they haven’t given you a reason to think otherwise. Or you start overthinking every little interaction because you’re worried something has changed. When that becomes a regular part of your relationships, it could be a sign of anxious attachment.
On Girls Gotta Eat, Huberman described how researchers first learned about attachment styles in babies using the “strange situation” setup. This is where a caregiver leaves the room and comes back.
The interesting part is not how the child reacts when the caregiver leaves, but how they react when the caregiver comes back. Anxiously attached babies get agitated. They don’t even feel fully better when the caregiver does come back. Take this situation and swap it: you’re the baby and your partner’s the caregiver. (Weird, we know. Stick with us here.) But basically, it’s the SAME situation.
Attachment styles shape how people respond to emotional closeness, to perceived rejection, and to uncertainty in general. On Girls Gotta Eat, Dr. Amir Levine described attachment as a surveillance system. It’s almost like there’s a thread between you and the person you’re attached to. When they’re “there,” you can tug the thread and feel they’re holding onto it. But when they leave and the thread snaps, it’s unsettling.
Signs of Anxious Attachment Style
Common signs of anxious attachment style include:
- Having a strong fear of rejection or abandonment, even when a partner hasn’t given you a reason to worry
- Needing your partner to regularly reassure you that everything is okay
- Seeking constant connection and getting anxious when someone takes too long to respond
- Overthinking little things, like a shorter text than usual or canceled plans
- Having a hard time calming yourself down without reassurance from your partner
- Sending multiple texts, starting arguments, or pulling away to see if your partner will react
- Struggling to focus on other things when you’re worried about where you stand in your relationship
When you basically have ALL of these warning signs going off at once, it’s exhausting. It’s also confusing. But this isn’t a “you’re stuck this way forever” kind of thing. You can intentionally work on the type of attachment you have in relationships.
How Anxious Attachment Style Affects Relationships
Emotional Triggers Hijack Your Day
With an anxious attachment style, your nervous system pretty much treats small disruptions like total emergencies. You could’ve had the most amazing weekend with your partner and everything could’ve gone perfectly as planned. But come Monday morning, they forget to text you when they wake up. For an anxious person? That signals the beginning of the end.
The anxious person is SO sensitive to potential danger in a relationship that they feel relationships can be very fragile. A forgotten text can’t just be an accident; it HAS to mean something. In short, anxious attachment triggers don’t wait for actual evidence to sound the nervous system alarms.
Seeking Constant Reassurance Can Push Partners Away
If you’re the type of person who looks for constant contact and reassurance, it can unintentionally create the exact emotional distance you’re afraid of.
On The Bossticks, Harvard-trained Behavioral Scientist Logan Ury actually broke down a super common pattern: Anxious and avoidant attachments mixed together. When an anxious partner pairs with an avoidant one, you get the anxious-avoidant loop. One chases while one pulls away, reinforcing each other’s triggers. The anxious person’s story is “I’m going to chase you and you’re going to pull away,” and the avoidant person’s story is “you’re going to smother me.”
Ironically though, Ury says that people get addicted to this cycle of not knowing. She compared it to a slot machine, which is exactly how people start to confuse anxiety for chemistry.
You Confuse Intensity With Connection
If you have an anxious ambivalent attachment style, you might find yourself drawn to someone who’s hot and cold because you never really know where you stand with them. Remember the slot machine example we mentioned earlier? Ury brought up research from psychologist B.F. Skinner to explain why that unpredictability can make it so hard to stop seeking someone’s attention. Partial reward schedules get us hooked to inconsistent people.
People should be with someone consistent and securely attached who shows up, but they think that is boring and get drawn to the person where they do not know when they will get attention.
It Can Make You Lose Yourself
When you’re constantly worried about keeping your partner happy or making sure they won’t leave, it’s easy to start putting your own needs aside. You might find yourself changing your plans, avoiding certain conversations, or agreeing to things you don’t actually want to do.
But having an insecure attachment doesn’t mean you’ll always feel this way. On Girls Gotta Eat, Huberman explained that attachment patterns can change over time, and the person you’re in a relationship with can make a difference, too.
If some of these behaviors sound familiar, our guide to unhealthy relationship signs can help you recognize other patterns worth paying attention to.
How to Heal Anxious Attachment Style
When we say “healing an anxious attachment style,” we’re not saying it’s a guaranteed cure. Instead, it’s about building healthier ways to respond to insecurity, uncertainty, and relationship stress. None of this is “fix yourself in a weekend.” It is a practice. Here is where the experts actually agree.
Learn to Self-Soothe
Across each conversation we’ve included with experts, they tend to agree that self-soothing is essential. If you can calm yourself down, you’re essentially not giving someone else control over your entire nervous system.
Huberman explained this perfectly in Girls Gotta Eat. He used tools like getting your sleep right and using breathing to relax as examples. When you feel overwhelmed, these tools basically help you figure out if you’re the problem, or if it’s actually your partner.
When a wave of anxious attachment triggers hits, a few slow breaths before you fire off a reaction genuinely helps.
Get Clear, and Ask for Consistency
Levine’s whole approach is asking for consistency instead of playing games. He told the story of a woman who, after a second date, simply told the guy that it mattered to her that people in her life be consistent, available, and responsive, and that if he could not do that, it would not work.
He said when she put it that way, it did not feel like such a huge ask, and years later they were married with kids.
The magic word, he stressed repeatedly, is not frequency, it is consistency. This is also where setting boundaries is HUGE. You have to learn to stand up for yourself, because there really is a difference between boundaries and attachment styles.
Our guide to how to set boundaries in a relationship without being controlling walks you through this step by step.
Build a Secure Support System
You don’t need ALL of your needs met by one single person. Each expert in the episodes above brings up how important it is to surround yourself with steady, reliable people. This way, when you are seeking support, you have a whole village instead of just one person.
When your sense of safety comes from multiple secure connections, chances are you won’t spiral over one person’s slow reply. That sense of community ultimately comes down to protecting your own nervous system.
Consider Couples Therapy or a Secure Partner
A secure attachment style can seriously be contagious. Levine described how being with his securely attached partner helped him break his own anxious patterns over time.
For couples stuck in the anxious-avoidant loop, couples therapy can be a HUGE help. Both partners eventually learn how to deescalate instead of reinforcing each other’s fears. The goal is a healthier relationship. Emotional closeness feels safe rather than threatening, and emotional distance doesn’t feel like abandonment.
Get Curious Before You React
Instead of treating every uncertain moment as proof that something is going wrong, practice asking what’s actually going on. This slowly teaches you whether your instinct is right or if your internal radar is freaking out for no reason.
It’s also how you build real intimacy! If you want a little inspiration for getting vulnerable, try our list of vulnerable questions to ask your partner.
You’re Not Stuck With an Anxious Attachment Style
TL;DR: Anxious attachment is a consistent fear of being abandoned that turns small moments into big spirals. But it’s a pattern, and you can always change a pattern. When it comes to navigating relationships with an anxious attachment, learn to self-soothe, ask for consistency, and build a secure support system around you.
For more episodes like these, including our roundup of the best podcasts for couples, check out the entire Dear Media network! With over 100 top-rated pop culture, entertainment, and lifestyle podcasts hosted by today’s most talked-about creators, there’s so much you have to catch up on.

item.dc:creator: Kate Rose
item.description: Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Wednesday, October 14: The Moon Opposes Retrograde Uranus Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 14, 2026. The Sagittarius Moon opposes retrograde Uranus in Gemini, reminding you that falling in love isn’t the end of the story. It's only the beginning if you allow it to be. item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Wednesday, October 14: The Moon Opposes Retrograde Uranus
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 14, 2026. The Sagittarius Moon opposes retrograde Uranus in Gemini, reminding you that falling in love isn’t the end of the story. It's only the beginning if you allow it to be.
Despite your best efforts, every relationship often finds itself in a rut. Life gets busy, and romance isn't always top of mind. On Wednesday, as the Sagittarius Moon opposes retrograde Uranus in Gemini, it may feel like everything is breaking apart. But this doesn’t mean you’re actually breaking up. In fact, this is a chance to break free from any ruts and choose to keep growing together.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Wednesday, October 14, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
If you want something, ask for it, Aries. You may be waiting to see if the person you’re with will suggest shifting your relationship towards something new. But if this is what you want, you must make it known.
On Wednesday, you are reminded that if you’re craving something new in your relationship, you should be the one to ask for it. Your partner isn't a mind reader, even if you wish they were at times.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Give what you hope to receive, Taurus. What you want from love has changed. And while you may still be getting used to this new truth, know that it’s not going to go anywhere.
That being said, greater depth and meaning don’t just happen in a relationship. On Wednesday, take time to reflect on how you can shift the energy in your connection instead of just putting it all on the other person.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You don’t have to stay, Gemini. Of course you love your partner, and you may even still want a life with them. But that doesn’t mean you have to stay.
You don’t owe them anything, nor do you need any more proof to listen to your inner self. Wherever it feels like you’re being guided, on Wednesday, it's time to start listening.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
A little change goes a long way, Cancer. You may be feeling antsy in your life and relationship at the moment. But this isn’t about the person you’re with.
On Wednesday, start creating space for spontaneity. You’ve been so enmeshed with plans and obligations that you forgot to create room for romance too.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You’re allowed to be happy where you are, Leo. While seeking new experiences is a part of who you are, don't forget to appreciate where you are now.
If you're not careful, you can live your life with such a fear of missing out that you don’t acknowledge how special someone is to you. On Wednesday, don’t make the mistake of underestimating your feelings.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You don’t always have to do more, Virgo. Let yourself learn what it means to simply be. Whether you are in a relationship or single, learning how to be present is key for both romance and your own personal journey.
To just be means you’re not always distracting yourself with work or frivolous dates. It means you’re comfortable with yourself and feel like you’re already enough. This is the key to a love that will last.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Make an offer they can’t refuse, Libra. But if they do, know that it is your sign to do it on your own.
On Wednesday, you feel inspired to finally approach your partner about an idea or dream you’ve been having. You’ve been nervous about where this would lead, but it's finally the right time. Regardless of what they say, this is something you need to let yourself experience.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can do anything, Scorpio. You don’t need to define yourself based on what you have or what you’ve accomplished. On Wednesday, let yourself finally see just how worthy and amazing you already are.
Truly embodying your worth changes everything, but no one can do it for you. Take time to practice affirmations and treat yourself kindly. Know that you deserve everything you desire.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your feelings are valid, Sagittarius. Instead of wasting time trying to talk yourself out of your feelings or make them more convenient, you're urged to listen to them on Wednesday.
This may mean preparing for a shift in your romantic life. It could change who you're with or even where you live. But the only way to finally feel settled is to listen to your heart and see where these feelings lead.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
There is a purpose for your path, Capricorn. Leave behind the comfort zone of logic and let yourself acknowledge the unique purpose you have in this lifetime.
You are a deeply intuitive individual, but you don’t always give yourself credit for that. Instead of relying solely on logic or just going through the motions, be willing to honor your intuition, no matter where it leads.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Seek out those who inspire you, Aquarius. On Wednesday, open yourself up to new connections and experiences. Rather than thinking you have to be a certain kind of partner or giving your loyalty to those who haven’t earned it yet, let yourself be inspired by life.
Be sure you’re not holding yourself back simply because of how you think you should be acting. You truly have the freedom to live the life you truly wish for. Let go of any expectations and start living for you.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Follow your purpose, Pisces. You will always find love, but you must make sure you're truly honoring your purpose no matter where it takes you.
You can make your dreams come true and still have that loving and safe home you desire. Wednesday helps you see that it’s not about choosing one path or the other but believing you can have both. After all, your home is what allows you to follow your purpose.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.content:encoded:
As the Sun and Uranus separate, moods can shift rapidly. Maybe someone will admit to a new feeling or a message will come out of the blue. A relationship that seemed set in stone can also suddenly take a different direction.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
Be prepared for the unexpected, but don’t react to every change. Sun-Uranus energy can be exciting, yet it can make emotions feel unsettled for a while. Couples may want more freedom or a break from routine. Singles might receive an unexpected call or notice a connection gaining momentum. Take in new information before making a major emotional decision based on one unusual event.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Taurus: You could feel unsafe if someone suddenly changes how they act. Don’t assume that the relationship is unstable. Take a little time before you decide what the change really means.
Leo: You may be surprised if someone asks for more independence or questions a plan. Don’t take it as rejection immediately. They may simply need space to express what they want differently.
Scorpio: You might feel very strongly about an unexpected message. Resist the temptation to check every detail immediately.
Listen to what is being said before adding your own fears into the mix.
Cancer: Your partner's mood swings can leave you feeling unsure. Try not to soak up their irritability. Once the immediate stress has passed, clear space for a calm conversation.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Aquarius: The changing tone of the day can work in your favour. A chance conversation, an unusual meeting or a sudden confession could lead to an exciting romantic possibility.
Gemini: An unexpected conversation can spark your interest when you least expect it. Be open to people who are not your usual type.
Aries:
Love may move forward when you bring bold energy. A direct invitation or unexpected romantic move could start something new.
Sagittarius:
A change of plan could improve your love life. Singles may meet someone at an impromptu event, while couples can enjoy a new experience together.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Virgo: A sudden change can be difficult to understand, but an open mind can help you stay grounded.
Libra: People in relationships need some space.
Capricorn: If you discover something that surprises you, think it through before making a long-term choice.
Pisces: Learning something new about your emotions might feel intense, but it may take some time to fully comprehend what it means.
Lucky Action of the Day
You do not have to define a sudden change immediately. Let the next few developments show whether it is truly a turning point.

item.content:encoded:
‘Love Is Blind: Netherlands’ Season 1: Which Couples Are Still Together?
As a Dutch girlie who is completely obsessed with Love Is Blind, I couldn’t wait to get my hands on the newest spinoff in the franchise. And let’s be honest, Love Is Blind is already a global phenomenon. With the Boston season debuting on October 14, and Love Is Blind: France and Love Is Blind: Japan stealing our hearts before it, the franchise is showing no signs of slowing down.
But I had a feeling the Dutch installment would be particularly juicy. Why? My people are known for being brutally direct, and boy, did they deliver with the inaugural season of Love Is Blind: Netherlands.
The newest entry into the Love Is Blind franchise brought hot singles from Amsterdam to Maastricht (it’s a ridiculously small country, okay?) together to blind date in the famous pods. After plenty of love triangles — and even a few love squares — we ended up with five engaged couples heading off to Zanzibar, because fun fact, the Dutch absolutely love Zanzibar.
We also got a racist comment that was trending across social media, an embarrassing meltdown from a grown man, and, naturally, some unexpected talk about lizards.
So, who actually found love behind the pods? Which FOUR couples have broken up since the trip? Which new couple joined the mix? It’s a record-breaking season, honestly. Let’s find out who is still engaged on Love Is Blind: Netherlands Season 1.
Love Is Blind: Netherlands, Season 1, Episodes 1-8, Streaming Now, Netflix
Love Is Blind: Netherlands, Season 1, Episodes 9, October 14, Netflix
