item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Tuesday, October 13: Love Yourself First
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 13, 2026. Lilith in Capricorn squares retrograde Neptune in Aries, reminding you to love yourself.
Too often, you search in another for what you must give or do for yourself. While you deserve someone to support you and be there for you as you heal, they can't do the work for you. On Tuesday, focus on self-exploration and self-love. Know that you don't need rescuing. Only you can save yourself.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Tuesday, October 13, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You are capable of creating the life you dream of, Aries. It’s normal to want to share your life with the person you love. But don't for one second think that means you're incapable of creating it for yourself.
On Tuesday, be sure you’re making plans and following through on your own dreams. Don't wait for a relationship to make them all a reality.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Do what resonates, dear Taurus. It’s understandable that you want to wait to make plans until you know for certain which way that special person is going to move. However, by doing that, you’re holding up your fate.
Understand that choosing to move forward doesn’t necessarily mean this relationship will end. What's most important is that you follow what feels authentic for you.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can only give so many chances, Gemini. You may be hesitant to leave a connection because of the sense of stability it brings to your life. However, you can't give this person too many chances, either.
Having boundaries is important, as is creating your own stability. Don't let yourself be reliant upon another person, even one you love.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Become what you’re seeking, Cancer. At first, it may seem counterintuitive to become what you are looking for in another. But that will actually help you attract it.
On Tuesday, start creating the life you desire for yourself. Don't wait for a relationship to make you happy. You will never regret giving yourself what you dream of.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can do this, sweet Leo. Just because you feel like a better version of yourself when you’re in a relationship doesn’t mean you can’t feel that way on your own.
Tuesday reminds you that you have to be willing to love and care for yourself and the details of life. Not only will this help you when you're single, but you’ll also be a better partner when you find your forever love.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t be so afraid of breaking the rules, Virgo. You don’t need to live your life the same way everyone else does. But that also means you don’t need a guarantee in order to make a decision.
If you’ve been hanging on to a relationship that’s already over, then you need to ask yourself why. It’s OK to be single. You might even enjoy it.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Create what you need, dear Libra. The energy on Tuesday calls you to focus on a very important part of your life: your home.
You've fantasized about creating your home with someone you love, both for yourself and as part of healing your inner child wounds. However, you must make sure you’re not accepting less just because you can’t imagine doing it on your own. Home doesn’t have to look a certain way, because how you feel matters most.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t worry about how your truth lands, Scorpio. You are one of the zodiac signs that represents themes of truth and transformation. That is being intensified on Tuesday.
Venus retrograde in your zodiac sign is making you see things differently. This also means you can’t worry about how others take your truth. Don’t censor yourself or feel like you have to sweeten it. Simply say how you feel and trust the process.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Love doesn’t make you worthy, Sagittarius. No matter how incredible your partner is, your relationship doesn't determine your worth. Even if the person you love comes with a certain status or accolades, you aren't special only for being with them.
On Tuesday, you need to see that your self-worth isn't tied to your relationship status. That is how you can see how powerful you really are. Even if you were to break up tomorrow, you'd still be just as worthy.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t just cut and run, Capricorn. You tend to do that in relationships. Whether it’s because you’re scared or you feel too vulnerable, escaping is your preferred coping mechanism. But if you’re always running, you’re never going to find the love you desire.
On Tuesday, make an effort to learn to work through your uncomfortable feelings. Be present for the process with the person you care about.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You must listen to your intuition, Aquarius. You are a highly spiritual zodiac sign; however, that doesn’t mean you always listen to that inner voice.
On Tuesday, don't wait for permission or a sign from someone in your life to listen to what you already know. Being able to trust your intuition doesn’t come from your relationship, but from the bond you forge with yourself.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You don’t need others to agree with your choices, Pisces. But you also don’t need to go in the opposite direction just to make a point. While you should be sure the choices you’re making are yours, that doesn’t mean your friends don't have some valid points about your romantic life.
Instead of dismissing them just because you don’t like to be told what to do, you may want to listen. After all, they might see what you are missing.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

Love Horoscope Today, October 13, 2026
Love horoscope for October 13, 2026, highlights a joyful and socially vibrant day for all zodiac signs, encouraging fun, emotional openness, and connection.
Love Horoscope Today, October 13, 2026: Today’s horoscope shows a joyful and socially vibrant day for all zodiac signs in terms of love. Aries, Gemini, and Cancer are encouraged to go out and have fun with their partner, while for Taurus, this is the perfect time to propose. Leo and Sagittarius should express their desires and feelings openly, which will deepen their relationship.
Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio will experience emotional closeness and mutual support, which will strengthen their relationship. Capricorn and Aquarius are reminded to enjoy the present, enjoying affection and attention without thinking too much. Pisces will experience peace and satisfaction in their current relationship. Overall, love flows smoothly through shared joy, connection, and emotional openness.
Aries Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says consider hitting the dance floor with your partner today, or if you are single, consider going out with some friends or family, as social activities are going to be a lot of fun today. Leave your worries, pressures of work or studies behind, and head out for some fun. Enjoy it!
Taurus Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that at this time, your partner and you connect completely; you haven’t been this happy in a long time. So, if you have been thinking of proposing to your partner for some time now, today is a great day to go ahead and propose. Chances are that your proposal will be accepted today.
Gemini Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today you should not allow yourself and your partner to stay at home for another evening; go out and have a lot of fun. Do something fun like taking a dance class or watching a movie together. You will find that this breaks the monotony and gives you both something to talk about again.
Cancer Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today you can go on a small outing out of town. It will be great to reconnect with your partner and have some fun, and you will feel refreshed. Your partner will shower you with love and affection, which will make you feel loved. If you have left the kids with their grandparents, don’t feel guilty, they are having a good time even after you left!
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today is the day to focus on what you want from your relationship. Express your desires to your partner and get positive results! Right now, you want to spend some time alone with your partner, just relax in each other’s arms. If you are still looking for love, you should keep your eyes and options open. You will find that the one who is made for you is always with you.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that at this time, your partner will support you in everything you do. When you ask them for more support, make sure you appreciate the support they have given you during difficult times. Always be ready to respond to this loving attitude and cooperation immediately.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today you may go on a trip to meet your partner, or both of you may go on a trip together. You will get a chance to spend time alone, leaving behind friends and family. This will be a great opportunity to understand each other’s busy lives and remember why you fell in love with this person in the first place. You will enjoy a warm and loving evening together.
Scorpio Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that your kindness and sensitivity are at their peak, and your partner responds to you. You will find that the more charming and confident you are, the more your partner will respond to you emotionally and physically. Be both a good speaker and a good listener today, and you will see your relationship reach new heights.
Sagittarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that your relationship with your partner is cordial, and you get loving support in everything you do. You are going through a phase of mutual harmony. Share your feelings with your beloved, and you will see this love reflected in you, too. Singles should focus on developing their best qualities, as someone close to you will surely notice them.
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today love, fun, affection, and escapism will feel surprisingly good – and perhaps it will, if you can sit on the sidelines and enjoy a few moments of bliss. Make a conscious and deliberate effort to make time for your partner and just have a good time without thinking about tomorrow.
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, you will find that socially, you are the center of attention due to your charm. You will feel as if all eyes are on you, and you will enjoy this special position! Do not let it dominate your mind, but enjoy it. Your desire to attract attention will bring you happiness, which will make you even more attractive to others. However, make sure that you not only flaunt your looks but also your charming personality.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today lovers will experience a lot of peace and stability with each other and will be satisfied with the current state of their relationship. Enjoy these days of happiness and harmony, as they do not last forever. Go to your favourite restaurant for some sweets and something to eat together.
Quick Answers
For Taurus, October 13, 2026, is described as the perfect time to propose to a partner because you connect completely and haven't been this happy in a long time.

item.title: [Phys.org] Love in the ruins: The paradox of modern romance
item.dc:creator: Martin LaSalle
item.description: Love in the ruins: The paradox of modern romance Ask young adults about love in this day and age, and their diagnosis is bleak: They live in an individualistic society, dating has been reduced to an algorithm, and a generation is afraid to commit. Yet people still fall in love. This paradox was the subject of Jules Pector-Lallemand's doctoral research, supervised by Université de Montréal sociology professor Barbara Thériault. An article based on the Ph.D. dissertation is now published in Sexual
item.content:encoded:
Love in the ruins: The paradox of modern romance
Ask young adults about love in this day and age, and their diagnosis is bleak: They live in an individualistic society, dating has been reduced to an algorithm, and a generation is afraid to commit.
Yet people still fall in love.
This paradox was the subject of Jules Pector-Lallemand's doctoral research, supervised by Université de Montréal sociology professor Barbara Thériault. An article based on the Ph.D. dissertation is now published in Sexuality & Culture.
Pector-Lallemand followed 41 young adults ages 18 to 35 in Montreal, Paris and New York over a four-year period, and 13 of them more intensively for a year and a half. The sample was diverse: heterosexual and LGBTQ+, monogamous and nonmonogamous, couples and singles.
He also took a job as a dishwasher in a Montreal bar to observe the "grammar of gestures"—a hand on the lower back, a head resting on a shoulder—and cross-referenced these with the narratives collected in the interviews.
The age of romantic malady
The first thing that struck Pector-Lallemand in the course of his fieldwork was the pervasive disillusionment with dating apps. He often heard the same refrain, frequently expressed in commercial similes: "Dating apps are like fast food, like a supermarket; I hate them—it's all about appearance. Things used to be different."
Some participants self-diagnosed their neuroses: "I've developed a fear of commitment, rejection phobia, an anxious attachment style."
The prevailing pessimism echoes French–Israeli sociologist Eva Illouz's argument about the decline of romantic love in books such as "Why Love Hurts" (2012) and "The End of Love" (2019).
Pector-Lallemand disagrees. "The statistics show that the proportion of people in relationships in Canada was roughly the same in 2021 as it was in 1921, and divorce rates have been declining steadily since the late 1980s," he observed. "The numbers are often ignored because they don't fit the gloomy narrative about our tawdry age and its unkindness to love."
The unexpected miracle
As he burrowed beneath those generalizations, Pector-Lallemand noticed a paradox. When he asked his pessimistic participants to tell their own stories, the tone changed dramatically and their skepticism gave way to accounts resembling fairy tales, each with a consistent structure.
Pector-Lallemand identified three recurring stages in the love stories he collected: the miracle, heroism and healing.
First came the miracle. Respondents said they weren't looking for love—or were even wary of it—when they met their soul mate. Whether it was via a dating app, through friends or by sheer chance, it happened in spite of themselves.
"No one explicitly said it was fate, a somewhat dated term that may seem ridiculous today, but fate was always there in the subtext," said Pector-Lallemand.
From fear to courage
At the same time, the narratives did not hinge on chance alone. The participants progressed from passivity to become the heroes of their own stories. They related how they had to courageously overcome their fears before they were able to commit.
One confronted their fear of nonmonogamy; another spoke of their insecurity after a sudden, unexplained breakup; yet another broke free from a "toxic" family model.
"A key moment in the love story is precisely when they dare to 'show vulnerability' by revealing their fears, anxieties and past wounds," said Pector-Lallemand. "The path to the first 'I love you' is never described as smooth and free of obstacles."
Thus, in this second part of the narrative, love is no longer something that happened to the participants; they earned it.
Love heals
Finally, in the third phase, participants described their current relationship as healing past wounds, something they had never experienced before. One participant said it had cured his "savior complex"; another found unexpected fulfillment in an open relationship.
Pector-Lallemand argues that this three-step process is perceived as exceptional only because it's framed against the pessimistic premise. "People contrast their 'true love' or 'authentic love' with what they see as a vapid age that embraces a distorted or degraded version of love," he said.
This insight led him to a critical reexamination of Illouz's theories. In his view, her grim analysis springs less from sociological evidence than from romantic discourse itself.
He cites a survey in France in which 80% of respondents said we live in an unromantic age, but 64% reported that they themselves were romantic, a figure that rose to 74% among young respondents.
"In love, the trend is to swim against the trend," Pector-Lallemand concluded.
"Criticizing romantic clichés is just as much a part of the discourse of love as the clichés themselves. It is this paradox that allows everyone to believe their own story is the exception, and to experience their own love as transcendent."
Publication details
Jules Pector-Lallemand, Pessimism and Exceptionality: A Sociological Approach to Romantic Love, Sexuality & Culture (2026). DOI: 10.1007/s12119-026-10617-3

item.content:encoded:
DEAR ABBY: My daughter is getting married soon. I purchased my dress for the wedding and sent a picture of it to the groom’s mother.
This past weekend, she went to get hers, and it’s almost the same as mine, just a different color. She didn’t send a picture of her dress to me; she sent it to my daughter.
I asked her if she had other options and thanked her for considering a different style. Her response was, “Oh, OK. Should I go purchase a different dress? I’m not sure I have enough time, and I really love the dress that I already have.”
What can I do?
— DRESS DRAMA
DEAR DRESS DRAMA: This does not have to be a problem. In fact, the “matching mothers” look is a trend that’s growing in popularity, symbolizing your harmonious dedication in support of your children’s union.
To keep the outfits from looking too similar, choose different jewelry, accessories, hairstyles and maybe even additional layers.
Remember that on her wedding day, the focus is supposed to be on your daughter, not on you or the other mother. Please try not to take this situation as a personal slight. I doubt it was intended that way.
DEAR ABBY: I went out to run errands, and when I returned home, I found a political sign in our front yard. It seems a candidate asked my husband for a pledge of support, and he agreed to place the sign in our front yard without consulting me.
Because of my job, I have always stayed neutral and never publicly endorsed any candidate for political office. When I expressed concern, my husband laughed at me and told our son, “Mom is worried what others will think.”
The issue is that I do not wish to publicly endorse any candidate, and neighbors will assume the person is someone we both endorse (which is not true at all).
Is this a form of passive-aggression on my husband’s part, displaying his lack of respect for my privacy? Am I wrong to believe that he has failed to respect the fact that we are a couple?
Had he discussed his desire to show support, I would have suggested he wear a button or place a bumper sticker on his personal vehicle. Instead, he placed a sign in front of our house!
— FUMING IN PENNSYLVANIA
DEAR FUMING: Your husband’s unilateral decision to allow the candidate to plant his sign on your lawn may have been made on impulse, without thinking it through. However, for him to have laughed and made light of your concern in front of your son was disrespectful.
In the state where I live, several individuals have confided that clients had made them feel — or told them directly — that if they knew they had voted for a different candidate, they would no longer employ them.
Does your husband act unilaterally or belittle you in front of your son when other disagreements arise? If so, you may need to discuss your relationship problem with a licensed marriage and family therapist.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips wrote the column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.content:encoded:
Welsh star makes candid dating app admission after filming new drama 'I've given up'
Welsh actress Elen Rhys has opened up about her love life, admitting she has “given up” on dating apps
Welsh actress Elen Rhys has made a candid admission about her own love life after revealing she has “given up” on dating apps.
The actress, who returns as detective Ffion Lloyd in the second series of hit Welsh crime drama Cleddau, opened up about her experience with online dating while discussing her character's own difficult encounters with the apps.
And while Ffion is still putting herself out there in the hope of finding love, Elen admitted she has decided to step away from dating apps in her personal life.
Asked whether she had ever had a bad experience using them, she said: “Oh, God, haven’t we all? I’m… I’ve given up on dating apps in my personal life.”
The subject takes on particular significance in the new series, with Ffion's attempts to move forward romantically becoming tangled up in one of the cases she is investigating.
In series two, Ffion is trying to rebuild her personal life and has started using a dating app. But when a woman's body is discovered in the River Cleddau, detectives begin to suspect that a killer could be using the same app to target victims.
Suddenly, something Ffion had been using as a way of finding companionship becomes part of a disturbing murder investigation. Elen said it was an interesting aspect of the character to explore because Ffion's dating life runs alongside the central investigation.
She said: “But what was really nice playing was… she is dating online. That runs parallel to this investigation.” The new series promises to take Ffion into much darker territory as her professional investigation begins to collide with her personal life.
Her complicated relationship with Rick, played by Richard Harrington, also remains unresolved. Rick is now separated and single, leaving the door open for the pair's relationship to develop as Ffion attempts to work out what she wants from her own life.
But the new case also forces Ffion to revisit a traumatic period from her past, adding another layer to an already complicated investigation.
As the pressure mounts, Ffion takes a personal risk which could have serious consequences for both the case and her career.
The first series of Cleddau became a major hit for S4C and attracted record numbers of iPlayer sessions for an S4C drama series.
Away from the drama, Elen has largely kept her private life away from the spotlight. She is a mum to her young son and has previously spoken about balancing motherhood with her demanding acting career.
The actress has built an impressive career across television and film, with roles in Keeping Faith, The Mallorca Files, Broadchurch and Silent Witness, as well as appearances on the big screen.
Series two of Cleddau launches on S4C and BBC iPlayer on October 11

item.content:encoded:
Susan, on Wednesday, October 7, delivered a passionate speech on Trump Accounts, where qualifying children born between 2025 and 2028 can receive a $1,000 government sponserded deposit in an investment account.
Since then, a barrage of social media users voiced their reactions to how she looked at the camera between her 61-year-old husband and the US President. That started the conversation about her personal life.
Also Read: Who is Susan Dell? Michael Dell's wife faces online scrutiny after White House appearance with Donald Trump
As per Texas Monthly, Michael and Susan first met on a blind date in Austin, Texas. It was February 1988, shortly after she relocated there to work for real estate developer Trammell Crow. A client of hers insisted that she meet Michael for lunch. A year earlier, he rebranded PC's Limited to Dell Computer Corporation and started to get recognized.
Also Read: ‘Mar-a-Lago face’ is famous again after Susan Dell’s White House remarks; what is it and how does it 'rewrite the rules of aging'
Shortly after returning from the blind date, Susan told her brother Steve that she was impressed.
“Most men I dated talked about themselves a lot and tried to impress me,” Susan recalled the outcome of the date to Texas Monthly in a 2000 interview. “He was the nicest guy I'd ever met... I always knew I would marry the greatest guy in the world.”
Regarding her previous dating, she liked mostly athletes. “Susan always went out with the star athletes - the quarterback, the pitcher for the baseball team,” Steve told the outlet about her days as a cheerleader. “She didn’t get serious with them, but they were serious about her.”
Also Read: Susan Dell’s ‘$50K MAGA makeover’ sparks frenzy: Why is Michael Dell’s wife trending after White House visit?
A year after meeting each other, they got married in 1989.
Michael Dell and Susan Dell on their wedding day in October 1989 in Austin. (Image courtesy: onedell)
The couple then had four children: Alexa, Kira, Juliette, and Zachary. The Dells brought up their family on an expansive Austin estate known as “The Castle,” which has eight bedrooms, 13 bathrooms, multiple swimming pools, and a tennis court.
Michael, currently the fourth richest person on this planet, possesses a net worth of $282.5 billion as per Forbes. In May this year, Dell secured a $9.7 billion contract with the US military to supply software.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Sunday, October 11: Retrograde Venus Squares Mars
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 11, 2026. Retrograde Venus squares Mars on Sunday, revealing the patterns in your romantic life so you can heal from them.
As these powerful planets clash, you're torn between what feels right to you and what looks right from the outside. It’s a battle of heart and the ego that wants to keep up appearances. But keeping up appearances is never the easiest option, no matter how much it might seem so. Notice where you feel stuck today, or what patterns reveal themselves, as this is where you are guided to direct your energy.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Sunday, October 11, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It doesn’t matter how your relationship looks, Aries. You can seem like the perfect couple and still have an unhealthy dynamic. What's really important is how you show up for one another.
A harsh truth may come to light on Sunday regarding the lack of reciprocity in your relationship. This is meant to help you see that how you feel matters and inspire you to start making different decisions.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Stop trying to keep up with others, Taurus. On Sunday, you need to seriously reflect on your own choices, particularly when it comes to your romantic life.
Rather than trying to make everything look beautiful and right, focus on truly following your heart. The right life for you may not look like what others are doing, and that’s OK.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
If you feel the need to sell yourself or your dreams to your partner, that's your sign to pause, Gemini. A relationship shouldn’t make you feel like you need to convince anyone of anything, including what you deserve to receive.
To be freely chosen by another means you have to sit back and let that happen. If it doesn’t, that is not an invitation to try harder. Remember this on Sunday.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You are worthy as you are, Cancer. Sunday's energy reveals a pattern in your romantic life. It seems like the way you treat those you care about is different from how they treat you.
When you love, you love big. You create meaningful moments of quality time, and you give genuine gifts because you’re always thinking of that special person. However, while you’re loving big, you’re often left feeling depleted because you're not getting the same in return. Pay attention to this cycle because it doesn't have to continue.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your partner deserves to take up space too, Leo. You have a grandiose presence. Even if it's not intentional, you naturally take up space with your personality and energy. While this is one of your divine gifts, you have to stop and reflect on how much space your partner is being allowed to take up.
Often without meaning to, your partner becomes a supporting character in your life instead of a main one on their own. Notice what arises on Sunday and try your best to correct it.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Learn to separate your intuition from your fears, Virgo. You have a deep connection with spirit; however, that doesn’t mean all those inner feelings are part of your intuition.
On Sunday, pay attention to how you’re listening to your intuition. It’s not meant to control or force anything in your romantic life. Nor should it be treated as the ultimate truth. Listening to your intuition is a practice of continually returning home to yourself.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You don’t need to pretend you’re fine if you’re not, Libra. You're allowed to take your time in relationships. You can even say no to a big social gathering if you're not feeling up to it.
The energy on Sunday reveals how you often try to suppress your needs in an effort to show up for everyone else around you. This also includes your partner. It’s a pattern you need to be careful of because it likely means you’re not actually having your needs met.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Stop looking for validation, Scorpio. Don't try to live up to a perfect picture of how you thought your life would go. This could have to do with everything from where you live and the work you do to, of course, your relationship.
Too often, you judge yourself against this vision. But this only leads you to feel stuck and be unnecessarily disappointed. On Sunday, focus on what and who you feel connected to rather than trying to be validated for your choices.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
There is no award for how outrageously or abundantly you lived your life, Sagittarius. While you are being blessed by luck and new beginnings right now, be sure you’re only choosing what feels authentic for you.
Don't make decisions for fame or glory. On Sunday, follow your heart and let this chapter of your life teach you what is most important.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Being wealthy doesn’t make you worthy, Capricorn. You deserve to be financially stable; however, that doesn’t determine your worthiness of being loved or supported.
Don't try to build an empire solely to feel like you’re finally good enough to be loved or chosen. This will always inevitably backfire. Build what you feel called to, but know that no matter where you are on your journey, you are already enough.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You never needed to be perfect, Aquarius. You often think that everything will become better if you just focus on how you can improve yourself. But a relationship is two-sided, which means that it’s not all on you to carry.
On Sunday, allow yourself to be human and release any pressure to be or look perfect. Showing up as yourself is the best way to feel genuinely loved.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You're free to live the life that feels right for you, Pisces. Just because others may have an idea of what you should be doing, or even who you should date, doesn’t mean you have to listen.
You are naturally drawn to a quiet life, and you should never feel pressure to do or be more. Honoring the kind of life that feels right for you is how you attract the love that is meant for you. On Sunday, let go of the pressure and expectations.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.content:encoded:
Love Horoscope Today, October 11, 2026
Love horoscope for October 11, 2026, predicts emotional shifts, with signs like Aries and Scorpio navigating anxiety, while Taurus and Aquarius enjoy romance.
Love Horoscope Today, October 11, 2026: Today’s love horoscope predicts emotional changes in love relationships. Aries, Cancer, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Pisces may feel anxiety or distance in their relationships, but are advised to communicate openly and rely on their partner’s support. Taurus, Leo, and Aquarius will experience romance and closeness, as well as happy moments and even marriage proposals.
Gemini, Libra, and Capricorn will find balanced and improving relationships, where open conversations can deepen the relationship. Virgo may face uncertainty, but also an opportunity to strengthen love by expressing true feelings. Overall, clarity, honesty, and emotional connection are important today.
Aries Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that Aries people may have some concerns in terms of love. You may feel that your love has gone away from you or is no longer with you. But you should keep in mind that your love is always with you and you will always get its support. Today, you will get the support of your spouse in every work, and he will always try to keep you happy. You can make your love a part of your life by sharing happiness with him.
Taurus Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today your love life will be good. Whoever you love with all your heart, your closeness with them will increase, and everything in your relationship will be as you want. You will get love in return, and you will spend happy moments with your partner. There may be some problems related to children in married life, so you should pay special attention to the health of your children. There will be an atmosphere of love and understanding in your relationship, and today your love life will be very happy.
Gemini Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s horoscope for Gemini people is better than average in terms of love. There are many possibilities for you regarding love today. Your relationship with your spouse can be better than average today. Your spouse will support you in everything and will try their best to keep you happy. Today, you may get a chance to have dinner with your spouse. This can add depth to your relationship. Today, you may get approval of your love from your family, which is very auspicious for you.
Cancer Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today there will be an atmosphere of anxiety in your love life. You may face uncertainty and instability in your relationship. You need to talk to your partner and understand him. Clarifying your feelings and talking openly about them can strengthen your relationship. Try to take your love out of emotions and move your relationship forward with satisfaction. You should try not to separate your love from your friends and family.
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today your love life will be very wonderful. Today you will get a chance to enjoy your personal life to the fullest. You would like to spend time in your home, which will bring happiness to your home. Today, there is a possibility of some auspicious work happening in your house. Unmarried people can get good marriage proposals today.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today can start with some uncertainty for Virgo people. You may have to prepare to do something new and auspicious in your life. You may also feel uncertain about your love. You should try to understand your feelings with your partner, and this may be the right time to tell them about your love. Today, you can get the right time to take your love relationship to new heights.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today your horoscope will tell you that now is the time to listen to your heart. Today will be a very auspicious day for you. Today, your horoscope will tell you that now is the time to listen to your heart, and you should talk to your partner. Today, your relationship will be strong, and you will find happiness with your partner. Today also you should also talk to your partner thoughtfully. Today, more goodness is coming into your relationship.
Scorpio Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, there may be some worries in your love life. You may feel that your love is going away from you, or there is some uncertainty in your relationship. But you do not need to worry. You should show trust and understanding in your love. You should maintain communication with your partner and try to solve problems with them. The conversation and understanding between you will strengthen your relationship, and you will always get the support of your partner.
Sagittarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today, there may be some more worries in your love life. You may feel that your love has gone away from you or that something has gone wrong. But despite this, you do not need to worry about your love. Those who will try to take your love away from you will go away from your life, and you will be helped to understand the real importance of your love. You should talk to them to make their love an important part of your life.
Capricorn Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today’s love horoscope will prove useful for Capricorn people. Today, your love situation may remain above average. There is a possibility of improvement in your relationships. If there is any dispute going on between you and your partner, then today you can reconcile. Your partner will try his best to convince you, and there can be a new beginning in your relationship.
Aquarius Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today will be a very romantic day for Aquarius people. There are signs of improvement in your relationships. If there was a dispute going on between you and your partner, then today you can reconcile. Today will be a very good day for you, and you can get a chance to make your relationship with your partner permanent. Today you will get time to think about your love, and you will be able to express your feelings better with your partner.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today you may face instability and anxiety in your married life. You may feel that you do not have time for love, and you may feel that your partner is not able to understand you. But you should not be disappointed because this time can be good for you. You should clarify things with your partner and share your concerns with them. This will lead to a better understanding and a relationship between the two of you.
Quick Answers
Taurus, Leo, and Aquarius will experience romance and closeness, alongside happy moments and potential marriage proposals.

item.content:encoded:
St Mary man allegedly used dating apps to lure, rob women
ST MARY, Jamaica — A man accused of using dating applications to lure and rob women has been convicted on ammunition charges in the St Mary Parish Court, while 12 other criminal cases, including rape, robbery and firearm offences, remain pending against him.
Demoy Pennington, a 41-year-old bar operator from Gordon Hall, Epsom, St Mary, was the subject of an islandwide manhunt before his capture on June 24 in St Mary.
Pennington, who has previous convictions, including for grievous sexual assault, is accused of impersonating well-known personalities, including police officers, to deceive women he reportedly met through dating applications.
Investigating officer Dr Jason McKay revealed that Pennington was apprehended by a joint police team after investigators from the St Catherine South Police Division tracked him to St Mary.
“It’s one case down, 12 to go,” McKay said, referring to the outstanding criminal matters.
“He probably thought he was safe in St Mary but St Catherine South has gone as far as St Thomas in the east and Hanover in the west in pursuit of parish-hopping criminals,” he added.
Pennington’s arrest followed investigations into an alleged incident on June 3 involving a woman he reportedly met through a dating application.
According to police reports, Pennington picked up the woman in Kingston, and the two travelled towards Hellshire Beach in Portmore, St Catherine.
While travelling along Port Henderson Road, Pennington allegedly stopped at a business establishment and asked the woman to purchase a bottle of water.
The woman reportedly left her handbag, containing her mobile phone, bank card and other personal belongings, inside the vehicle. However, when she returned, Pennington and the vehicle were gone.
The matter was reported to the police, and subsequent investigations reportedly revealed that $7,000 had been withdrawn from the woman’s bank account using her card.
Pennington was later positively identified during an identification parade and charged with simple larceny and unauthorised access to computer data.
He had previously been charged in connection with at least two other incidents involving the alleged robbery of women he met through dating applications.
Most of the 12 outstanding criminal cases against Pennington reportedly stem from incidents in Portmore, St Catherine.

item.title: [New York Post] Dear Abby: I’ve fallen in love with my first cousin, can I marry her?
item.dc:creator: Dear Abby
item.description: DEAR ABBY: I am a man in his 60s who lost his wife two years ago to a heart attack. I have fallen in love with my cousin, who is also in her 60s, divorced and a lawyer. item.content:encoded:
DEAR ABBY: I am a man in his 60s who lost his wife two years ago to a heart attack. I have fallen in love with my cousin, who is also in her 60s, divorced and a lawyer. Is it reasonable for me to ask her to go with me on dates? Can a man marry his first cousin? — CONFUSED IN NEW JERSEY
DEAR CONFUSED: According to the free legal reference website Justia (law.justia.com), first cousins are not listed among the types of forbidden marriages or civil unions in the state of New Jersey. In other words, yes, it seems to be legal where you live.
Even so, you will want to tread very carefully here. You say you’ve fallen in love with her, but are you sure she has romantic feelings for you? If not, you risk alienating a family member you deeply respect and admire.
DEAR ABBY: I have two brothers, “Derek” and “Paul,” who have not spoken to each other in more than six years. There was no falling-out; they’re simply bad at communicating (even with other siblings). Last year, Derek wanted to get together with all the siblings, but Paul wouldn’t come (no reason given).
I just found out that Derek has terminal cancer. He doesn’t want Paul to know. I assume it has to do with Paul not wanting to get together, which hurt Derek’s feelings. I believe Paul should be told about Derek’s condition. What is the best way to get Derek to reconsider informing Paul of his diagnosis? — IN THE MIDDLE
DEAR IN THE MIDDLE: You and your family have my sympathy for Derek’s condition. It’s not wise to assume anything in a situation like this. If you want to know why Derek is keeping his cancer a secret from Paul, ask him. Tell him you’re there for him and will help him break the news if he would like.
Meanwhile, approach Paul to plan a sibling get-together that would fit his schedule. If he still refuses, it’s likely these two have problems you’re unaware of that go beyond poor communication skills.
DEAR ABBY: I recently took a friend on a day trip. While I was driving, she took out her clippers and trimmed her fingernails in my car. Later, when she changed into her walking shoes, she put the soles of these shoes on the dash of my car to tie them. Thank goodness there wasn’t a pebble stuck in the bottom, or my dashboard would have been scratched in addition to the dirt. I was dumbstruck that someone would do this in someone else’s nice car. What is a good way to ask that these things stop? I was unprepared and without words. — BOTHERED IN THE WEST
DEAR BOTHERED: The most effective way to have delivered the message to your disrespectful friend would have been to say, clearly and firmly, “Excuse me! I don’t want footprints on my dashboard or nail clippings in my car.” Follow it up by asking her to clean up both messes.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at http://www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.content:encoded:
A judge ruled Friday that a model and social media influencer accused of stealing from people she met through dating apps is mentally competent to stand trial.
Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Maria Cavalluzzi announced Friday that psychiatrist Dr. Phani Tumu found Adva Lavie, 29, “presently competent,” according to media reports. The finding clears the way for criminal proceedings to resume after they were suspended in August.
Lavie, also known as Mia Ventura, has pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from allegations that she stole money and valuables from people she met through dating apps, including wealthy older men and younger women.
Prosecutors allege Lavie targeted victims in Westlake Village, West Hollywood, Los Angeles and Beverly Hills between 2023 and 2025, posing as a girlfriend or travel companion to gain access to their homes before stealing cash, jewelry and designer merchandise.
She is charged with two counts each of grand theft and unauthorized use of personal identifying information, along with one count each of first-degree residential burglary and first-degree residential burglary with a person present.
Lavie was ordered to stand trial following a preliminary hearing in March, but criminal proceedings were suspended in August after her attorney raised concerns about her mental competency.
A judge had earlier denied a defense request for a mental health diversion program.
Lavie has remained in custody since July, when she was arrested while free on electronic monitoring. A judge subsequently denied bail.
She is also facing a separate criminal case in Riverside County involving allegations that she stole more than $11,000 worth of luxury items from an Airbnb rental during the 2025 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival.
Lavie had been engaged to billionaire real estate investor and former gubernatorial candidate Stephen Cloobeck, who was arrested in May and charged with attempting to dissuade witnesses from testifying in the criminal case against her.
Cloobeck pleaded not guilty Aug. 7 to three felony counts involving alleged witness intimidation and a misdemeanor count of making annoying telephone calls.
The alleged victims named in the criminal complaint against Cloobeck are also alleged victims in Lavie’s case.
Lavie faces up to 11 years and eight months in state prison if convicted as charged in the Los Angeles County case, according to prosecutors.

item.title: [OSV News] Bishops discuss cohabitation of young couples at Vatican meeting on marriage and family
item.dc:creator: Courtney Mares
item.description: VATICAN CITY (OSV News) — On the third day of a weeklong Vatican meeting on marriage and family Oct. 9, Catholic bishops grappled with a trend that worries many Church leaders: young couples choosing to live together rather than wed. “We cannot ignore the fact that the number of marriages is currently declining throughout the world, both civil marriages and marriages celebrated in the Church,” Cardinal Kevin Farrell, prefect of the Dicastery for Laity, Family, and Life said as he opened the day’
item.content:encoded:
VATICAN CITY (OSV News) — On the third day of a weeklong Vatican meeting on marriage and family Oct. 9, Catholic bishops grappled with a trend that worries many Church leaders: young couples choosing to live together rather than wed.
“We cannot ignore the fact that the number of marriages is currently declining throughout the world, both civil marriages and marriages celebrated in the Church,” Cardinal Kevin Farrell, prefect of the Dicastery for Laity, Family, and Life said as he opened the day’s discussion.
The cardinal noted the concern of many Christian parents today “whose children suffer from loneliness, remain hesitant to make a lasting commitment, or categorically reject the path that their parents themselves had embraced with joy.”
The third day of the Oct. 7-14 gathering of the world’s bishops’ conference presidents and the heads of Eastern Catholic churches marking the 10th anniversary of “Amoris Laetitia” was devoted entirely to “young people and the discovery of the vocation to marriage.”
Auxiliary Bishop Stephen Eustace Victor Fernandes of Bombay, one of 26 experts invited to contribute to the discussions, was one of two featured speakers at the morning plenary session Oct. 9.
How Church can accompany couples living together outside marriage
Bishop Fernandes addressed how the Church can accompany couples who live together outside marriage. He urged bishops to avoid both indifference and condemnation, emphasizing the importance of listening to young people to understand their experiences and concerns.
Listening, he said, “enables us to distinguish between a rejection of marriage and a fear that lifelong committed love may no longer be possible.”
That distinction is particularly important for young people who have experienced family breakdown, separation, violence, abandonment or failed relationships, he said. Their reluctance to marry may reflect both emotional wounds and genuine questions about commitment.
“The first task is to know their story: Why have they chosen to live together? What do they hope for? What fears or obstacles stand before them? What is already good in their relationship?” Bishop Fernandes said.
“But accompaniment must also involve genuine discernment. The question is not simply: How can we move this couple towards a wedding? It is also: Are these two people truly called to marriage, and are they ready to enter into a lifelong marital covenant? Some cohabiting relationships may contain authentic love and important elements of commitment, while still lacking the conditions necessary for a mature marital covenant,” he added.
Stressing importance of forming young people in virtues
Bishop Fernandes also stressed the importance of forming young people in the virtues that sustain marriage, including fidelity, responsibility, chastity, forgiveness, perseverance, generosity and openness to life.
That formation involves teaching young people to communicate, resolve conflict, apologize and forgive, he said, while helping them understand that love depends not only on emotion but also on repeated decisions to seek the good of another person.
“Rather than presenting Christian morality primarily in terms of prohibitions and obligations, we need to speak of love as gift, freedom as self-giving, sexuality as the person’s capacity to love and give oneself, fidelity as the foundation of trust and stability, and marriage as a covenant capable of giving meaning to life,” he said.
Archbishop Timothy Costelloe of Perth, Australia, also addressed the issue of cohabitation, saying many young people no longer understand or accept the traditional Christian connection between sexuality, marriage and procreation.
He pointed to the influence of social media, entertainment and online culture, which often emphasize personal fulfillment and autonomy over permanence and sacrifice.
“We are competing with many other approaches to the meaning of marriage,” he said.
Meeting cohabiting couples where they are
“Although young couples who live together before marrying are falling short of the ideal of Christian marriage, this does not mean that there is nothing good in their relationships: we met them where they are and accompany them as they move forward to a fuller expression of the Christian ideal,” Archbishop Costelloe added.
Speaking with OSV News after the morning session, Archbishop Costelloe said Australia’s highly secular culture continues to make it difficult for the Church to engage deeply in people’s lives.
He recommended that if local parish communities can discover ways in which the witness of married couples and families can be both visible and celebrated, the fear of commitment and doubts about permanence which trouble many young people might be mitigated to some extent.
“As one married couple explained to me, The most persuasive argument for Christian marriage is often a married couple living it well,” he said.
Among the 11 married couples from around the world invited to share their testimonies with the bishops are Charmaine Bernadette Villegas and Eren Lyle Villegas from the Philippines who are serving as missionaries in Rome with the Couples for Christ apostolate.
Offering example of Christian marriage rather than impose beliefs
In their work with couples who live together, the Villegases said they seek to offer an example of Christian marriage rather than impose their beliefs.
“We don’t want to force who we are as a married couple, but just simply living out as a witness of what we believe marriage is, and in the hope that they too will see it the way we see it,” Eren Lyle Villegas told OSV News.
Charmaine Bernadette Villegas said many young people in the Philippines are postponing marriage rather than rejecting it outright. Some want to establish their careers first, while others face economic pressures and believe they need financial stability before marrying.
The couple, who have been married for 16 years and do not have children, said they continue to pray for a family while embracing what they describe as a call to serve as spiritual parents to young people in their parish and community.
“We’ve been praying since day one, but we have always believed that the Lord is faithful. And in his perfect timing will answer that prayer,” Eren said.
Gathering’s format outlined during a briefing
Father Giacomo Costa, a consultant to the General Secretariat of the Synod who oversees the meeting’s methodology, outlined the gathering’s format during an Oct. 9 briefing at the Holy See Press Office.
Participants are divided into 16 small groups seated at round tables in the Paul VI Hall, using the “conversation in the spirit” method employed during the Synod on Synodality, he said.
The groups reflect the global reach of the Church, Father Costa said. Italian-speaking groups, for example, include participants from China, Poland, Mexico, Central Asia, Greece, Bulgaria, Slovenia, Germany and Croatia.
Each of the 16 groups approved a report and presented it to the wider assembly during the afternoon plenary session, he said.
Discussions during the meeting’s first days also addressed the formation of seminarians who grew up in a digital culture and, in some cases, in blended families. Participants considered how those experiences shape seminarians’ understanding of relationships and how formation programs can help them understand their own histories and learn to accompany others, Father Costa said.
Another focus was the meaning of accompaniment and the practical steps needed to make it effective.
“We asked ourselves how we can bridge the gap between the desire to be close and to accompany and the actual capacity to do so?” Father Costa said.
Church must consider who is equipped to accompany people
Accompaniment risks becoming a concept that participants endorse in principle without a clear understanding of how to put it into practice, he said. The Church must consider who is equipped to accompany people, what preparation is needed and how to respond to different situations.
The Vatican also announced the members of the commission responsible for preparing the meeting’s summary report, which is expected to be published Oct. 14, the final day of the gathering.
The commission includes Cardinal Pablo Virgilio Siongco David of the Philippines; Cardinal Mario Grech; Cardinal Matteo Zuppi; Archbishop José Manuel Imbamba of Angola; Philippe Bordeyne, president of the Pontifical John Paul II Theological Institute for Marriage and Family Sciences; and Orietta Rachele Grazioli, a professor at the institute.
The bishops are scheduled to turn their attention to the first years of marriage during the weekend discussions. Spanish Cardinal José Cobo Cano and Argentine theologian María Marcela Mazzini are scheduled to address the gathering on Oct. 10 before the bishops take Sunday off as a day of rest.
Courtney Mares is Vatican editor for OSV News. Follow her on X @catholicourtney.

item.dc:creator: The Argus Staff
item.description: A new wedding trends survey reveals that almost two thirds (62 per cent) of people in Brighton would opt for a ‘phone-free’ wedding, suggesting uninterrupted and meaningful ceremonies are on the rise. The research, conducted by the engagement ring experts at Austen & Blake comes from a survey they ran of 1000 respondents in the UK to reveal the wedding traditions of 2026. As wedding planning continues to evolve, the findings provide insight into the priorities, values, and emerging trends reshap
item.content:encoded:
A new wedding trends survey reveals that almost two thirds (62 per cent) of people in Brighton would opt for a ‘phone-free’ wedding, suggesting uninterrupted and meaningful ceremonies are on the rise.
The research, conducted by the engagement ring experts at Austen & Blake comes from a survey they ran of 1000 respondents in the UK to reveal the wedding traditions of 2026.
As wedding planning continues to evolve, the findings provide insight into the priorities, values, and emerging trends reshaping modern celebrations.
The outdated wedding and proposal traditions
According to the survey, over a third of people in Brighton (35 per cent) think that the three month spending rule on engagement rings is outdated and asking parental permission before proposing should be a thing of the past (22 per cent).
The wedding traditions Brighton would most likely get rid of:
When it comes to the wedding day, the people of Brighton think parents paying for the wedding is the tradition they would most likely get rid of (30 per cent), followed by the first dance (19 per cent).
The wedding tradition that’s here to stay in Brighton!
The research shows that the wedding tradition that is here to stay in Brighton is having bridesmaids and groomsmen. A huge 90 per cent of Brighton think this is the most important tradition and the least likely to be replaced any time soon.
AI takes a front seat
Although the new trend of ‘phone free’ weddings has emerged from the research, the use of technology when it comes to preparing for proposals and weddings is still a top priority for Brits.
According to the research, 19 per cent of people in Brighton would use AI to organise the perfect proposal, and 16 per cent would use AI to write their wedding vows.
AI is also taking a front seat when it comes to wedding planning, with digital wedding planning including the use of apps and AI (32 per cent) taking over traditional forms of planning such as wedding journals (18 per cent) and wedding planners (18 per cent).
Wedding guest etiquette
The survey also reveals what UK respondents feel is the worst wedding etiquette, proving that there are traditions and ‘unspoken’ rules when it comes to the big day. Drinking too much is considered to be the worst wedding etiquette in Brighton.
- Drinking too much — 19 per cent
- Bringing an uninvited plus one — 19 per cent
- Posting on social media without permission — 16 per cent
- Joining in on the first dance — 16 per cent
- Wearing white as a guest — 11 per cent
How does Brighton feel about destination weddings abroad in 2026?
With more travel-led weddings happening than ever before, the jewellery specialists asked Brighton how they feel about attending weddings abroad.
When asked which statement best describes their view on destination weddings, over a third (38 per cent) said they are stressful and expensive for guests, while 24 per cent cited them as a fun excuse for a holiday, and 16 per cent would describe them as fun and romantic.

item.title: [RADII] Can AI Tell Your Fortune? How Chinese Divination Is Going Digital - RADII
item.dc:creator: John Lim
item.description: Ask an AI chatbot about your career, relationship, or future, and it will probably give you an answer. item.content:encoded:
Ask an AI chatbot about your career, relationship, or future, and it will probably give you an answer. Ask it to read your ba zi, however, and you enter a very different kind of conversation.
Across Chinese social media, users have been feeding detailed birth information into AI models such as DeepSeek and asking them to interpret their ba zi, or Four Pillars of Destiny. On Xiaohongshu, the practice became a viral trend, with users sharing prompts for everything from relationship compatibility to career and fortune readings. Some users ask whether they should change jobs; others ask about romantic compatibility or when a particular period of good fortune might arrive. In 2025, the trend became prominent enough in China that the hashtag #DeepSeekFortune racked up tens of millions of views on Xiaohongshu.
The appeal is obvious. A traditional fortune-teller might require an appointment, a fee, and some idea of what you want to ask. There’s also the potential awkwardness of telling someone your deepest thoughts, most worrying concerns, and other forms of deep desires. An AI oracle is available whenever you are, whether that means after a bad day at work or while wondering if you should text an ex at 1 AM. It can also happily explain the same chart over and over again, without charging by the hour. And, of course, no awkward silence to weather through.
And increasingly, you don’t even need to know what you’re doing. A growing crop of apps now combine AI with ba zi, feng shui, I Ching, Zi Wei Dou Shu and other forms of Chinese metaphysics, turning practices that can take years to learn into something resembling a chatbot conversation.
From Reading the Stars to Reading a Chatbot
Chinese divination encompasses a sprawling collection of traditions rather than one single system. Ba zi, or the Four Pillars of Destiny, uses a person’s year, month, day, and hour of birth to construct a chart based around the traditional Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches. Other systems, such as I Ching divination and Zi Wei Dou Shu, use different methods to interpret a person’s circumstances and possible future.
For generations, accessing these systems often meant finding someone who had spent years learning how to interpret them. That expertise was not simply a matter of plugging information into a formula. A practitioner would interpret a chart, ask questions about a client’s circumstances, and use their experience to decide which details mattered.
AI changes that relationship by putting the interpretation layer into the interface.
A user can generate a ba zi chart through an app, paste it into ChatGPT, Claude, or DeepSeek, and ask the model to explain it. Some dedicated services now go much further. Cantian AI, for instance, offers ba zi, Liu Yao divination, feng shui and I Ching readings alongside an AI interpretation layer, while YiMatrix combines ba zi with Zi Wei Dou Shu, multiple forms of divination and an AI chat assistant that can explain a user’s chart.
Other apps are making the process even more familiar. FengShui AI offers personalized daily readings, compatibility analysis, I Ching readings, and even the ability to upload photographs of a space for an AI feng shui assessment. Another app, 8Luck.AI, combines ba zi with AI face and palm analysis.
Your Digital Fortune Teller Is Always On
That accessibility may be the most significant change.
A 2025 South China Morning Post report spoke to young Chinese users who were combining traditional astrology apps with generative AI. One 21-year-old user described generating her ba zi chart and then feeding it into ChatGPT to assess her compatibility with her boyfriend.
The questions being asked are remarkably ordinary: Will my career improve? Is this relationship right for me? Should I make this decision? When will things get better?
That may help explain why AI fortune-telling has found an audience among young people who might not necessarily describe themselves as deeply religious or superstitious. A 2026 study of young Chinese users found that people engaged with AI fortune-telling in several ways, including playfully, emotionally, and through combinations of digital tools and existing spiritual practices. Another study of more than 1,000 social-media posts and user interviews found that people often treated LLM fortune-telling less as a precise predictive system and more as a source of emotional support.
In other words, you don’t necessarily have to believe that the chatbot can see your future to find the exercise useful. It can just be curiosity, interest, or even mere amusement.
There is something oddly familiar about this, too. People have long turned to fortune-telling during uncertain periods, whether because they genuinely believe in it or simply want another perspective on a difficult decision, or to find some levity. AI removes much of the friction involved. You don’t have to explain why you’re asking, worry about being judged, or wait for an appointment. You can simply ask again, and again.
What Happens When You Can Ask Fate Until You Like the Answer?
Unlike a human fortune-teller, an AI can produce another reading almost instantly. If the answer doesn’t sound right, you can change the wording of the prompt, provide more information, or ask the question from another angle (for better or worse).
Research into Chinese users of generative-AI fortune-telling has found this behavior precisely. In one 2026 study involving interviews with 22 regular users and an analysis of 1,842 online community posts, researchers found that some users repeated queries until they received interpretations that aligned more closely with what they expected. Users appreciated AI’s convenience and efficiency, but also felt that it lacked some of the spiritual mystique associated with human divination.
That creates an interesting paradox.
Traditional divination is often presented as a way of confronting uncertainty: you ask a question, receive an interpretation, and decide what to do with it. AI can instead turn divination into an iterative conversation. The “oracle” doesn’t necessarily deliver one answer. It gives you an answer, waits for your response, and then gives you another.
The distinction matters because today’s AI fortune tellers aren’t supernatural machines. Large language models generate responses from patterns in their training data, and specialized applications combine those models with systems for calculating and interpreting traditional charts. Their predictions are not scientifically validated, and even the apps themselves generally frame their readings as guidance, entertainment, or reference rather than certainty.
The New Fortune Teller Doesn’t Need a Crystal Ball
For thousands of years, divination has adapted to whatever tools people had available: calendars, almanacs, coins, charts, stars, and specialized texts. The smartphone may simply be its latest interface.
But as with everything else AI-related, the use cases here are accessibility and immediacy. Someone’s desire to know the future is not dependent on an appointment anymore; they can simply do so through a screen.
Plus, a person who knows nothing about the Four Pillars can now generate a chart in seconds. Someone curious about feng shui can photograph a room and ask for suggestions. Someone worried about a relationship can ask an AI to compare two birth charts. And someone who has never sat across from a fortune-teller can have an extended conversation with one without ever leaving the sofa.
That doesn’t mean the human fortune-teller is about to disappear. Far from it. Traditional practitioners still argue that genuine interpretation requires experience, intuition, and an understanding of the person sitting in front of them. There’s no replacing that.
Instead, divination is becoming less of a specialized service and more of a digital habit. Like trying to figure out how to interview for a job without needing to ask a career coach, or understanding stock exchanges without having to consult a stockbroker.
Cover image via RADII/Nano Banana Pro.

item.dc:creator: Kate Rose

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Wednesday, October 7: Put Yourself First Today
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for October 7, 2026. The Virgo Moon squares retrograde Uranus in Gemini, encouraging you to focus on yourself.
A relationship should make you feel safe, but it shouldn’t be your only source of stability. It’s important to recognize that you can make yourself feel safe regardless of your relationship status. Try to lean into this on Wednesday. The Virgo Moon wants to keep you safe, but retrograde Uranus is tempting you with all that’s possible. Slow down and make the choices that feel right for you.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Wednesday, October 7, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You must be open to change, Aries. Wednesday's energy is all about taking risks and getting out of your comfort zone. Rather than trying to find guarantees in your relationship or life path, you must find them within yourself.
Don't stay somewhere just because you've gotten comfortable. Let yourself evolve, even if that means facing challenges. That's how you will find the love that’s meant for you.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be honest with yourself, dearest Taurus. You don’t have to know everything at this moment. But you do need to be sure you’re taking time to figure out what you actually want.
You recently began an intense period of transformation that is guiding you to rethink your priorities. While this will impact your love life, it’s moreso about you figuring out what your most authentic life looks like.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You deserve the best of both worlds, Gemini. On Wednesday, you may feel torn between the comforts of home and following your wildest dreams.
You're having a hard time deciding, but the reality is you don't actually have to choose. Instead, figure out how you can have both. You can evolve into the person you’re meant to be, and still have what and who represent the home you hold so dear.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be willing to keep growing, Cancer. October 7 brings a shift in what you thought you wanted. This may have to do with a particular relationship or your love life as a whole.
You're having some mixed feelings on Wednesday, as you realize some deep truths about how you’ve approached relationships. Know that you are allowed to speak up and change your mind. Set boundaries and don't give your energy to those who don’t truly appreciate it.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be careful of your commitments on Wednesday, Leo. You want to help someone in your life, perhaps a friend or romantic interest. While this is a worthwhile endeavor, make sure it's not going to hurt your own sense of security, especially if money is what they need.
Of course, if you can help them and you feel this is a reciprocal relationship, then feel free to. But if this comes with strings or threatens your own standing, be wary of what you commit to.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be flexible, dearest Virgo. As an earth sign, stability is one of your greatest strengths. However, you often feel secure because of the plans you make and what you feel you can control.
October 7 is challenging all of that, but in the best way possible. Rather than balk at what arrives, see what is happening on Wednesday as the best thing for you. Flowing with the universe will bring you where you’re meant to be.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t be so rigid, Libra. You are meant to take a chance and embrace an era of new beginnings and romance. But you may be having a hard time seeing the difference between your intuition and your wounds.
There is a relationship in your life you intuitively thought was meant to be. However, you’re finally seeing that it may have been your inner wounds talking. On Wednesday, try to accept this shift in perspective and remain open to what arises, even if it’s not what you expected.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You’re not meant to remain the same forever, Scorpio. Be careful of people who seem threatened by you growing and changing. Those who truly love you will support you in whatever you do, even if that means you’re embracing your own path for a while.
The same is true for you. Change often brings you on a wild adventure, but you should never be afraid of losing people you care about. Just keep growing and trust that any changes are meant to help you.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You don’t need to carry it all, Sagittarius. You have a strict idea of what you need to have built for you to be ready for a great love. While this stems from your desire to show up with greater maturity, you must realize love doesn’t wait for you to be ready.
Be open on Wednesday, especially toward a person who feels like everything you ever wanted. You don’t have to be perfect to give this connection a chance.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Embrace change, Capricorn. You can say yes to life and love, but you can’t necessarily determine how it will play out.
On Wednesday, you are encouraged to shift the foundations of your life. This can include changes to your routine and even career. Yet, with the energy of Virgo, you may feel like it’s happening differently than you planned. Try to breathe through any fears and trust that it’s safe to let go and give it all a chance.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You are your own safe space, Aquarius. Your romantic relationship never has to look a particular way to be real. Yet this is something you must learn for yourself. Before you can do that, though, you need to realize the safety you’re looking for can only be found within.
October 7 is a day to invest in yourself. Practice affirmations and reflect on what you’ve built. This will allow you to have the confidence to truly choose the love that’s authentic for you.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t shut out love, dearest Pisces. You've been working hard to invest in your home and create a true sanctuary. Yet, you may inadvertently be shutting down possibilities for romance. You can have both.
On Wednesday, make sure you’re creating space for the love you say you want. This doesn’t mean you need to go all in immediately or throw caution to the wind, but make sure you’re not shutting out new possibilities for romance.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.
